column1: AI Incorrectly Selects Effective Date Due to Multiple Mention
column31:
*Summary* 

The AI encounters confusion when determining the correct *Effective Date*, as the term appears multiple times within the contract. In certain cases, it selects *the date marked with brackets* or the *Commence Date*, instead of the correct *(Effective Date)* notation. This inconsistency leads to incorrect data extraction and validation errors.

*Steps To Replicate*

# Upload a contract document containing multiple mentions of the term *Effective Date*.[^The-Dylan-Dial-A-Bug-Exterminator-contract-1.1.2025-12.31.2025-Oriana.pdf] 
# Complete the process
# Verify the selected *Effective Date* in the Existing Contracts.
# Observe whether the AI correctly picks the date explicitly mentioned as *(Effective Date)* or mistakenly selects another variant.

*Expected Result:* 

The AI should *always* select the date that is explicitly marked as *(Effective Date)* in the contract.

*Actual Result*

The AI sometimes picks:

* The date enclosed in brackets *(e.g., [Effective Date])*
* The *Commence Date* instead of the correct *(Effective Date)*

*Suggestions to Fix:*

* Implement a *keyword validation system* to ensure the AI prioritizes dates explicitly marked as *(Effective Date)* over other similarly named terms.
* Enhance *context-based parsing* to differentiate between *Commence Date* and *Effective Date* when multiple instances exist.
* Train the AI model to reference *preceding clauses and contract structures* for improved accuracy.

*Troubleshooting:*

* Check if the document formatting causes misinterpretation (e.g., brackets vs parentheses).
* Test different contract samples to evaluate whether variations in notation impact AI selection.
* Review AI extraction logs to identify the rule triggering incorrect selections.

*Severity:* *Major*

column1: AI Leaves Renewal Term Blank Instead of Defaulting to "N/A"
column31:
*Summary* 

When contracts are uploaded *without a specified Renewal Term*, the AI should automatically *set the field to "N/A"* by default. However, in some cases, the AI *incorrectly leaves the field blank* in both the *application UI* and the *network response*, storing it as an empty string ({{""}}). This inconsistency affects data accuracy and contract clarity.

*Steps To Replicate*

# Navigate to the *Contract Management* page in the application.
# Upload a contract that *does not contain a Renewal Term* in its details.
# Allow the AI to process and extract contract data.
# Check the displayed *Renewal Term* field in the Existing Contracts UI.
# Inspect the *network response* and verify the stored Renewal Term value.
# Observe whether the AI correctly assigns *"N/A"* or leaves the field blank ({{""}}).

*Expected Result:*

The AI should *always* set the *Renewal Term* field to {{"N/A"}} if no renewal terms are provided in the contract.

*Actual Result:*

* The AI *sometimes leaves the field blank (*{{""}}*)* in both the application UI and network response.
* The contract details show a missing value instead of {{"N/A"}}, leading to potential misinterpretation.

*Suggestions to Fix:*

* Implement a *fallback logic* to automatically assign {{"N/A"}} when the contract lacks renewal terms.
* Ensure that the database and network response *store* {{"N/A"}} instead of a blank field.
* Introduce a *validation check* to prevent blank Renewal Term values before finalizing contract data.

*Troubleshooting:*

* Verify if this issue occurs *only for specific contract types* or across all uploads.
* Check whether the AI extraction logic *misinterprets missing fields* instead of applying defaults.
* Test different contract formats to confirm consistency in handling missing renewal terms.

*Severity:* *Major* – Affects contract integrity and data accuracy.

column31:
*Acceptance criteria*

* user should able to upload the client  scope of work and should display in client scope  library tab
* The modal should open when the user clicks *Create > client Scope Library* from the dropdown.
* The modal should be *centered* on the screen with a blurred background.
* Users should be able to *close the modal* using:
** The *"X" button* on the top right.
** The *Cancel button* at the bottom.

h4. *2. Modal Structure & Fields*

* The modal title should be *"Upload client Scope Library"*.
* It should contain the following *form fields*:
*# *Scope Of Work Name (Text Input)*
*#* Placeholder text: *"Enter Scope Of Work name"*.
*#* Input should be *mandatory* before uploading.
*#* This field will  be a unique field
*# *Client Name (Dropdown)*
Placeholder text: *"Select Client name"*.
Input should be *mandatory* before uploading.
It should be a single select
*# *Service (Dropdown)*
*#* Placeholder text: *"Select services"*.
*#* Users should be able to choose from a predefined list of services.
*#* This should include both services and subservices 
*#* this field should be a single select
*# *Upload Scope Of Work (File Upload)*
*#* Users can either *click to upload* or *drag and drop* files.
*#* Allowed file formats: *PDF (need to be confrimed by basim)*
*#* An error message should be displayed if an unsupported format or an oversized file is uploaded.

h4. *3. Action Buttons*

* *Cancel Button*
** Clicking *Cancel* should close the modal without saving changes.
* *Upload Button*
** The *Upload button* should remain *disabled* until all mandatory fields are filled.
** Once clicked, the file should be validated and uploaded to the system.
** Upon successful upload, the modal should *close automatically* and display a loading message modal
** Modal should show the message : *Extracting Base Scope of Work...* sub text as : *Please wait while we extract the Base Scope of Work. This may take a few moments..*
** In case of an error, an appropriate *error message* should be shown (e.g., "File upload failed. Please try again.").
** Once the system extracts the file it should open the extracted scope of work in view form. 
** user should able to close the file by clicking on close button 
** User should able to edit the file by clicking on edit icon in the view page and it will open in edit format. 
** User should able to modify any points 
** Once the user clicks on update button, it should update the content of data and update the last updated by value 
* *SOW Edit Mode*
** user should able to click on edit from the list page 
** User should able to reupload the file in the same sow. 
** once the user clicks on edit button, it should open the create modal in Edit mode and should able to reupload the file after deleting the current file 
** TItle should be “Edit client scope Library“
** client should be disabled,Service and Scope of work name should be enabled and user should able to change the name and service from the dialog box . 
** User should able to remove the current file and reupload the file from the system 
** user shuold able to cancel the reupload and it should not update the file.
* 
* *Deactivate* 
** User should able to deactivate the scope of work from the list page. 
** deactivate confirmation message should be displayed when user clicks on deactivate option 
** once the user clicks on deactivate it should change the color to red and should able to activate again once the user clicks on active button again 
* *_When Client user logs in_*
** client should able to navigate to client scope library and should able to view list of scope of work created under client. 
** User should able to create the client scope of work  based on the permission added. If the user doesnot have required permission then user shouldnot able to create or edit the client of scope library,they will have only view permission..

*Acceptance Criteria*

# The *Client Scope of Work Creation Page* should open when the user clicks the *"Create >Create client scope of Work"* button from the list page.

h3. *Form Fields*

# The following fields should be available and marked as *mandatory (*{{*}}*)* where applicable:
#* *Client Name**: A dropdown list of available clients.
#* *Service Category**: A dropdown list to select the relevant service category.
#* *Service**: A dependent dropdown list populated based on the selected service category.this include both Servces/Subservices. This will be a single select.
#* *Scope of Work Name**: A text input field where the user enters the name of the SOW. This will be a predefined value in the format : <Service name>-
#* *Property Selection**: A dropdown list to select the associated property/properties.this field will be a multi select

h3. *Scope of Work Selection Options*

# Users should have *three options* to choose or generate a Scope of Work:
#* *Choose Scope of Work*:
#** Dropdown with options to select an SOW from:
#*** *Base Scope Library*
#*** *Client Scope Library*
#** If user selects base scope library, then base scope library dialog box will open to select the base scope of work. 
#*** Scope of work name field will be enabled and it will be a dropdown. this will list all the base scope of work. this field will be a single select
#*** Service field will be disabled and populated with the selected service from the client scope of work create form

*Extracting Document using AI*

>*Extracting Base Scope of Work...Please wait while we extract the Base Scope of Work. This may take a few moments. -*For base scope of work

Processing Status Fails to Change to "Rejected" When Uploading Invalid Document/PDF
column31:
*Summary* 

When an incorrect document/PDF is uploaded to the *Base Scope Library*, the *Processing* status does not change to *Rejected* as expected. Instead, the system keeps the status as *Processing*, leading to confusion regarding the validation outcome. This issue impacts workflow accuracy and prevents users from recognizing incorrect uploads in a timely manner.



*Steps To Replicate*

# Navigate to the *Base Scope Library* in the application.
# Attempt to upload an invalid or incorrect document/PDF.
# Observe the status update under the *Base Scope Of Work listing* section.
# Notice that the status remains *Processing*, instead of updating to *Rejected* when the document fails validation.



*Expected Result:* 

* If the uploaded document is invalid, the status should automatically change to *Rejected* to indicate an unsuccessful upload.

*Actual Result*

* The status remains *Processing*, even when an invalid document is uploaded, leading to uncertainty about the upload status.
* The application does not correctly reject invalid files, preventing users from identifying failed uploads.

*Suggestions to Fix:*

* Implement *document validation checks* that trigger an automatic status change to *Rejected* when an upload fails.
* Ensure *error handling mechanisms* are correctly updating the status field upon invalid uploads.
* Introduce a *clear rejection notification* to inform users when their document has been deemed invalid.

*Troubleshooting:*

* Verify if the issue occurs across all invalid document types or only specific formats.
* Check whether system logs record the validation failure but fail to update the UI accordingly.
* Test different rejection scenarios to confirm proper error handling in failed uploads.

*Priority:* *High* – Affects workflow efficiency and user understanding of validation processes.

*Severity:* *Major* – Prevents users from quickly identifying invalid uploads.

column1: Contract Upload AI UI
column31:
*Acceptance Criteria*

As a Connexus user or client, i should able to upload Existing contracts under the client detail > Existing contracts section

# *Upload Interface*
#* Users can see an "Upload your existing contracts here" message with a clear upload button.
#* Upon clicking on file upload it should able to open the file selection dialogbox and user should able to upload the file 
#* The upload button should display an icon and initiate the file upload process upon selection.
# *Supported File Types and Size*
#* Only pdf file should able to upload 
#* it should throw error if other files are uplaoded 
#* File size should be restricted to a specified limit with an error message displayed for files exceeding this limit.
# *Progress Indication*
#* After selecting a file, the upload process should show a "Processing..." indicator with a loading icon to inform users that the file is being uploaded.
#* Once the upload completes, the processing status should update to either success or error.
#* Processing screen should have back button to move to the file upload tab
# *AI Processing and Validation*
#* The system should use AI to analyze the uploaded contract and extract relevant information (if applicable, depending on the functionality).
#* System should throw errors when the upladed file has properties which are not created in application. 
#* Prerequirsite for uploading the file upload : Client and All properties should be created under the connexus application.
# *File Upload tab*
#* When user clicks on back button, user will navigate to file upload tab where it list all the files uploaded under the client tab. 
#* Table will have file name, Uploaded by,Uploaded Date,Status 
#* user should able to view the status of the file uplod : Pending,Pending for Approval,completed,Error.
#* User should able to click on each record and system should take the user to the processing screen
#* The uploaded file should be displayed in the "Existing Contracts" section with an option to view, download, or delete the document.
# *Pending for Approval Status:* 
#* Pending for Approval status will be displayed for 2 cases : Vendor creation confirmation and preview of processed data
#* If the vendor added in the pdf is not an existing vendor then system should create internally but in a draft state. 
#* If the vendor added in the file has a matching name then user should able to view the matching vendor list in a screen and also user should able to have a provision to  create as new vendor. 
#* if the vendor name already existed in the system it will not ask for the screen and skip the creation part.
#* Once the vendor is created then it will show the preview screen with all the processed data from the file
#* User should able to modify the data using inline eidt functionality 
#* user should able to confirm the screen by clicking on confirm button.
#* once the user confirm,it will move to existing contracts tab. 
# *Existing Contract Tab*
#* All successful file upload and confirmed by client files will be visible under existing contract tab as a table of records with the below column header : 
#* Property Name ,Legal Entity Service,Types,Contract Execution,City.State,Annual Contract Value,Cost per unit/year, Vendor Name,Contract start date,Contract ENd date,Renewal date ,total Term,End term type.
# *Data Validation* 
#*  Property Name : Property Name mentioned in the file should be added. If the uplaoded file has multiple properties, then it will be consider as multiple records. Each record in the table will be based on signle property. 
#* Legal ENtity: this field should be obtained frm legal entity of property.
#* Service : this field should be added based on the service mentioned in the ocntract or proposal. iff there are multiple services under the same contract,all the services should be mentioned in the table for each property
#* Contract Start Date : It should display the contract start date if the file uploaded is a contract. else it should show NA 
#* Contract End date: It should display the contract End date if the file uploaded is a contract. else it should show NA 
#* Total term of contact: it should display the total term of contract. if its not a contract then it should display NA 
#* Vendor name: this value will be populated based on the input we recieved while processing. if its non connexus vendor client system will create a new vendor or match with the existing vendor based on the client innput 
#* Cost per unit : this column header will change based on the client type added and property added by the client. This field will be a calculated field  : Annual contract value/No.of units if the client type is HOA else for other client type according to the metrics added in property value will be changed 
#* End Terms: Two fields will be addded. Early termination & Regular Termination 
#* Early termination should have two values : Termination Fee and Early Termination Requirements. 
#* Regular Termination Will have : Notice requirements and Renewal terms. 
#* All the end term value will be processed from contract after analyzing the data. 
# *Existing Contract Table.* 
#* All list should be sorted based on the contract expiration date and all the expired contract data should be listed at the top and about to expire should be the next. all the normal contracts will be displayed at the bottom. 
#* Expiration date will be color coded. for all expired contracts data will be in red color, about to exire contracts will have orange color and all normal contracts will have in black color 
# *New Requirement for Renewal terms*

** User should able to upload the zip file for bulk upload and system should validate if the extension is neither zip nor .pdf or doc. 
** System should not allow the user to add multiple contracts in pdf or Zip extension in the same window

column31:
*Descripton:*

"As an admin, I want to ensure that during client and vendor creation or editing, a parent company's parent is not its child so that hierarchical relationships remain logically correct and prevent circular dependencies."

*Acceptance Criteria:*

# During *client and vendor creation or editing*, the system should prevent selecting a child company as the parent company.
# The *parent company selection field* should dynamically exclude any child company from appearing as valid choices.
# If a circular relationship is attempted, an *error message* should be displayed, informing the user of the invalid selection.
# The system should allow *successful creation and editing* when hierarchy rules are correctly followed.

column1: Existing Contracts :  "Continue" Button in Download Reports Allows Multiple Clicks, Leading to Multiple File Downloads
column31:
*Summary* 

The *"Continue"* button in the *Download Reports* modal should *disable after the first click* to prevent multiple file downloads. Currently, the button remains active, allowing users to click multiple times, which results in multiple file downloads and keeps the modal open indefinitely unless manually closed.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Navigate to the Existing Contracts page
# Click on the  *Download*  section.
# Select a *File Type* from the available options.
# Click the *"Continue"* button multiple times.
# Observe that *multiple files* are downloaded, corresponding to the number of clicks.
# Notice that the modal does *not close automatically*, requiring manual intervention.

*Expected Behavior:*

* The *"Continue"* button should *disable after the first click* to prevent multiple downloads.
* The modal should *close automatically* upon successful action.
* Only *one instance of the selected file* should be downloaded per user action.

*Actual Behavior:*

* The *"Continue"* button remains enabled, allowing *repeated clicks*.
* The system downloads *multiple copies of the file* based on the number of clicks.
* The modal does *not close automatically*, requiring manual intervention.

*Recommended Fix:*

* *Disable the "Continue" button* immediately after the first click.
* Ensure *only one file* is downloaded per user action.

*ScreenRecord :* [https://jam.dev/c/9085b1dd-1666-4abb-b632-01e71de9dbd6|https://jam.dev/c/9085b1dd-1666-4abb-b632-01e71de9dbd6|smart-link]

column1: Delayed contract listing update and success toaster message causes duplicate uploads
column31:
*Summary* 

When users upload contracts consecutively, the system experiences delays in displaying newly uploaded files in the listing page. Additionally, the success toaster message is delayed and may appear after subsequent uploads, further confusing users about whether their initial upload was successful. Since the "Create" button remains enabled during this process, users may attempt additional uploads before the previous ones are fully processed, leading to duplicate entries.

*Steps To Replicate*

# Navigate to the contract listing page.
# Click "Upload" and select a contract file.
# Submit the upload and wait for confirmation.
# Observe that the first upload does not appear promptly on the listing page.
# Repeat the steps
# Notice that the success toaster for some uploads in the middle is delayed and may display after subsequent uploads.
# The "Create" button remains enabled, allowing users to initiate another upload before the previous one is fully processed.
# Due to these delays and lack of feedback, attempt to re-upload the same contract, assuming the initial upload failed.

*Expected Result:* 

* Uploaded contracts should appear in the listing promptly.
* The success toaster message should display immediately after each upload to confirm completion and avoid confusion.
* The "Create" button should be temporarily disabled until the current upload is fully processed to prevent duplicate uploads.

*Actual Result*

* The system experiences a noticeable lag in displaying newly uploaded contracts on the listing page.
* The success toaster message appears late, sometimes after other uploads, making users unsure whether their initial upload was successful.
* The "Create" button remains enabled, leading users to initiate additional uploads before the previous ones complete, causing duplicate entries.

*Visual Proof* [https://jam.dev/c/ef5ff8db-5db6-4eee-8306-b5dda066e30e|https://jam.dev/c/ef5ff8db-5db6-4eee-8306-b5dda066e30e|smart-link] 

*Troubleshoot*

* Analyze the delay in the contract listing update process.
* Investigate backend processing time and potential bottlenecks.
* Verify whether caching or database update latency contributes to the delay.
* Assess why the success toaster message appears late and if it depends on previous processes.
* Check if the "Create" button remains active unintentionally during an ongoing upload.

*Suggested Fix*

* Temporarily disable the "Create" button during an upload process and enable it once the upload is fully processed.
* Ensure the success toaster does not get queued behind other processes, allowing it to display promptly.

column1: Error Occurs When Reuploading .doc/.docx Files from the Edit Page
column31:
*Summary* 

Users experience an error when attempting to *reupload a .doc or .docx file* from the *Edit Page*. Instead of successfully replacing or updating the document, the system either fails to upload or does not reflect the updated content correctly. This issue disrupts the document revision workflow.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Navigate to the Base Scope Library listing page
# Navigate to the *Edit Page* where document modification is enabled.
# Select  .doc or .docx file and attempt to *reupload* it.
# Observe whether the file successfully replaces the old version or displays an error.
# Verify whether the uploaded content is *correctly reflected* in the application.

*Expected Result:*

* The system should *seamlessly reupload* the modified .doc/.docx file and *update the document contents*.

*Actual Result:*

* The *reupload process fails* or does not reflect the updated file correctly.
* Users experience *errors preventing file replacement* from the Edit Page.

*Suggestions to Fix:*

* Ensure the *file replacement logic* is correctly handling .doc and .docx formats.
* Validate whether the *file update mechanism* correctly overrides the previous upload.
* Implement a *clear error message* specifying why the reupload fails.

*Troubleshooting:*

* Test the *reupload function* across multiple document formats to determine if the issue is exclusive to .doc/.docx.
* Verify *system logs* to identify any backend errors preventing successful reuploads.
* Check if *browser-specific issues* affect document replacement.

*Priority:* *High* – Critical for maintaining document revisions and workflow efficiency.

*Severity:* *Major* – Prevents users from properly updating edited documents.

column31:
*Acceptance Criteria*

# *RFP Name Field*
#* Must be pre-filled with the existing RFP name.
#* Should be editable and user should able to change the RFP name
# *Client Field*
#* Must be pre-filled with the associated client name.
#* Should be non-editable (read-only dropdown or text field).
# *Service Field*
#* Must be a required dropdown field.
#* User must select a valid service from the dropdown to proceed.
#* it should be non-editable 
# *Portfolio Selection*
#* Two radio buttons: {{Individual}} and {{Group}}.
#* Only one can be selected at a time.
#* Default option should reflect the existing data.
# *Property Selection Table*
#* Should display a paginated table with property details:
#** Property Name
#** Full Address
#** State
#** County
#** Status
#* Checkbox should be available to select/deselect each property.
#* “Select All” option must select/deselect all properties on the current page.
#* “View Selected Property” button must show a filtered list of selected properties.
# *Property Count*
#* Should show the number of properties selected out of the total.
# *Scope of Work* 
#* It should list all the selected scope of work and should able to select new scope of work or create the scope of work
#* Button should be disabled unless at least one property is selected.
#* USer should able to attach multiple files in manage attachments dialog box
# *Contract Start Date, RFP Due Date, RFI Date, RFP Award Date, RFP Extended Due Date*
#* All fields should be editable 
#* {{RFP extension date }} should be editable. 
#* Past dates should be restricted where applicable.
# *Term Field*
#* Free text input for contract duration.
#* Should be optional unless business logic dictates otherwise.
# *RFP Attachments*

* Users should be able to upload multiple files.
* Existing files must be shown with an option to remove.
* Allowed formats should include PDF, DOCX, etc. (as per business rule)

# *Update RFP Button*

* Should remain disabled until all required fields are valid.
* On clicking, should submit the form and show a success/failure message.

# *Cancel Button*

* Clicking this should discard all changes and redirect to the previous page or listing screen.

# *Field Validations*

* Display appropriate error messages for missing required fields.
* Dates must follow correct format.
* File uploads must show error if unsupported formats or limits are violated.



Functionality ; 

* System should able to validate the uniqueness of the scope of work name while editing 
* After the update the recent values should be able to reflect in the form.  
* User should able to cliick on update button both in save as draft option as well as active status 
* If 2 users open the same RFP file, then the latest edited values to be reflected.

column1: Manage attachment Integration
column31:
*Acceptance Criteria for "Manage Attachments" Dialog Box*

# Dialog Box Display & Title:

*  The "Manage Attachments" dialog box should open centered on the screen when the "Manage Attachment" action is triggered from a "Selected Scope of Work" record.
*  The dialog box title should clearly display "Manage Attachments".
* The dialog box should have a close icon (X) in the top right corner. Clicking this icon should close the dialog box.

# *Attachment Management per Property:*

*  Property Sections: The dialog box should display collapsible sections for each "Property" associated with the selected Scope of Work (e.g., "Property 1", "Property 2", etc., as seen in the screenshot).
*  Expand/Collapse: Each Property section should have an expand/collapse icon (e.g., a minus/plus sign). Clicking it should toggle the visibility of the attachment management area for that specific property.
*  File Upload: Within each expanded Property section, there should be:
* An "Add" button.
*  Successful Upload: Upon successful file selection and "Add" (or equivalent action), the attachment should be listed under the respective Property with its "Name" (filename) and a link to the "Attachment" (the file itself).
* View Attachment: Each listed attachment should have a "View" icon (eye icon). Clicking this icon should open the attachment in a new tab/window for viewing.
*  Delete Attachment: Each listed attachment should have a "Delete" icon (trash can icon). Clicking this icon should prompt a confirmation and then remove the attachment from the list and the system.

# Search and Filters:

*  Search Functionality: There should be a search bar with a placeholder "Search". Users should be able to type in keywords, and the displayed attachments should filter dynamically based on the search query (e.g., by file name).
*  Filter Button: There should be a "Filters" button. Clicking this button should reveal filtering options with property field and has attachments yes or NO 

# Pagination:

* Pagination Controls: The dialog box should display pagination controls (e.g., "1", "2", "...", "9", "10", and navigation arrows for previous/next/first/last).
*  Page Navigation: Users should be able to navigate between pages of attachments using these controls.
*  Page Information: The current page and total number of pages should be displayed (e.g., "Page 1 of 10").

# Empty States:

*  No Attachments: If a Property has no attachments, the attachment list area within that Property section should clearly indicate "No attachments found" or similar.
*  No Search Results: If a search yields no results, a message like "No matching attachments found" should be displayed.

# Error Handling:

* : Invalid File Type: The system should prevent uploading of unsupported file types and provide a clear error message.Supported format : all files should be supported except media files 
*  Upload Failure: In case of an upload failure (e.g., network issue), a clear error message should be displayed to the user.

# Integration with Scope of Work Record:
When user clicks on manage attachment by default the record will be created in draft mode.

column1: Auto-selected vendor not displayed on Vendor Selection tab (inactive or draft vendor) and "Create Vendor" field is disable
column31:
*Summary* 

When the system auto-selects a vendor—either inactive or in draft status—their name is not displayed on the Vendor Selection tab. Additionally, the “Create Vendor” text field remains disabled, preventing users from taking alternate action. This lack of visibility and control creates confusion, as users may not understand why they're unable to create or view a vendor selection.



*Steps To Replicate*

# Upload a contract (Vendor name should be present in the system and also it should be inactive or draft mode)
# Click the contract and Navigate to the Vendor Selection screen.
# Check the Vendor Selection tab and the “Create Vendor” field.

*Expected Result:*

* The auto-selected vendor (even if draft/inactive) is shown on the Vendor Selection tab.
* If the vendor is not shown, an informational message should explain their status.
* The “Create Vendor” field should be enabled if the auto-selected vendor is not valid for current use.

*Actual Result:*

* No vendor is displayed.
* “Create Vendor” field is disabled.
* User is left with no clarity on what happened or how to proceed.

*Impact:*
This leads to confusion, unnecessary troubleshooting, and potentially incorrect assumptions that the system has failed to select a vendor. It also blocks users from resolving the issue themselves.

*Environment:*
all environments

column1: System error when pressing backspace on the vendors dropdown in the client creation page
column31:

When the user selects *Approved Vendors* as "Yes" and searches for a vendor name in the Vendor field, pressing *backspace* causes a system error. The error message: {{"Cannot read properties of null (reading 'label')"}} appears, forcing a page refresh.

* Platform: Windows 11
* Browser: Chrome

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Navigate to the Client Creation page.
# Select Aprrove Vendors  ‘YES’
# Click on the Vendors dropdown.
# Begin typing a vendor name.
# Press backspace to delete characters.

*Expected Behavior:*

* The dropdown should update dynamically without causing a system error.

*Actual Behavior:*

* The system throws an error: {{"Cannot read properties of null (reading 'label')"}}
* The page displays an "Ooops, something went wrong :(" message with a refresh button.

*Possible Cause:*

* The dropdown component fails to handle the backspace event properly, possibly due to a missing value or improper reference to a null property.

*Suggested Fix:*

* Ensure proper validation and handling of empty states when backspace is pressed.
* Implement a check before accessing the 'label' property to prevent null reference errors.

When creating a new client, drafted vendors should be listed in the *Vendor* dropdown, but currently, no options appear when searching for vendors.

*Environment:*

* *URL:* {{https://stage.joinconnexus.com/client}}
* *Platform:* Windows 11
* *Browser:* Chrome

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Navigate to the *Client Creation* page.
# Set *Approved Vendors* to "Yes."
# Click on the *Vendor* field and type a drafted vendor name.

*Expected Behavior:*

* The dropdown should list available *drafted vendors* matching the search query.

*Actual Behavior:*

* The dropdown displays *"No options"* even when matching vendors exist.

*Possible Cause:*

* Drafted vendors may not be included in the dropdown population logic.
* Filtering conditions may unintentionally exclude drafted vendors from the list.

*Suggested Fix:*

* Verify that drafted vendors are correctly retrieved in the dropdown query.
* Ensure drafted vendors are not excluded due to a filter mismatch or visibility restriction.

*Type:* Backend 
*Summary:* Update the {{Services}} model to support a self-referencing hierarchy.
*Description:*

* Add {{parentServiceId}} and self-referencing relation.
* Remove {{subServices}} relation.
* Remove {{ServiceType}} enum.
*Labels:* prisma, schema, migration

----

h3. *Task 2: Schema Cleanup - Remove SubServices Model*

*Type:* Backend
*Summary:* Remove the {{SubServices}} model from the database schema.
*Description:*

* Completely drop the {{SubServices}} model.
* Remove all associated relations and references from the schema.
*Labels:* prisma, schema, cleanup

----

h3. *Task 3: Schema Update - Refactor PropertyServiceMap Model*

*Type:* Backend
*Summary:* Simplify {{PropertyServiceMap}} model.
*Description:*

* Remove {{subServiceId}}, {{subservice}} relation, and {{serviceType}} field.
* Remove self-referencing structure.
*Labels:* prisma, schema

----

h3. *Task 4: Schema Update - Refactor ScopeOfWork Model*

*Type:* Backend
*Summary:* Remove {{subServiceId}} from {{ScopeOfWork}} model.
*Description:*

* Update schema and all relations using {{subServiceId}}.
*Labels:* prisma, schema

----

h3. *Task 5: Data Migration Script*

*Type:* Backend
*Summary:* Write SQL migration to merge SubServices into Services.
*Description:*

* Migrate {{SubServices}} into {{Services}} table.
* Rename migrated services to ensure uniqueness.
* Update {{parentServiceId}} for child services.
* Update foreign keys in {{PropertyServiceMap}} and {{ScopeOfWork}}.
* Drop {{SubServices}} table after migration.
*Labels:* prisma, migration, SQL

----

h3. *Task 6: Code Cleanup - Remove Sub-Services Module (connexus-be)*

*Type:* Backend
*Summary:* Delete {{sub-services}} module from {{connexus-be}}.
*Description:*

* Remove entire {{apps/connexus-be/src/services/sub-services/}} directory.
*Labels:* cleanup, refactor

----

h3. *Task 7: Refactor Services Module (connexus-be)*

*Type:* Backend
*Summary:* Update services module for self-referencing model.
*Description:*

* Update service creation to handle {{parentServiceId}}.
* Fetch {{childServices}} in queries.
* Update DTOs to remove {{subServices}} and add {{parentServiceId}}.
* Simplify {{validateServiceNames}}.
* Prevent deletion of parent services with children.
*Labels:* refactor, backend

----

h3. *Task 8: Refactor Property-Services Module (connexus-be)*

*Type:* Backend
*Summary:* Refactor {{property-services}} to support flat service IDs.
*Description:*

* Accept flat array of service IDs in DTOs.
* Remove all sub-service mapping logic.
*Labels:* refactor, backend

----

h3. *Task 9: Refactor Properties Module (connexus-be)*

*Type:* Backend
*Summary:* Refactor properties module to align with new service mapping.
*Description:*

* Update {{create-property.dto.ts}} to accept flat service IDs.
* Refactor {{property-helpers.ts}} to align with new DTOs.
*Labels:* refactor, backend

----

h3. *Task 10: Refactor Contracts Module (connexus-be)*

*Type:* Backend
*Summary:* Update {{findServices}} logic in contracts module.
*Description:*

* Update search to handle parent-child service hierarchy.
* Adapt to the new {{servicesName}} structure.
*Labels:* refactor, backend

----

h3. *Task 11: Refactor Scope of Work Modules (sow-rfq)*

*Type:* Backend
*Summary:* Refactor scope of work and client scope of work modules in {{sow-rfq}}.
*Description:*

* Remove all {{subServiceId}} logic.
* Update DTOs to use only {{serviceId}}.
* Simplify service selection logic.
*Labels:* refactor, backend


----

h3. Affected Applications & APIs

h4. 🏢 *Connexus-BE Application*

h5. 1. Service Management ({{/services}} endpoints)

*Breaking Changes:*

* {{POST /services}}
** ❌ No longer accepts nested {{subServices}} array
** ✅ New: Use optional {{parentServiceId}} to create child services
** ❌ Removed: {{subServices}} property from request body
* {{GET /services}}
** ❌ Response no longer contains nested {{subServices}} array
* {{GET /services/:id}}
** ❌ Response no longer contains {{subServices}}
* {{DELETE /services/:id}}
** 🚫 Now prevents deletion if service has {{childServices}}

*Removed Endpoints:*

* All {{/sub-services/*}} endpoints (entire module deleted)

----

h5. 2. Property Services ({{/property-services}} endpoints)

*Breaking Changes:*

* {{POST /property-services}}
** 🔄 Completely restructured
** Old: Complex object with parent service and sub-services
** New: Simple {{{ propertyId, serviceIds: string[] }}}
* {{GET /property-services}}
** 🔄 Response simplified
** ❌ Removed: Parent/child structure and {{serviceType}} field
* ❌ {{PATCH /property-services/:id}} endpoint removed
** Service associations now managed via individual add/delete operations

----

h5. 3. Property Management ({{/properties}} endpoints)

*Breaking Changes:*

* {{POST /properties}}
** 🔄 {{services}} field changed
** Old: Nested object structure
** New: Flat array of service IDs ({{string[]}})

----

h5. 4. Vendor Management ({{/vendors}} endpoints)

*No External API Changes:*

* ✅ {{POST /vendors}} and {{PATCH /vendors/:id}} endpoints unchanged
* ✅ {{services}} and {{additionalServices}} fields remain as flat string arrays
* 🔄 Internal logic updated for new {{VendorServices}} model

----

h4. 📋 *SOW-RFQ Application*

h5. 1. Scope of Work Management ({{/scope-of-work}} and {{/client-scope-of-work}})

*Breaking Changes:*

* {{POST /scope-of-work}}
** ❌ No longer accepts {{subServiceId}}
* {{PATCH /scope-of-work/:id}}
** ❌ No longer accepts {{subServiceId}}
* {{POST /client-scope-of-work}}
** ❌ No longer accepts {{subServiceId}}
* {{GET /scope-of-work}}
** ❌ Filtering by {{subServiceId}} removed
* {{GET /client-scope-of-work}}
** ❌ Filtering by {{subServiceId}} removed
* 🔄 All responses no longer contain sub-service data

----

h3. Frontend Impact

⚡ *Critical:*
Any frontend components relying on the old two-level service/sub-service structure must be updated to handle the new flat service model.

----

h3. Testing Required

Service creation with parent-child relationships, Property service associations, Vendor service assignments, Scope of work creation and filtering, All affected API endpoints, Frontend service selection components

*Medium* – Affects usability and accuracy in service selection, though a workaround (exact match input) is available.

column31:
h3. *User Story: AI-Assisted Contract Field Extraction and Prompt Refinement*

*As a* developer working on an AI-based contract analysis tool,
*I want* to automatically extract and validate the "start date" and "end date" fields from various construction-related service procurement contracts,
*So that* I can generate accurate, generic prompts for large language models (LLMs) to extract these fields reliably—even in exceptional or non-standard cases.

h3. *Acceptance Criteria:*

# *Upload and Analyze Contracts:*
#* The system uploads each contract to Gemini (or any capable LLM).
#* The model is prompted to act as a _contract analyzer experienced in construction-related service procurement_.
# *Field Extraction Reasoning:*
#* For each field ("start date" and "end date"), the AI must:
#** Identify the extracted value.
#** Explain the reasoning behind the selected value (e.g., based on specific clauses, phrasing, or placement in the document).
# *Definition and Clarification:*
#* If the AI cannot confidently identify a field, it must:
#** Ask for a definition of the field.
#** Suggest what additional context or business rules might be needed.
# *Handle Exceptional Cases:*
#* Contracts with exceptional structures or non-standard formatting are included.
#* AI must identify reasons these cases are challenging and suggest logic to handle them.
# *Prompt Refinement:*
#* Based on the gathered reasoning and exceptions:
#** Ask the AI to generate accurate, *generalized prompts* to extract "start date" and "end date" from similar contracts.
#** Prompts should include logic to improve performance in both typical and exceptional cases.
# *Iterative Improvement:*
#* Use feedback from multiple contracts to continuously refine the prompts.
#* Ensure final prompts are field-specific, context-aware, and business-useful.

column1: Add File Type Selection & Download Feature to SOW List Page
column31:
h2. Objective

Implement a file type selection and download feature on the SOW (Scope of Work) list page, available on all three tabs. This feature should allow users to select a file type (e.g., PDF, Excel) via a popup and download the SOW list in the chosen format.

----

h2. Requirements

h3. 1. UI Changes

* *Download Button*

* Add a download button to the SOW list page, visible on all three tabs.

* The button should be styled and positioned consistently with the current SOW list page UI.

* *File Type Selection Popup*

* When the download button is clicked, display a popup/modal for file type selection.

* The popup should include:

* A header/title (e.g., "Select File Type")

* File type options (e.g., PDF, Excel)

* "Continue" and "Cancel" actions

h3. 2. Functionality

* *Popup State Management*

* Use a state variable (e.g., {{fileSelectionPopup}}) to control the popup’s visibility.

* *File Type Handling*

* When a file type is selected and confirmed, trigger a function to call a new SOW download API with the selected file type as a parameter.

* *API Integration*

* Implement a new API endpoint for the SOW module that accepts the file type and relevant filter parameters, and returns a URL for the generated file.

* The API should follow the workspace's standard API writing pattern ({{api-writting-pattern}} rule).

* On successful API response, open the returned file URL in a new tab or trigger a download.

h3. 3. Code Structure

* *Component Reuse*

* Use or adapt a popup/modal component for the file type selection.

* Ensure the popup and button logic works for all three SOW list tabs.

* *State and Handlers*

* Add state and handler functions for opening/closing the popup and handling file type selection.

* Integrate handlers with the SOW list page’s logic.

h3. 4. Testing

* Test the download button and popup on all three SOW list tabs.

* Verify the correct file type is sent to the API and the file is generated/downloaded as expected.

* Ensure the UI/UX is consistent with the SOW module’s design.

----

h2. References

* *Popup Component*

Use or adapt an existing popup/modal component for file type selection.

* *API Writing Pattern*

Follow the workspace's {{api-writting-pattern}} rule for new API implementation.

----

h2. Deliverables

* Updated SOW list page with file type selection and download feature on all tabs.

* New SOW download API endpoint and integration.

* Code reviewed and tested for all scenarios.

----

* Sanitize service name extraction to eliminate empty entries before rendering

02/Sep/25 4:38 PM;6090062d2c2f6c0068c1341b;h1. Vendor Matching Conditions

h2. Overview

The system finds vendors that can service a property's location using multiple matching strategies while respecting client vendor approval preferences.

h2. Vendor Matching Sources

The system checks *four different sources* to find eligible vendors:

h3. 1. Approved Vendors ({{APPROVED_VENDOR}})

*Condition*: Vendors explicitly approved by the client

*Query Logic*:

* Must be in {{ApprovedClientVendors}} table for the client
* Must provide the requested service (exists in {{VendorServices}})
* Must have status {{ACTIVE}} or {{DRAFT}}
* *Geographic coverage ignored* - can serve anywhere for approved clients

*Business Rule*: Approved vendors get priority and can serve any location for their client.

h3. 2. Continental US Vendors ({{CONTINENTAL_US}})

*Condition*: Vendors that cover the entire continental United States

*Query Logic*:

* Must have {{vendorServiceCoverContinentalUs = true}}
* Must provide the requested service
* Must have status {{ACTIVE}} or {{DRAFT}}
* *Geographic coverage ignored* - can serve anywhere in continental US

*Business Rule*: These vendors have nationwide coverage capability.

h3. 3. Outside Service Area Vendors ({{OUTSIDE_SERVICE_AREA}})

*Condition*: Vendors interested in receiving RFPs outside their defined service areas

*Query Logic*:

* Must have {{vendorInterestedReceiveRfpOutside = true}}
* Must provide the requested service
* Must have status {{ACTIVE}} or {{DRAFT}}
* *Geographic coverage ignored* - want to expand beyond defined areas

*Business Rule*: These vendors want opportunities outside their normal service areas.

h3. 4. Geographic Coverage Vendors ({{GEOGRAPHIC_COVERAGE}})

*Condition*: Vendors with specific geographic coverage in the service area

*Query Logic*:

* Must have coverage in {{ServiceUnitCoverage}} table
* Uses *hierarchical OR logic*:
** City coverage: {{geoScope = 'CITY' AND geoId = cityId}}
** County coverage: {{geoScope = 'COUNTY' AND geoId = countyId}}  
** State coverage: {{geoScope = 'STATE' AND geoId = stateId}}
* Must provide the requested service
* Must have status {{ACTIVE}} or {{DRAFT}}

*Business Rule*: Standard geographic matching based on defined service coverage areas.

h2. Exclusion Rules

h3. Always Excluded

# *Non-Approved Vendors*: Vendors in {{ClientNotApprovedVendor}} table with {{isDeleted = false}}
# *Inactive Vendors*: Vendors with status other than {{ACTIVE}} or {{DRAFT}}
# *Non-Service Providers*: Vendors who don't provide the requested service

h3. Service Requirement

*All vendor categories must provide the requested service*. This is enforced through:

* Join with {{VendorServices}} table
* Filter: {{vendorServices.serviceId = requestedServiceId}}

h2. Deduplication Logic

* Combines results from all four sources
* Removes duplicates based on: {{vendorId + serviceId}}
* Preserves the first occurrence found (approval status takes precedence due to query order)

h2. Response Structure

Each matched vendor includes:

{noformat}{
  tenantId: string,
  vendor: {
    id: string,
    name: string, 
    status: string,
    stage: string
  },
  coverageType: GeoScope, // CITY | COUNTY | STATE
  serviceId: string,
  matchingSource: VendorMatchingSource // How vendor was matched
}{noformat}

h2. Hierarchical Coverage Logic

For geographic coverage matching, the system uses *OR logic*:

* *City Match*: Vendor has city-level coverage for the property's city
* *County Match*: Vendor has county-level coverage for the property's county
* *State Match*: Vendor has state-level coverage for the property's state

*Any match is acceptable* - vendors don't need coverage at all geographic levels.

h2. Example Usage

{noformat}const vendors = await serviceCoverageService.getVendorsForProperty({
  clientId: 'client-uuid',
  cityId: 'chicago-id',      // Optional
  countyId: 'cook-county-id', // Optional  
  stateId: 'illinois-id',     // Required
  serviceId: 'plumbing-id'    // Required
});{noformat}

column31:
h1. *BgJobs - Background Job Management System*

h2. *Overview*

The BgJobs system is a comprehensive background job management solution that provides real-time monitoring, status tracking, and user interaction capabilities for long-running asynchronous tasks in the Connexus web application. The system is specifically designed to handle SOW (Statement of Work) template generation tasks with extensible architecture for future job types.

h2. *Core Components*

h3. *1. Redux State Management (bgJobs.slice.ts)*

* *State Structure*: Manages job queues and UI state using Redux Toolkit
* *Job Types*: Currently supports {{SOW_TEMPLATE_GENERATION}} with extensible enum for future job types
* *Job Status*: Three states - {{PENDING}}, {{SUCCESS}}, {{ERROR}}
* *Actions*: CRUD operations for job management (setItem, deleteItem, updateItem, resetBgJobs)
* *UI State*: Controls popover visibility and trigger display

h3. *2. Background Job Indicator (BackgroundJobIndicator.tsx)*

* *Visual Indicator*: Floating button positioned at bottom-right corner (z-index: 50)
* *Smart Visibility*: Only appears when background jobs are active
* *Animation*: Pulsing shadow animation ({{bgjob-shadow-animate}}) for 6 seconds when jobs are pending
* *Popover Interface*: Expandable panel showing all active background jobs
* *Auto-hide*: Users can dismiss the indicator with an X button

h3. *3. Job Status Viewer (BgStatusViewer.tsx)*

* *Status-specific UI*: Different visual states for PENDING, SUCCESS, and ERROR
* *Interactive Actions*:
** Download button for completed jobs
** Retry button for failed jobs
** Clear button to remove jobs from queue
* *Visual Feedback*: Loading spinners, status icons, and color-coded buttons
* *Delete Confirmation*: Modal dialog for job removal with confirmation

h3. *4. SOW Template Poller (SowTemplatePoller.tsx)*

* *Dual Role*: Acts as both poller (hidden) and viewer (visible)
* *Real-time Polling*: 10-second intervals to check job status via API
* *Status Synchronization*: Updates Redux state based on backend task status
* *File Download*: Handles template download with progress indication
* *Retry Logic*: Allows users to retry failed template generation

h2. *Key Features*

h3. *Real-time Monitoring*

* Automatic polling every 10 seconds for pending jobs
* Immediate status updates when jobs complete or fail
* Visual feedback with animated indicators

h3. *User Experience*

* Non-intrusive floating indicator that appears only when needed
* Expandable popover with detailed job information
* One-click actions for download, retry, and clear operations
* Toast notifications for user feedback

h3. *Error Handling*

* Graceful handling of failed jobs with retry capability
* Clear error states with actionable buttons
* Automatic cleanup of completed jobs

h3. *Performance Optimization*

* Lazy polling (only when jobs are pending)
* Efficient Redux state management
* Minimal re-renders with React.memo and useMemo

h2. *Integration Points*

h3. *API Integration*

* {{useTemplateGenerationTask}} hook for status polling
* {{useGenerateClientSowTemplate}} for template generation
* {{useCreateDownloadUrl}} for file download handling

h3. *Layout Integration*

* Embedded in {{ProtectedLayout}} for global availability
* Positioned absolutely to avoid layout interference
* High z-index to ensure visibility

h3. *SOW Module Integration*

* Integrated with SOW template download functionality
* Handles both PDF and DOCX format generation
* Prevents duplicate job creation for same SOW/format combination

h2. *Technical Specifications*

h3. *State Management*

{{type BgJobValueMode = {}}

{{  status: BgJobStatus;}}

{{  name: string;}}

{{  type: BgJobType;}}

{{  metaData?: TemplateGenerationTaskType;}}

{{  retryCount: number;}}

{{  bgJobKey: string;}}

{{};}}



h3. *CSS Animation*

{{@keyframes bgjob-shadow-pulse {}}

{{  0% { box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 rgba(1, 82, 148, 0.7); }}}

{{  70% { box-shadow: 0 0 16px 8px rgba(1, 82, 148, 0); }}}

{{  100% { box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 rgba(1, 82, 148, 0); }}}

{{}}}



h3. *Polling Configuration*

* Initial delay: 10 seconds before first poll
* Polling interval: 10 seconds
* Automatic stop when job completes or fails

h2. *Future Extensibility*

* Enum-based job type system allows easy addition of new job types
* Modular component architecture supports different job handlers
* Redux state structure can accommodate additional job metadata
* UI components are generic and reusable for different job types

This system provides a robust foundation for managing background tasks with excellent user experience and technical reliability.

column1: Optimising SOW Template DOC Generation
column31:
h3. 
*🎯 Objective*

Optimized the {{generateSowTemplate}} method to improve performance, prevent duplicate requests, and provide better user experience.

h3. *✅ Changes Implemented*

h4. *1. Duplicate Request Prevention*

* Added check for existing pending template generation tasks

* Returns existing pending task instead of creating duplicates

* Prevents unnecessary SQS processing and database entries

h4. *2. Smart Template Reuse*

* Added check for existing completed templates

* Compares timestamps of related data (client, service, scope of work, properties)

* Reuses existing template if no data has changed since generation

* Reduces redundant template generation

h4. *3. Force Regeneration Feature*

* Added {{forceRegeneration}} parameter to DTO

* Allows users to force fresh template generation when needed

* Maintains backward compatibility

h4. *4. Database Query Optimization*

* *Reduced queries*: From 3+ separate queries to 2 optimized queries

* *Transaction wrapping*: Ensures data consistency and prevents race conditions

* *Selective field fetching*: Only fetch required fields ({{id}}, {{modifiedAt}}) instead of full records

* *Property optimization*: Only check most recent property instead of all properties

h4. *5. Enhanced User Experience*

* *Improved response messages*:

* Pending: "Template generation already in progress"

* Completed: "Using existing template (generated on [date])"

* Force regeneration: "Template generation started (forced regeneration)"

* New task: "Template generation started"

h3. *📈 Performance Improvements*

* *Data transfer reduced by 80-90%* (selective field fetching)

* *Query count reduced* (from 3+ to 2 queries)

* *Memory usage optimized* (only essential data loaded)

* *Property checking optimized* (1 property vs potentially hundreds)

h3. *🔧 Technical Details*

* *Files modified*:

* {{client-scope-of-work.service.ts}}

* {{get-sow-template.dto.ts}}

* *New DTO field*: {{forceRegeneration?: boolean}}

* *Database*: Uses Prisma transactions for consistency

* *Logic*: Comprehensive change detection across all related entities

[SOW] Filter UI: Uploaded vs. Updated Date Chips Look Identical, Causing Confusion
column31:
*Summary* 

When applying filters for both _Uploaded Date_ and _Updated Date_, the values are displayed as UI chips that look identical in style. This makes it difficult for users to distinguish which chip corresponds to which filter type. This can lead to misinterpretation of the filter criteria and potential errors in filtering results.



*Steps To Replicate*

* Navigate to the SOW page with filter options.
* Apply a date range for _Uploaded Date_.
* Apply a date range for _Updated Date_.
* Observe the chips displayed in the filter summary section.



*Expected Result:* 

Chips should have clear labels or distinct styles indicating whether they belong to _Uploaded Date_ or _Updated Date_. UI needs to be improved for better clarity.

*Actual Result*

Chips for both date filters appear visually identical and lack context labels, leading to confusion.

*Suggested Improvement*

* Add labels to date chips (e.g., “Uploaded: [Date Range]” vs “Updated: [Date Range]”).
* Consider grouping chips by filter categories for better visual separation.





*Screenshots*

Pagination on Select SOW Tab Retains Last Opened Page
column31:
*Summary:*
In the "Select Scope of Work" tab, pagination does not reset to the first page when the tab is reopened. Instead, the system retains the last viewed page, requiring users to manually navigate back to page 1.

*Environment:*

* *Module:* Scope of Work Selection
* *Tab:* Select SOW (Client Scope Library / Commensus Scope Library)

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Open the "Select Scope of Work" tab.
# Navigate to page 2 or beyond.
# Close or switch away from the tab.
# or Create an SOW using Connexus or Client Library
# Reopen the tab.
# Observe that the pagination remains on the previously viewed page.

*Expected Behavior:*

* Pagination should reset to page 1 upon reopening the tab.
* This ensures consistent user experience and avoids confusion when selecting new scopes.

*Actual Behavior:*

* The system retains the last opened page.
* Users must manually navigate back to the first page to view initial entries.

*Impact:*

* Reduces usability and efficiency, especially for users expecting a fresh view.
* Increases risk of overlooking earlier entries.
* May cause confusion in workflows involving multiple scope selections.

*Suggested Fixes:*

* Implement a reset trigger for pagination when the tab is reopened.
* Optionally, allow users to configure default pagination behavior (e.g., “Remember last page” vs. “Always start at page 1”).
* Include confirmation messaging or visual cue indicating current page context.

column31:
h1. Comparison of Boundary Data Sources for Service Areas

h2. 1. OpenStreetMap (Overpass API)

*Description:*  
Queries live OpenStreetMap data to retrieve administrative boundaries such as cities, counties, or states.

*Pros:*

* Free to use and globally available.
* Updated frequently (changes appear within minutes).
* Detailed boundaries for many regions.
* Works directly with GeoPandas for easy processing.

*Cons:*

* Rate limits on the public Overpass API (may need self-hosting for high volume).
* Boundary accuracy can vary in less-mapped regions.
* Complex queries may require some OSM data model knowledge.

----

h2. 2. Mapbox Boundaries API

*Description:*  
Commercial API providing administrative boundary polygons derived from OSM and official datasets.

*Pros:*

* High accuracy and consistent coverage.
* Regularly updated from multiple authoritative sources.
* Easy-to-use API, returns ready-to-use GeoJSON.
* Includes additional metadata like population, ISO codes, etc.

*Cons:*

* Paid service (limited free tier).
* Requires API key and internet access at runtime.
* Slight delay between OSM edits and API updates.

----

h2. 3. HERE Geocoding & Search API

*Description:*  
Geocoding API with administrative area data, including polygon boundaries for many locations.

*Pros:*

* Reliable global coverage with commercial-grade data.
* Updated regularly.
* Simple integration with familiar geocoding workflows.
* Provides both point and polygon geometry.

*Cons:*

* Paid service after free tier.
* Not all places have detailed polygon boundaries.
* Update frequency varies by region (may not be as fast as OSM).

----

h2. 4. US Census TIGER/Line Data

*Description:*  
Official US Census Bureau shapefiles containing precise boundaries for counties, cities, and other administrative divisions (US only).

*Pros:*

* Very accurate and authoritative for US boundaries.
* Available for multiple administrative levels.
* Free to use and downloadable in bulk.

*Cons:*

* US-only coverage.
* Updated annually (not suitable for real-time changes).
* Large file sizes can make processing slower without simplification.

----

h2. 5. GeoPandas Processing

*Description:*  
Python library for working with geospatial data; can be used to process and combine boundary data from various sources.

*Pros:*

* Works with multiple formats (Shapefile, GeoJSON, PostGIS, etc.).
* Can merge, simplify, or transform boundaries easily.
* Integrates with both static datasets (Census, shapefiles) and dynamic APIs (OSM, Mapbox).

*Cons:*

* Not a data source itself — needs external datasets or APIs.
* Handling large datasets may require optimization.
* Requires Python environment and dependencies.

----

h2. Recommendation

*Recommended Approach:* *Mapbox Boundaries API*

*Reasoning:*

* Provides global, production-grade boundary data with consistent accuracy.
* Updated regularly from both OSM and official government sources.
* Easy to integrate directly into applications via API.
* Eliminates need to self-host or manage large shapefiles.
* Ideal for creating and maintaining accurate service areas without heavy infrastructure.
* Easy for migrating existing data

column1: Contract End Date Not Calculated from 'Terms of Contract'
column31:
*Summary* 

In the RFP creation and detail views, the *Contract End Date* field incorrectly displays *"N/A"*, even when a valid *Contract Start Date* and *Terms of Contract* are provided. The system fails to compute and populate the end date based on the selected contract duration.



*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Navigate to the *RFP Create* page.
# Enter a valid *Contract Start Date*.
# Select a value for *Terms of Contract* (e.g., 6 months, 1 year).
# Save the RFP and view it in the *RFP Detail* page.
# Observe the *Contract End Date* field.



*Expected Behavior:*

* The system should calculate the *Contract End Date* by adding the duration from *Terms of Contract* to the *Contract Start Date*.
* The calculated end date should be displayed in  the  *RFP Detail* views.



*Actual Behavior:*

* The *Contract End Date* field displays *"N/A"* regardless of the selected *Terms of Contract*.
* No calculation is performed, and the field remains blank or non-functional.



 *Impact:*

* Leads to incomplete contract data in RFP records.

 Suggested Fix:

* Implement logic to dynamically calculate and populate the *Contract End Date* based on the selected *Terms of Contract* and *Contract Start Date*.
* Ensure recalculation occurs on edit and is reflected in all relevant views.

#* Navigating to other modules

* The user session should be terminated immediately.
* All further actions should be blocked.
* A message should be displayed:



* “Your account has been deactivated. Please contact support to reactivate access.”



 *Actual Behavior*

* Account status is updated to “Inactive.”
* Session remains active.

column1: Change in response comment for already satisfied queries.
column31:
*Description:*
In the current GPT-based SOW editing service, when a customer’s prompt requests a change, we handle invalid or irrelevant inputs by returning a generic message: _"The provided input is not related to SOW."_

We need to enhance the response logic to differentiate between:

* *Case 1:* Input is unrelated to the SOW → return existing generic message.
* *Case 2:* Input is related to the SOW but the requested requirement is already addressed in the existing document → return new message:
_"_-_Requested change is already covered in the current SOW_-_." “_*Duplicate Detected:*The change you requested is already included in the current Scope of Work” [~accountid:62146cb42d057500723ebae2] Please add this message.

*Acceptance Criteria:*

* Implement check to identify when a requested change matches existing SOW content.
* Ensure GPT returns the new “already covered” message for Case 2.
* Retain existing unrelated-input message for Case 1.
* Add test cases for both scenarios.

*Impact:*
Improves clarity for users by giving more specific feedback and avoiding the impression that relevant changes are being ignored.

* Preserve selected SOWs in session or local state to maintain continuity.

* No validation message is shown.
* The form allows submission with invalid date logic.



 *Expected Behavior:*

* The *Extended Due Date* should be saved correctly.
* A validation check should prevent users from selecting an Extended Due Date that is *on or before* the original RFP Due Date.
* A clear error message should be displayed, e.g.:
* "Extended Due Date must be later than the original RFP Due Date."

 *Actual Behavior:*

* Selected Extended Due Date is not saved.
* No validation is triggered for illogical date entries.
* Form submission proceeds without warning.

 *Impact:*

* Allows invalid RFP timelines, potentially confusing vendors and internal teams.



 *Suggested Fixes:*

column1: UX- No Feedback on Timeout or Slow Network – RFP Page Shows "No Results"
column31:
*Summary* 

When the network is slow or times out, the *RFP listing table* fails to load data and displays *“No results”* without any indication of the underlying issue. Users are left unaware whether:

* The data is still loading,
* A timeout occurred,
* Or no data exists.



📌 Steps to Reproduce:

# Simulate a slow or unstable network connection.
# Navigate to the *Request For Proposal* section.
# Observe the table — it shows “No results” without any loading indicator or error message.



❌ Actual Behavior:

* Table appears empty with “No results.”
* No visual feedback (e.g., spinner, timeout alert, retry option).
* Users may assume there is no data, leading to confusion or incorrect assumptions.



🧭 Expected Behavior:

* Display a *loading spinner or skeleton UI* while data is being fetched.
* If a timeout or network error occurs, show a *clear message* such as:
* 
* “We’re having trouble loading the data. Please check your connection or try again.”
* 
* Include a *Retry button* or auto-retry logic.
* Optionally log timeout events for backend monitoring.



✅ Suggested Fix:

* Implement frontend error handling for API timeouts and slow responses.
* Add visual indicators for loading and error states.
* Ensure fallback messaging is user-friendly and actionable.

column1: ChatGPT redesign of prompt and flow as per client requirement
column31:
Acceptance criteria: 

As a user i want to create scope of work from chatgpt from my application and it should be a conversational mode. 

*Acceptance criteria:* 

h3.  Scope of Work Generation Screen Layout

* *Left Side:* Chat Window (Conversational Assistant)
** Default: expanded view.
** Provides conversational prompts to refine scope of work (e.g., "Do you want to add labor hours?").
** Has a *minimize option*, collapsing into a *robot icon* (as shown in second screenshot).
** When minimized:
*** Only the robot icon is visible.
*** Clicking the icon re-expands the chat window.
** Provides conversational prompts to refine scope of work (e.g., "Do you want to add labor hours?").
* *Right Side:* Output Window
** Displays the *generated Scope of Work*.
** Generated content includes editable text.
** User can click *edit icon* to modify the text directly.
** Any manual changes are retained until user leaves the screen.
* When user add the input in chat window it will AI should respnd based on the input and should able to genrate the document based on the output. 

h3. 3. Data Persistence

* While in chat session:
** Chat history is *not saved* anywhere.
** On leaving the screen → chat data is lost.
* Only when the user *clicks "Generate Scope of Work" button*:
** The final scope of work content is stored in the database along with linked *Client, Service, and Property*.

h3. 4. Navigation Behavior

* User can navigate to other screens using the left sidebar menu.
* If user tries to leave while still in the Scope of Work screen:
** A *confirmation modal* appears:
*** Message: _“Are you sure you want to leave this page? Your chat session will be lost.”_
*** Options: *Yes, Leave* | *Cancel*
** If confirmed:
*** Navigation proceeds.
*** Chat session is discarded.

column1: Service Category Name Uniqueness Validation Ignores Trailing/Leading Spaces
column31:
*Summary* 

*Module:* Service Category Management / SOW Creation
*Issue:*
The system currently allows creation of service categories with names that differ only by leading or trailing spaces. This bypasses uniqueness validation and results in duplicate entries that appear identical to users.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Create a service category named *"CAPEX"*
# Attempt to create another service category named *"CAPEX "* (with a trailing space)
# System allows the second entry without flagging it as a duplicate

*Expected Behavior:*
Service category names should be treated as *trimmed strings* during uniqueness validation. Names like {{"CAPEX"}} and {{" CAPEX "}} should be considered duplicates and rejected with a clear error message.

*Actual Behavior:*
The system treats {{"CAPEX"}} and {{"CAPEX "}} as distinct entries, allowing both to be saved.

*Impact:*

* Duplicate service categories with visually identical names
* Confusion during selection and reporting
* Increased risk of misclassification and data inconsistency

*Suggested Fix:*

* Apply {{.trim()}} logic to service category names before validation
* Update error messaging to reflect trimmed comparison (e.g., “Service category name must be unique.”)

*Severity:* Medium – affects data integrity and user experience

column1: [Trello] Request For Proposal – Copy/Duplicate Button Missing in RFP Template Actions
column31:
📝 *Description:*

*What*
On the *RFP Template page*, the action menu (three dots) currently includes:

* View RFP Details
* Edit RFP Description
* PDF Format Download
* Doc Format Download

However, the *Copy (Duplicate) option* is missing. Users have no way to quickly duplicate an RFP Template for reuse.

*Where*
Module: *Request For Proposal*
Screen: *RFP Template*
Action Menu (top right corner)

*Expected*

* Add a *Copy/Duplicate button* in the action menu, alongside existing actions.
* When clicked, it should:
** Create a new RFP Template with the same details (title, body, attachments, etc.).
** Allow the user to edit before saving to avoid unintentional duplication.
* Button label: *Copy* or *Duplicate* with an appropriate icon (two overlapping rectangles).

*Impact*

* Without this option, users must manually recreate RFP Templates, leading to inefficiency.
* Increases the risk of data entry errors.
* Slows down the workflow when similar RFP Templates are needed across multiple clients/projects.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Navigate to *Request For Proposal → RFP Template*.
# Open the action menu (three dots).
# Observe that options for View, Edit, and Downloads exist.
# Note that *Copy/Duplicate option is missing*.





_Comments by Mike : please scope out the time to determine timing for this feature. One enhancement is that client should be able to duplicate an RFP without going into the template. So they should be able to do so from the scroll view._

column1: [Trello] Request For Proposal – Attachments in Detail View Missing Delete Option
column31:
📝 *Description:*

*What*
On the *RFP Detail page*, uploaded files (e.g., *TPS-Landscaping.pdf*) are displayed with a download link, but there is *no option to remove/delete* them. Users can view and download attachments but cannot manage (delete) them.

*Where*
Module: *Request For Proposal*
Screen: *RFP Detail View*
Section: *Attachments*

*Expected*

* Each uploaded file should be displayed with:
** *File name* (clickable to view/download).
** *Download icon* (✔ already exists).
** *Remove/Delete (X) icon* to allow users to delete the attachment if needed.
* A confirmation modal should appear before deletion:
** Example: “Are you sure you want to delete TPS-Landscaping.pdf?”

*Impact*

* Users cannot remove outdated, incorrect, or duplicate files.
* Increases risk of version confusion and clutter in RFP records.
* Prevents proper document lifecycle management.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Navigate to *Request For Proposal* → create or edit an RFP.
# Upload a file (e.g., PDF, DOC).
# Save the RFP and go to *RFP Detail View*.
# Observe that attachments are displayed with a download option only.
# No *delete (X) option* is available for file removal.



!image (40).png|width=1291,height=535,alt="image (40).png"!









_Comments by Mike : a details screen is not commonly the action screen. From a user experience perspective, being able to drilldown into edit and delete from there makes logical sense. Allowing for a deletion without formally editing opens up other rule and permission based concerns architecturally that we shouldn’t be crossing at this point._

column1: SOW Preview Updates Incorrectly After User Sends 'No' Confirmation
column31:
*Summary* 
SOW preview content changes even when user rejects AI-generated summary



*Environment:*

* Module: SOW Chat Panel
* Component: Scope of Work Preview

 *Description:*

When the AI assistant asks the user to confirm changes to the Scope of Work (SOW) and the user responds with *"No"*, the system still proceeds to update the SOW preview with changes. This behavior contradicts the user's intent and undermines the approval workflow.

 *Steps to Reproduce:*

# Interact with the AI in the SOW Chat Panel.
# Receive a proposed summary or update to the Scope of Work.
# Respond with *"No"* when asked to confirm changes.
# Observe that the SOW preview on the right side still reflects the proposed updates.

 *Actual Result:*

* SOW preview is updated despite user rejecting the changes.
* No rollback or preservation of the previous version is triggered.

 *Expected Result:*

* If the user responds with *"No"*, the SOW preview should remain unchanged.
* The system should either retain the previous version or prompt the user for further clarification before applying any updates.

 *Impact:*

* May lead to incorrect documentation being finalized
* Reduces trust in AI-driven content generation and review process

 *Suggested Fix:*

* Implement conditional logic to block SOW updates when user response is negative
* Preserve the previous version of the SOW until explicit approval is given
* Optionally, prompt the user with follow-up options (e.g., “Would you like to revise the changes instead?”)

*Environment:* SOW AI Chat Panel (Windows 11)

 *Issue Summary:*

The AI is incorrectly responding to Scope of Work (SOW) prompts by requesting quantity data (e.g., number of doors/windows) instead of generating the expected content sections. This behavior disrupts workflow and contradicts prompt intent.

 *Affected Prompts & Expected Behavior:*

# *Prompt:*
_“Mention inspection checkpoints for quality assurance during the repair process.”_

*  *Expected Behavior:*
AI should list relevant QA checkpoints such as:
** Pre-repair structural assessment
** Mid-repair alignment and sealing checks
** Post-repair functionality testing
** Final client walkthrough and sign-off
*  *Actual Behavior:*
AI responds by asking for the number of doors/windows instead of listing QA checkpoints.



# *Prompt:*
_“Mention client responsibilities such as clearing access areas and approving material choices.”_

*  *Expected Behavior:*
AI should generate a client responsibilities section including:
** Clearing furniture or obstructions near repair zones
** Providing access during scheduled work hours
** Reviewing and approving material selections
** Signing off on completed work
*  *Actual Behavior:*
AI asks for repair counts or repeats the prompt instead of generating the responsibilities section.

 *Impact:*

* Reduces efficiency in SOW drafting workflows
* Requires manual rephrasing or clarification
* Breaks expected prompt-to-output logic

 *Suggested Fix:*

* Improve prompt parsing to distinguish between *instructional prompts* vs. *data-gathering prompts*
* Default to generating content when prompt includes action verbs like “mention,” “outline,” or “list”
* Assume reasonable defaults when quantity is not explicitly requested

column1: AI Response Editable by User in Chat Panel
column31:
*Summary* 
*Environment:* SOW Module – Chat Panel Interface
*Module:* Client Scope of Work via AI
*Precondition:* User is authenticated and has initiated a Scope of Work session

*Issue Summary:*

AI-generated responses within the Chat Panel are currently *editable by the user*, which violates expected behavior and risks compromising the integrity of system-generated content.

 *Steps to Reproduce:*

# Navigate to the Scope of Work module
# Click *Create → Client Scope of Work*
# Initiate a session using *Client Scope using AI*
# Observe the AI-generated messages in the Chat Panel
# Attempt to click or edit the AI response text

 *Expected Behavior:*

* AI responses should be *read-only* for users
* Only user-generated prompts should be editable or revisable
* System-generated content must remain locked to preserve auditability and trust

 *Actual Behavior:*

* AI responses appear editable in the Chat Panel
* Users can modify or overwrite system-generated content
* No visual distinction or lock state is applied to AI messages

 *Impact:*

* Breaks UI/UX expectations for chat-based systems
* Risks miscommunication or misrepresentation of AI-generated Scope of Work content
* Compromises traceability and version control in collaborative environments

 *Suggested Fix:*

* Apply a *read-only state* to all AI-generated messages in the Chat Panel
* Visually distinguish AI responses from user prompts (e.g., shaded background, lock icon)
* Prevent cursor focus or text selection on AI messages

The chat input field remains active and editable while the AI assistant is generating a response. This allows users to submit overlapping prompts, which can lead to confusion, race conditions, or broken conversational flow.

 *Steps to Reproduce*

# Navigate to the SOW creation interface.
# Initiate a Scope of Work session using AI.
# Enter a prompt and submit it.
# While the AI is processing, observe that the chat input field remains enabled.

* A visual indicator (e.g., spinner, “AI is thinking…” message) should be shown.
* Field should re-enable only after the AI response is fully rendered.

*Actual Behavior*

* Input field remains active during AI processing.
* Users can submit multiple prompts but it is not displayed on the chat panel
* No visual cue indicating that the system is busy.



📉 *Impact*

* Breaks conversational UX expectations.
* Risks duplicate or conflicting requests.
* Reduces clarity and trust in AI response flow.
* May cause backend strain or unintended behavior.



🔧 *Suggested Fix*

* Apply a temporary {{disabled}} state to the chat input field during AI response generation.
* Add a loading spinner or status message to indicate processing.
* Re-enable input only after the response is complete.
* Optionally queue additional user prompts if entered during processing.

*Summary:*
When searching for a file name (e.g., "pool") in the {{POOL_CONNEXUS_LIBRARY}} → Updated History section, the system returns all files instead of filtering by file name. This occurs because the search logic incorrectly includes service metadata (e.g., "pool" as a service) in its matching criteria.

*Environment:*

* *Module:* Document Library – Updated History
* *Search Field:* Top-right search bar

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Navigate to the {{POOL_CONNEXUS_LIBRARY}} Updated History view.
# Enter the keyword "pool" in the search bar.
# Observe the returned results.
