column1: SSO Signup from Vendor registeration page
column31:
User story : 

As a vendor user I want to register my company and use SSO or standard login to login to the connexus applciation

*Acceptance Criteria*

h4. 1. Vendor Registration Page (No Email Field)

* The registration page *must not display an email field*.
* User must be able to fill all required vendor details (Company, Services, Address, State, City, Contact Person, etc.).
* Mandatory fields should show inline validation if left empty.
* User must be able to click the next button from the form only after filling all required fields.

h3. *2. Post-Registration Dialog Box*

After the vendor clicks Next:

* System must display a dialog with the following options:
** *Sign up via Standard Login*
** *Google SSO*
** *Microsoft SSO*
* The dialog must appear immediately after successful form submission.
* If the user closes the dialog, they must still be able to reopen it until they choose an option.

h2. *3. Google SSO Flow*

* When user selects *Google Signup*:
** User must be redirected to Google authentication.
** On successful Google authentication:
*** User is redirected to *Connexus Login Page*.
*** If their account is configured for SSO:
**** Login using Google should be successful.
** Vendor should be added to the connexus application with an active status
** If the google authentication failed then the vendor should be soft deleted and will not be visible in the systems

h3. *4. Microsoft SSO Flow*

* When user selects *Microsoft Signup*:
** User must be redirected to Microsoft authentication.
** On successful authentication:
*** User is redirected to Connexus Login Page.
*** If the user is SSO-enabled:
**** Login via Microsoft succeeds.
*** If not enabled:
**** Show the same masked validation message as above.

h3. *5. Standard Login (Non-SSO) Flow*

* If user selects *Standard Login*:
** It should open the dialog box for entering the email address
** System must send an *invitation email* to the user’s email id 
** Email contains a *Reset Password link*.
** Clicking the link opens a page to create/set a new password.
** SSO options must *not* be enabled for this user.

h3. *6. Reset Password Behavior*

h3. *6.1 If the user is already logged in*

* Clicking the “Reset Password” link:
** Should open the application.
** User must be redirected to the *Profile → Reset Password Dialog*.
** On click on reset password it should send the reset password email and user should navigate tothe reset page and should able to reset the password. After reset a confirmation message should be shown as “Password reset successfull!! please login again “

h3. *6.2 If the user is logged out*

* Clicking the “Reset Password” link:
** Should take the user to the *public Reset Password page*.
** User sets a new password and is redirected to the login page for authentication.

h3. *7. Security & Validation*

* Reset password link must expire after a defined validity period.
* If link is expired or already used:
** Show a generic masked message like: _“This link is no longer valid. Please request a new one.”_
* Password must meet the system’s configured password policy.
* No sensitive user-related information should be revealed in any error messages.

h3. *8. Success Conditions*

* Vendor record is created successfully after form submission.
* User must be able to authenticate based on the option chosen:
** Google SSO
** Microsoft SSO
** Standard Login (Username + Password)
* User must be able to reset password from the profile page.

column1: Order sequence field UI does not align with user story and creates confusing user interaction
column31:
h3. *Summary:*

The user story clearly states that the system should *“Add recipients in ordered sequence.”*
However, the current UI implementation of the sequence field does *not meet user expectations*:

* The sequence number is displayed *inside a text input–styled box*, implying that it is editable.
* The cursor appears when clicked, giving the impression that the field is *typable*, but typing is disabled.
* The field is *not editable*, yet it looks like an editable input field rather than a static sequence indicator.

This creates confusion and negatively impacts user experience.

----

h3. *User Story Reference (Highest Priority):*

{quote}*Add recipients in ordered sequence*{quote}

This implies a clear, intuitive, non-confusing ordering mechanism.

----

h3. *Steps to Reproduce:*

# Navigate to  *Send for Signatures*.
# Scroll down to the *Add Recipients* section.
# Observe the *Order* column.
# Click on the number displayed (e.g., 1, 2).
# Notice that a text cursor appears but typing is not permitted.

----

h3. *Expected Result (Based on User Story):*

* The order should be shown as a *non-editable sequence indicator*.
* It should not appear as an input box.
* For drag-and-drop ordering:
** Only the drag handle should be interactive.
** The sequence number should auto-update without attempt to manually type.

*In short:*
The field must look and behave like a proper _static order indicator_, not an input box.

----

h3. *Actual Result:*

* A *box resembling a text input field* is shown around the sequence number.
* Clicking the box displays a *text cursor*, misleading the user to think it’s editable.
* Typing does nothing, causing confusion.
* This results in *poor usability and deviation from the intended “ordered sequence” experience*.

----

h3. *Impact:*

* Misleads users into thinking they can manually edit the sequence.
* Causes confusion and interrupts workflow.
* Does not reflect the clarity expected from the user story.
* Increases likelihood of usability complaints.

column1: System Notification UI & FE integration
column31:
User story: 

*As a* user
*I want to* view all my notifications in one place and perform actions.
*So that* I can quickly understand what requires my attention.

h2. *1. Notification Listing*

* The system must display a list of notifications grouped by category (e.g., General, Client Notifications).
* Each notification must show:
** *Title*
** *Subtitle/Description (Lorem Ipsum placeholder in design)*
** *Timestamp (e.g., “5 min ago”)*
** *Status tag* (e.g., “3 Days Remaining”, “Due in 4 days”, “Submitted Bid”, “RFP Closed”)
** *Action buttons* depending on notification type:
*** _RFP_: *Accept*, *Decline*, *View*
*** _Other notifications_: *View*
** A *close/dismiss (X)* icon to remove a notification from the list.

h2. *2. Filtering by Category*

* A *Select Category* dropdown must be available at the top-left.
* Dropdown options must include:
** *All Category*
** *Client*
** *Vendor*
** *RFP*
* User can select one or multiple categories using checkboxes.
* On selecting a category, the notification list must refresh to show only notifications belonging to the selected categories.
* “All Category” must show *all notifications* irrespective of type.

h2. *3. Search Functionality*

* A search bar must be available at the top-right.
* Users must be able to search notifications by:
** Title
** Description
** Status tag
* The results should update in real-time as the user types.

h2. *4. Read / Unread Toggle*

* Two toggle buttons: *Read* and *Unread*.
* Default state: Show *all* notifications.
* Selecting:
** *Read* → Show only read notifications.
** *Unread* → Show only unread notifications.
* Unread notifications should be visually distinct (e.g., bold text or background highlight).

h2. *5. Sorting*

* A sorting icon must be present (as shown in the design).
* Sorting options must include:
** *Newest First* (default)
** *Oldest First*
** *Due Date – Soonest First* (where applicable)
* The list must reorder based on the selected sort order.

h2. *6. Notification Actions*

h3. *Accept / Decline*

* Only RFP-related notifications display *Accept* and *Decline* buttons.
* On clicking Accept:
** Notification status updates to “Accepted”.
** Notification record should be removed after the action
* On clicking Decline:
** Notification status updates to “Declined”.
** Notification record should be removed after the action 

h3. *View*

* Clicking *View* opens the corresponding RFP page
* The notification must be marked as *Read* after viewing.

h3. *Dismiss (X)*

* Clicking the close icon removes the notification from the visible list.
* It should have bulk delete optiong and should be placed right corner of the table [~accountid:63c8e40fd579d7c687552750] {color:#ff5630}*currently bulk delete not implemented*{color}

h2. *7. Notification Count Badge* [~accountid:63c8e40fd579d7c687552750] {color:#0747a6}As discussed, currently the system displays the Unread count (right end of Unread) and the total count (Right end of Notifications Heading){color}

* The top-left header must show the number of unread notifications (e.g., *12*).
* Count must update dynamically when:
** Notifications are read
** Notifications are dismissed
** New notifications arrive

h2. *8. "View All" Links*  [~accountid:63c8e40fd579d7c687552750] {color:#ff5630}Currently this is not implemented{color}

* “View All” shown on the right of each category section must navigate to:
** A full-screen view showing *all notifications under that group*.
* The list must respect active filters (category, search, read/unread, sort).

h2. *9. UI/Design Consistency*

* Screen must match the spacing, font styles, colors, and layout provided in the Figma design.
* Status tags must follow color logic:
** Yellow → Remaining days
** Red → Due soon / overdue
** Blue → Submitted or info
* Buttons must match the design (Primary: Accept, Secondary: View, Danger: Decline).

h2. WorkFlow: 

* When user accepts the screen notifcation, it should expire the mail notification and vice versa
* When user declines the screen notifcation, it should expire the mail notification and vice versa

column1: Suggestion: Enable Simultaneous Contract Email Delivery to All Vendors
column31:
h3. *Current Behavior*

The system sends contract emails to vendors *one at a time*, based on the recipient order. Vendor 2 receives the contract email *only after* Vendor 1 signs, and so on.

h3. *Issue*

This sequential workflow causes delays and slows down the overall contract signing process, especially when multiple vendors are involved.

h3. *Suggested Improvement*

Modify the contract email workflow so that *all vendors receive the contract email simultaneously* once the user initiates the send action.

h3. *Expected Benefits*

* Faster contract turnaround time
* Improved user experience
* No dependency on the signing sequence
* More efficient multi-vendor contract handling

column1: System Not Blocking Duplicate File Uploads in Contract Templates
column31:
*Module:* Connexus E-Sign → Contract Templates
*Page:* Contract Template Upload
*Type:* Functional Bug
*Environment:* Test Environment

----

h2. *Summary*

The system allows users to upload *duplicate contract template files* (same file name and file type).
There is *no validation* to prevent duplicate uploads, resulting in multiple identical templates appearing in the list.

----

h2. *Steps to Reproduce*

# Log in to Connexus.
# Navigate to *Connexus E-Sign → Contract Templates*.
# Click *Upload Template*.
# Choose a file that already exists in the template list (e.g., {{Landscape_Service_Contract.docx}}).
# Upload the file.
# Repeat the upload with the same file again.

----

h2. *Actual Result*

* System *allows the same file* to be uploaded multiple times.
* The template list shows *duplicate entries with the same file name, type, and size*.
* No error or warning message is displayed.

----

h2. *Expected Result*

* System should *block duplicate uploads*.
* If a file with the same name already exists, show a message such as:
*“A template with this file name already exists. Please rename the file or upload a different template.”*

----

h2. *Impact*

* Confusing for users managing templates.
* Leads to unnecessary storage usage.
* Causes duplication in selection lists during contract creation.
* Reduces data quality and increases the chance of selecting the wrong template.

----

h2. *Suggested Fix (For Dev Team)*

* Add backend validation for *duplicate file name check* (case-insensitive).
* Add frontend validation to prevent users from selecting already uploaded names.
* Show a clear validation message.

h3. *Observation:*

The Audit page is currently displaying as shown. During requirement and design review, *no detailed requirement or UI design specifications were found for this Audit page*, which means the expected formatting and data presentation standards are not clearly defined. Most fields on the Audit page — especially in the *Settings* and *Meta* columns — are displaying *raw coded structures / JSON-like objects* rather than properly formatted, readable values.
This reduces clarity and does not align with standard UI/UX expectations for audit logs.

When clicking the *Download* button at the bottom of the Audit page, the system downloads the audit log as a plain {{.txt}} file containing *raw technical JSON and backend values*.
There is *no formatting*, making it difficult for users to read or analyze.

Expected behavior:

h2. *Summary*

Both *Documents in Process* and *Sign Management* tabs under the *Connexus E-Sign module* are failing to load data. When navigating to either page, the UI displays an HTTP 500 server error and the grids remain empty. This issue prevents users from viewing or managing ongoing or pending e-signature documents.

----

# *Sign Management*
# *Documents in Process*

----

h3. *For Sign Management*

# Go to *Connexus E-Sign* in the left menu.
# Click *Sign Management* tab.
# Page attempts to load sign requests.
# Error message appears:
#* _“Error loading contracts – HTTP 500”_
#* Toast notification: _“Error – HTTP 500”_

h3. *For Documents in Process*

# Go to *Connexus E-Sign*.
# Click *Documents in Process* tab.
# API call fails.
# Error message appears:
#* _“Failed to load: HTTP 500”_
#* Empty grid with no records.

h2. *Actual Result*

* Both tabs show *HTTP 500 server errors*.
* No data is displayed in the grids.
* Toast notification shows _“Error – HTTP 500”_.
* Filters and search also remain disabled since no data is loaded.

----

h2. *Expected Result*

* Both pages should successfully fetch and display e-sign document records.
* No server errors should be triggered.
* Filters, search, and download should be available once data loads.

----

h2. *Impact*

* Users cannot view any *pending, ongoing, or completed sign requests*.
* The *E-Sign workflow is completely blocked*.
* Affects contract sending, tracking, and document status management.

column1: Save Draft button is non-functional on both Actual Contract Generation page and Send for Signature page
column31:
h2. *Summary:*

The *Save Draft* button does not perform any action when clicked.
This issue occurs on:

# *Actual Contract Generate Page* (after selecting the contract template )
# *Send for Signature Page* (during recipient assignment and field mapping)

The system gives *no response*, *no loading state*, and *no draft is saved*.

----

h2. *Steps to Reproduce:*

h3. *Scenario 1: Actual Contract Generate Page*

# Navigate to an awarded RFP detail page.
# Click *Generate Contract*.
# Select Template
# Update the actual contract.
# Click *Save Draft*.
# Observe that nothing happens.

h3. *Scenario 2: Send for Signature Page*

# Open any contract template and proceed to the *Send for Signature* screen.
# Add recipients.
# Click *Save Draft* at the bottom.
# No action occurs.

----

h2. *Actual Result:*

* Save Draft button is *not working* in both pages.
* No draft is saved.
* No confirmation, error, or UI feedback.
* Button appears clickable but performs *no action*.

----

h2. *Expected Result:*

* Clicking *Save Draft* should save the current contract in a draft state.
* System should display a success message such as:
*“Draft saved successfully.”*
* Draft should appear under:
** _Documents in Process_, or
** Relevant Drafts section (based on system design).

----

h2. *Impact:*

* Users cannot save progress while preparing or editing a contract.
* Work is lost if the user navigates away .

h2.

*Expected Result:*

* DOCX files should upload successfully, and the system should convert them to PDF without errors.
* File type handling should be consistent with the *RFP module*, where only *DOC* and *DOCX* formats are allowed.

*Additional Note on Consistency:*
In the *RFP module*, the system restricts uploads to *DOC* and *DOCX* formats. To ensure a consistent user experience and alignment across modules, the *eSign module* should enforce the same file format restrictions.

*Impact:*

* PDF should display clean, non-overlapping text.
* All columns should maintain proper spacing and alignment.
* Long text should wrap appropriately or be truncated with ellipsis.

----

h3. *Impact:*

Users cannot read or share exported PDF reports, affecting documentation, auditing, and communication with stakeholders.

*Page:* Sign Management → Document Preview Modal

*Issue:*

column1: Clarify Expected Workflow for ZIP File Upload in Sign Management
column31:
*Description:*
The Sign Management → Upload Contracts popup currently allows uploading *PDF, DOC/DOCX, and ZIP* files. However, the expected system behavior when a *ZIP file* is uploaded is not defined.
A clarification is required to understand how the system should process ZIP uploads.

*Points to Clarify:*

# Should the system *automatically extract* the ZIP file upon upload?
# If extraction is required, should the system:
#* Extract *all files*, or
#* Extract only *supported formats* (PDF, DOC, DOCX)?
# Should the system *create multiple contract entries*, one for each extracted file?
# If multiple files exist in the ZIP, should the system allow the *user to select* which document to proceed with first for signature?
# Are there any *restrictions* on ZIP content (e.g., only one document allowed, naming requirements, unsupported file types inside ZIP, etc.)?

*Expected Outcome:*
A confirmed workflow definition so QA can validate correct system behavior

h3. 1. Automatic extraction

Yes. ZIP files are automatically extracted during upload.

h3. 2. What gets extracted

Only supported formats:

* PDF files (preferred — used directly)

* DOCX files (converted to PDF)

h3. 3. Multiple files handling

* Only the first file is used:

* If multiple PDFs exist → uses the first PDF

* If no PDFs but DOCX exists → uses the first DOCX

column1: property insurance module email template integration
column31:
*User Story*

*Title:* Automated compliance status management and notification triggers

*As a* Compliance/System Administrator
*I want* the system to automatically update record compliance statuses based on end dates and manual updates
*So that* records always reflect their correct compliance state and the right email notifications are sent at the right time without manual intervention.

h2. Business Rules Summary 

h2. Statuses supported:

* Non-Compliant (default)
* Compliant
* Expiring
* Expired
* Deficient

*Email notifications:*

* Compliant (one-time)
* Expiring (30 days before end date)
* Expiring (15 days before end date)
* Deficient (when a non-compliant record expires)

h2. Acceptance Criteria

h3. 1. Default Status on Record Creation

*Given* a new record is created
*When* no manual status is set
*Then* the system shall set the record status to *Non-Compliant*
*And* no email shall be triggered at this time.

h3. 2. Non-Compliant Record Passing End Date

*Given* a record is in *Non-Compliant* status
*And* the current date is later than the record end date
*When* the system evaluates record status
*Then* the record status shall automatically change to *Deficient*
*And* a *Deficient email notification* shall be triggered once.

h3. 3. Manual -or Automatic- Change to Compliant

*Given* a record is in *Non-Compliant* status
*When* the record status is changed to *Compliant* (manually )
*Then* the system shall trigger a *Compliant email notification*
*And* the compliant email shall be sent *only once per compliant transition*


h3. 4. Compliant Record Passing End Date

*Given* a record is in *Compliant* status
*And* the current date is later than the record end date
*When* the system evaluates record status
*Then* the record status shall automatically change to *Expired*
*And* no deficient email shall be triggered.

h3. 5. Expiring Status – 30 Days Before End Date

*Given* a record is in *Compliant* or *Non-Compliant* status
*And* the current date is exactly 30 days before the record end date
*When* the system evaluates record status
*Then* the system shall mark the record as *Expiring*
*And* a *30-day Expiry Reminder email* shall be triggered once.

h3. 6. Expiring Status – 15 Days Before End Date

*Given* a record is in *Compliant* or *Non-Compliant* status
*And* the current date is exactly 15 days before the record end date
*When* the system evaluates record status
*Then* the record shall remain *Expiring*
*And* a *15-day Expiry Reminder email* shall be triggered once.

h3. 7. No Duplicate Expiry Notifications

*Given* an expiry reminder email (30-day or 15-day) has already been sent
*When* the system re-evaluates the record on the same day
*Then* the system shall not send duplicate expiry reminder emails.

h3. 8. Status Priority Rules

*Given* multiple conditions could apply at the same time
*When* the system determines the record status
*Then* the following priority order shall apply:

# Deficient (Non-Compliant + End Date Passed)
# Expired (Compliant + End Date Passed)
# Expiring (15 or 30 days before end date)
# Compliant
# Non-Compliant

h3. 9. Automated Evaluation

*Given* records exist in the system
*When* the scheduled status evaluation job runs (daily or configured interval)
*Then* all records shall be evaluated against the defined rules
*And* statuses and email notifications shall be updated accordingly.



PF the email template : 

[https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1xEaFNgwma62-9wQjyPs9y9ol4ssFJONhbGypmzz8g10/edit?gid=0#gid=0|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1xEaFNgwma62-9wQjyPs9y9ol4ssFJONhbGypmzz8g10/edit?gid=0#gid=0|smart-link] 

Status Trigger : 

|By default all the records status will be updated as Non- compliant|
|if the non compliant record is expired(passed the end date ), status should default to deficient and should trigger the email|
|if the record is compliant or manually changed from non-compliant to compliant, system should trigger email for compliant (one time)|
|If the record is compliant and record end date is passed then it should change the status to expired.|
|If the record is either compliant or non- compliant and it is about to expire, it should trigger email for 30 days and 15 days|

!image-20251217-063935.png|width=927,alt="image-20251217-063935.png"!


As per the current workflow, In the contract *edit/preview page*, the *Service* dropdown supports *only single selection*. However, some contracts created through *AI extraction* contain *multiple services*.

Because of this limitation:

* Only the *first service* is shown in the Service field.
* Other services already linked to the contract (like _Software > Procurement_) do *not appear in the dropdown search*, as the system treats them as already selected.
* This happens for both *single-service and multi-service* contracts.

*Update:*

We have updated the behavior so that the *Service* dropdown now lists all available services *except the one currently displayed* on the contract edit/preview page. This allows users to view and select other applicable services without the dropdown appearing empty or incomplete.
*Note:* If the user selects a different service and saves the update, the system will display *the newly selected service along with all other services*, except the one that was removed.

column1: Pending Insurance Tab : Upload file
column31:
*Acceptance criteria:* 

h3. *1. File Upload (Pending Insurance Tab)*

h3. *1.1 Upload Modal Display*

* When the user clicks *Upload File*, an upload modal should appear displaying required fields.

h3. *1.2 Field Visibility Based on User Type*

* *If the logged-in user is a Connexus user:*
** The modal must display:
*** _File Name_ (text field)
*** _Client Name_ (dropdown) : All Active clients should be displayed
*** _File Upload_ area : 
* *If the user is not a Connexus user:*
** The modal must display only:
*** _File Name_ (text field)
*** _File Upload_ area : it should allow both doc and pdf
** The _Client Name_ field must be hidden.

h3. *1.3 File Upload Validation*

* The system should allow uploading of *PDF or DOC* files only.
* The *Submit* button must remain disabled until all required fields are completed.
* On clicking *Submit*, the file must be successfully uploaded and a confirmation toast/modal should appear.
* {color:#97a0af}_Allow only one file upload_ {color}[~accountid:63c8e40fd579d7c687552750]{color:#97a0af} Could you please confirm this case?{color}

h2. *2. File Processing* 

h2. *2.1 Automatic Processing*

* After submission, the system must automatically trigger:
** *OCR extraction*
** *AI data processing*

h3. *2.2 Status Display*

* The file must appear in the *Pending Insurance* tab with:
** File name
** Uploaded date
** Status : 
 *Processing* (If the file is still in Processing),*Pending* (system needs manual intervanetion to complete the process especially for selecting the properties. It shoud be allowed for all the client users.,*Pending from Connexus* (If the file is not able to extract and AI fails to recogonize then by default it should fail and status should change to pending ocnnexus. when connexus user logs in they should able to view the logs and error messages. ))
** Property column : property column should display the properties they mapped to this property. 

h3. *2.3 Completion Handling*

* Once processing is complete:
** Status should update to *Property Selection Required*.

h2. *3. Property Selection*

h3. *3.1 Property Mapping Screen*

* When the user clicks a pending file, a property selection screen must appear.
* The screen should show:
** *Properties found from extracted text* (left section)
** *Suggested properties* by AI (right section)
** A *search field* to manually find additional properties.
** It should list only Active properties

h3. *3.2 Selection Logic*

* Users must select *one* property from the suggestions or search results.
* The *Next* button should remain disabled until one property is selected.

h3. *3.3 Confirmation*

* After selection and clicking *Next*, a success message should appear:
** “Property Uploaded Successfully”

h2. *4. Insurance Tab Population*

h3. *4.1 Data Movement*

* After property selection, the processed file record must:
** Move from *Pending Insurance* tab → *Property Insurance* tab.
** Be removed from the Pending list.

h3. *4.2 Table Display*

* In the *Property Insurance* tab, the file data should display in table format.
* All extracted fields must appear as separate columns, including:
** File name
** Property name
** Client name
** Effective date
** End date
** Coverage values
** Any other AI-extracted fields

h3. *4.3 Sorting and Filters*

* Columns should support sorting.
* Filters must be available to narrow down results.

h2. *5. System Checks (if applicable later)*

_(Optional for this release but included per workflow description)_

* System should flag insurance records as *Expired* if the end date is older than the current date.
* System should mark whether the *Client is insured or not*, based on extracted data.

column1: Suggestion: Improve First Mail and Reminder Email Content for Clarity and Better Deadline Messaging
column31:
h3. *Suggestion Summary:*

The existing reminder email sent to clients/vendors every two days for pending signatures is not clearly communicating its intention. The wording can be improved to better highlight that the user still needs to sign a document. Additionally, although the email includes the validity period in UTC, the current phrasing is not intuitive for recipients.

This suggestion is to enhance the email content for better clarity, user experience, and higher signature completion rates.

----

h3. *Current Gaps Identified:*

* The email does not explicitly convey that it is a reminder to sign a pending document.
* The urgency and purpose of the email are not clearly communicated.
* The UTC deadline is present but not user-friendly or easy to understand.
* The call-to-action link could be more clear and visually emphasized.

----

h3. *Suggested Enhancements:*

# Rewrite the email content using more intuitive and user-friendly language.
# Improve the UTC deadline message using clearer phrasing, such as:
#* “Please complete your signature by {{DueDateUTC}} UTC.”
#* “This signing link is valid until {{DueDateUTC}} UTC.”
# Include the improved validity/expiry line in *all  emails*.
# Clearly inform the recipient why they are receiving the email.
# Add a stronger, simpler call-to-action for signing the document.

----

h3. *Proposed Updated Reminder Email Format (for Implementation):*

*Subject:*
*Reminder: Your Signature Is Needed for Document #{{DocumentNamer}}*

*Body:*
Hello {{UserName}},

This is a friendly reminder that your signature is required for Document #{{DocumentName}}.

Please complete the signing process at your earliest convenience to avoid any delays.

*Due Date:*
This signing link is valid until *{{DueDateUTC}}* UTC.

 *Open Signing Page (button)*

If the button doesn’t work, please copy and paste this link into your browser:
{{SignURL}}

Thank you,
*Connexus Sign*

----

h3. *Proposed Updated Email Format (for Implementation):*

*Subject:*
*Your Signature Is Requested for Document #{{DocumentName}}*

*Body:*
Hello {{UserName}},

You have been requested to review and sign *Document #{{DocumentName}}*.
Please complete the signing process to move forward without delays.

*Due Date:*
This signing link is valid until *{{DueDateUTC}}* UTC.

👉 *Open Signing Page*

If the button doesn’t work, you can copy and paste this link into your browser:
{{SignURL}}

Thank you,
*Connexus Sign*

----

h3. *Expected Outcome:*

* Clearer communication and purpose
* Improved understanding of the deadline in UTC
* Better user experience

column1: Incorrect Email Heading for Approver (Client) – Shows Signature Request Instead of Approval Request
column31:
*Description:*
When the Client acts as an *Approver*, they are not assigned any signature fields in the document. After the approval step is completed, the system sends an email to the Approver.
However, the *email heading/subject incorrectly displays a “Signature Request” message*, which does not match the actual action required from the Client.
This creates confusion because the Client is only required to *approve*, not *sign*.

----

h3. *Steps to Reproduce:*

# Send a contract  where the *Client* is assigned the role of *Approver* (no signature fields).
# Check the email subject and heading received by the Client.
# Observe the incorrect wording indicating a signature request.

----

h3. *Expected Result:*

* The email sent to the Approver Client should clearly indicate that the document requires *approval*, not a signature.
* Email heading/subject should display something like *“Your Approval Is Requested for Document #Document Name”*

----

h3. *Actual Result:*

* Email heading shows *“Your Signature Is Requested”*, even though the Client has *no signature field* and only needs to approve.
* The message does not correctly convey the required action.

----

h3. *Impact:*

* Causes confusion for Clients regarding what action is needed.
* Reduces clarity and accuracy of the e-sign workflow communication.
* May result in delays if users misunderstand the purpose of the email.

----

column1: Bid Submission Email Not Received by RFP Creator (both authorised and unauthorised)
column31:
*Summary*
Bid submission notification email is not received by the RFP Creator after a vendor submits a bid.

*Description*
When a vendor successfully submits a bid for an RFP, the system is expected to send a notification email to the RFP Creator. However, the RFP Creator does not receive any email confirmation or notification after the bid submission.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Log in as a Vendor.
# Open an active RFP.
# Submit a bid successfully.
# Check the RFP Creator’s email inbox.

*Expected Result*
An email notification should be sent to the RFP Creator confirming that a vendor has submitted a bid.

*Actual Result*
No bid submission email is received by the RFP Creator.

*Note*
✔️ Bid submission *thank-you email is successfully received by the Vendor*.

!image-20251224-103700.png|width=666,alt="image-20251224-103700.png"!



*Impact*
The RFP Creator may be unaware of new bid submissions, leading to delays in review and evaluation.

*Environment*

* Environment: Test 
* Module: RFP → Bid Submission → Email Notification

** An *email notification* is sent to the *RFP Creator* and *Property Manager*.
** A *system notification* is generated and visible in their respective accounts.
* Notification content should clearly indicate that the *RFP due date has passed*.
* Notifications should be triggered *only once per RFP*.

column1: Primary Vendor Contacts Not Receiving Email Notification on RFP Closure
column31:
*Summary* 

When an RFP is closed, email notifications are not sent to all primary contacts of the vendor. Only the primary contacts who have submitted a bid receive the closure notification, while other primary contacts linked to the same vendor do not receive any email, despite being marked as *Primary*.



*Steps To Replicate*

* Create an RFP and invite a vendor that has multiple contacts marked as *Primary*.
* Submit a bid using one of the primary contacts.
* Close the RFP.
* Check the email inboxes of all primary contacts for the vendor.



*Expected Result:* 

All primary contacts associated with the vendor should receive the RFP closure email notification, regardless of whether they submitted a bid.

*Actual Result*

Only the primary contact(s) who submitted the bid receive the RFP closure email. Other primary contacts do not receive any notification.

*Summary* 

When a vendor has already been invited for a client, the same vendor can still be selected again from the Existing Vendors list during the Invite Vendor workflow.

*Steps to Replicate:*

# Log in to the application.
# Invite an existing vendor successfully.

# Observe the system behavior.

The system allows the already invited vendor to be selected again without any restriction or validation message.

column1: Replace Generic “Invalid or Expired Token” Message with Status-Specific RFP Messages
column31:
h2. *Description*

Currently, when a user clicks *Accept* or *Decline* on an RFP email link after the action has already been completed or when the link is expired, the system displays a generic message:

{quote}*Invalid or expired token!*
Failed to accept vendor response. Please try again.{quote}

This message is unclear and does not reflect the actual RFP status, causing confusion for vendors.

----

h2. *Proposed Content Changes*

h3. *1. Already Accepted RFP*

*Header:*
RFP Already Accepted

*Message:*
This RFP has already been accepted using this link.
If you wish to review details, please log in to your account.

----

h3. *2. Already Rejected RFP*

*Header:*
RFP Already Rejected

*Message:*
This RFP has already been rejected.
No further action is required.

----

h3. *3. Expired Link*

*Header:*
Link Expired

*Message:*
This link has expired and can no longer be used.
Please log in to your account to view or respond to the RFP.

----

h2. *Scope*

* Replace the existing *“Invalid or expired token”* message.
* Display the appropriate message based on:
** RFP already accepted
** RFP already rejected
** RFP link expired
* Applies to both *Accept* and *Decline* actions triggered via email links.

----

h2. *Acceptance Criteria*

* System identifies the correct RFP state before rendering the message.
* Correct header and message are displayed based on status.
* No further action is allowed via the email link once the RFP is accepted or rejected.
* *Back to Login* button remains functional and redirects correctly.
* Messaging matches the provided content exactly.

column1: Deactivate functionality in Existing contracts along with hidden and active filter
column31:
*User Story*

*As a* Contract Management user
*I want* the ability to deactivate existing contracts
*So that* inactive or no-longer-relevant contracts are hidden from the default contract view while still being retrievable and manageable when required.

*Acceptance Criteria*

h3. 1. Deactivate Action Availability

* A *Deactivate* action button shall be available for existing contracts in Contract Management.
* The Deactivate action shall be accessible based on user permissions.
* On clicking *Deactivate*, the system shall update the *Contract Status* to *Deactivated*.

h3. 2. Contract Status Update

* When a contract is deactivated:
** The *Contract Status* column shall display *Deactivated*.
** The status update shall be saved successfully without data loss.

h3. 3. Visibility in Existing Contracts Tab

* Deactivated contracts *shall not be visible* in the *Existing Contracts* tab by default.
* Deactivated contracts shall be *hidden* unless explicitly retrieved using filters.

h3. 4. Filter Behavior – Contract Status

* The *Contract Status* filter shall include *Deactivated* as an option.
* When the *Deactivated* filter is applied:
** Deactivated contracts shall be visible in the contract list.
* When the filter is cleared:
** Deactivated contracts shall remain hidden from the Existing Contracts tab.

h3. 5. Editing Deactivated Contracts

* Users shall be able to *open and edit* a deactivated contract.
* Users shall be able to change the contract status from *Deactivated* to any other valid status (e.g., Current, Future, Expired, etc.).

h3. 6. Reactivation Behavior

* When a deactivated contract’s status is changed to any status other than *Deactivated*:
** The contract shall reappear in the *Existing Contracts* tab.
** The contract shall follow standard visibility and filtering rules based on the new status.

h3. 7. Data Integrity & Audit

* Deactivating a contract shall not delete the contract data.
* All historical data and associations (documents, vendors, properties) shall remain intact after deactivation.

column1: RFP Actions Show Error After Accepting from Vendor/Branch Notifications
column31:
*Description:*
When a vendor accepts an RFP from the *vendor-level Notifications*, the same RFP in the *vendor’s branch Notifications* is automatically marked as read. However, the *Accept* and *Decline* actions are still enabled, and clicking them throws an error stating that the RFP is already accepted or declined.

The same issue occurs in reverse. If the vendor logs into a *branch account* and accepts the RFP from the *branch Notifications*, the same RFP in the *vendor-level Notifications* is marked as read, and the *Accept/Decline* actions throw an error indicating the RFP has already been accepted or declined.

*Steps to Reproduce (Vendor → Branch):*

# Log in as a Vendor user.
# Open Notifications and accept an RFP.
# Open Notifications for the same RFP.
# Click *Accept* or *Decline*.

*Steps to Reproduce (Branch → Vendor):*

# Log in to a Vendor Branch account.
# Open Notifications and accept an RFP.
# Open Notifications for the same RFP.
# Click *Accept* or *Decline*.

*Actual Result:*

* The RFP is marked as read in both Vendor and Branch Notifications.
* *Accept* and *Decline* actions are still visible and clickable.
* Clicking these actions shows an error message stating the RFP is already accepted or declined.

*Expected Result:* [~accountid:62146cb42d057500723ebae2] [~accountid:61e900cef0ed0400689392d4] 

* Once an RFP is accepted or declined from either the *Vendor* or a *specific Branch*, the action should apply *only to that respective entity* (Vendor or individual Branch).
* The RFP for a Vendor and its Branch should be treated as *separate and independent*.

** Days Remaining (e.g., _7 Days Remaining_)
** RFP Closed
** Due Soon / Due in X Days
* Users must open the RFP to understand its current status.

** *7 Days Remaining / Due in X Days*
** *RFP Closed*
** Other contextual RFP state indicators
* These tags should be updated dynamically based on the RFP state.

*Impact:*
Missing tags reduce visibility of important RFP status information and increase unnecessary navigation, impacting user experience.

*Priority:* Medium

column1: [TRELLO] Unable to Update Services in Existing Contracts
column31:
h3. Description

[https://trello.com/c/JghqrFB4|https://trello.com/c/JghqrFB4|smart-link]  [~accountid:63c8e40fd579d7c687552750] 

*(Update in point 6 below)* In the *Existing Contracts* section, users are unable to update or change services for certain contracts. Even after saving changes, the service either does not update or results in an error stating that a record for the property already exists. This issue is occurring with contracts that initially have multiple services assigned (e.g., AI-generated services).

----

h2. *Steps to Reproduce:*

# Go to *Contract Management*.
# Search for the property *Academy Apartments*.
# Open the *first contract* (the one showing multiple services due to AI).
# Attempt to change the service(s).
# Click *Update*.
#  
#* After multiple attempts, the service has  updated now (e.g., changes to *Access Control*).
#* Now When trying to change the service again (e.g., to *Landscape and Snow*), the system shows the error:
#*“A record with this property ID already exists.”*
#* So we needed resolution for initial issue and as it was intermittent, now we have 2 issues that need resolution.

----

----

h2. *Actual Result:*

* The service remains unchanged and shows the *previously selected service* in the list view after clicking Update.
* After multiple attempts, the service may partially update (e.g., changes to *Access Control*).
* When trying to change the service again (e.g., to *Landscape and Snow*), the system shows the error:
*“A record with this property ID already exists.”*

----

h2. *Expected Result:*

* Services in existing contracts should update correctly on the first attempt.
* Users should be able to reassign or change services without errors.
* The system should handle existing records gracefully without blocking valid updates.

column1: [TRELLO] Incorrect Email Content When RFP Status Is Set to “Close for Bids”
column31:
[https://trello.com/c/Hx4uI4LB|https://trello.com/c/Hx4uI4LB|smart-link] 

When the RFP status is updated to *“Close for Bids”* from the RFP level, the system sends an incorrect email notification to vendors.

*Issues Observed:*

# The email subject/content is sent as *“Update is made in RFP”* instead of indicating that the *RFP is closed for bids*.
# The email includes a *“View RFP”* button and message asking vendors to view updates made by the client.
# However, when *“Close for Bids”* is selected, there are *no actual updates* for vendors to view at the RFP level.
# This creates confusion, as the email suggests changes were made when none exist.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Go to an active RFP.
# Change the status to *“Close for Bids”* at the RFP level.
# Observe the email sent to vendors.

*Expected Behavior:*

* When the status is set to *“Close for Bids”*, the email should clearly indicate that the RFP is closed for bidding.
* The email should *not* prompt vendors to view updates if there are no updates available.
* Email behavior should be consistent with the *“Closed”* status, which currently works correctly.

*Actual Behavior:*

* Email is sent as an update notification instead of a status change notification.
* Email includes misleading messaging and a “View RFP” button when there is nothing new to view.

column1: [TRELLO] Add Common Identifier Between “File Upload” and “Existing Contracts” Tabs
column31:
[https://trello.com/c/KbVuTFT7|https://trello.com/c/KbVuTFT7|smart-link]

----

# Go to *Contract Management*.
# Upload a contract using the *File Upload* tab.
# Update the contract from pending to completed.
# The contract moves to the *Existing Contracts* tab.
# Attempt to track or identify the same contract between both tabs.

----

h2. *Expected Result:*

* There should be a *common field/identifier* (e.g., Contract ID, Upload Reference, or Source Tag) visible in both tabs.
* The team should be able to easily track a contract as it moves from File Upload to Existing Contracts.
* This will improve traceability and reduce confusion.

column1: Access to child companies from parent companies for the same account
column31:
*Problem:*
Currently, a parent company user needs to access child companies to perform operations within them. However, based on the existing architecture and earlier requirements, the system was designed such that a parent company user has *view-only access* to child companies.

Additionally, a parent company user cannot be added as a user in a child company because email addresses must be *unique across the entire system*.


*Solution:*

Implement a *multi-tenant membership model* that allows a single user to be associated with multiple companies (e.g., a parent company and one or more child companies). Each company will independently assign roles and permissions to the user, enabling different access levels per company as required.

User authorization will be determined by company membership and assigned roles, eliminating the need for special parent–child access rules.

*Key Considerations:*

* Roles and permissions will be managed independently within each company.
* User access audits and revocation must consider all company memberships.
* Clear governance is required to prevent incorrect role assignments across companies.

column1: Credential Storage Solution [DevOps]
column31:
Critical credentials are currently scattered or dependent on individual team members. When these individuals are unavailable, work is blocked, and auditability is weak.



h3. *Objective:*

Store all shared credentials securely in *AWS Secrets Manager* to enable:

* Team-wide controlled access
* Auditable credential usage
* Rotation and lifecycle management
* Removal of single-person dependency



h3. *Scope:*

* Database credentials (RDS, NoSQL, etc.)
* API keys / tokens / SSH keys
* Third-party service credentials
* ECS or other cloud workloads can fetch secrets securely



h3. *Acceptance Criteria:*

# All identified credentials migrated to AWS Secrets Manager
# Secrets encrypted using AWS KMS
# ECS task definitions (and other workloads) reference secrets via {{secrets}} *field*
# IAM roles configured for *least-privilege access*:
#* ECS tasks → required secrets only
#* Team members → read-only where justified
# Access is logged via *CloudTrail*
# Secret rotation implemented where possible (manual or automatic)
# Documentation created:
#* Where secrets are stored
#* How to access them
#* Access approval workflow
# Legacy credentials removed from:
#* Hardcoded source files
#* Environment variables

column1: Policy Status Auto-Assignment with Manual Override Support
column31:
h2.  Description

Implement *policy Status handling logic* during *Save* actions with support for *manual user selection*.

The system should *auto-assign Status based on End Date by default*, but *respect the user-selected Status if manually changed*.

----

h2. ✅ Requirements

h3. *1. Default System Logic (No Manual Change)*

When the user does *not manually change the Status field*:

* *End Date in the past* → Status = *Expired*
* *End Date today or future* → Status = *Non Compliant*

Applies to:

* New policy upload
* Edit & save existing policy

----

h3. *2. Manual Override Logic*

* If the user *explicitly selects a Status* from the dropdown:
** The system must *save the selected Status as-is*
** End Date–based auto logic *must not override* the user’s choice
* Applies to both *Upload* and *Edit* flows

----

h2. 🔁 Final Decision Matrix

||End Date||User Manually Changed Status?||Status to Save||
|Past|No|Expired|
|Future / Today|No|Non Compliant|
|Past|Yes|User-selected status|
|Future / Today|Yes|User-selected status|

----

h2. 🎯 Acceptance Criteria

* Status is auto-set only when user has *not interacted* with the Status field
* Manual selection always takes precedence
* Status persists correctly after Save
* Status is reflected consistently across:
** Policy details modal
** Listing page
** Filters & reports

column1: Contract Status Management & Email Triggers
column31:
Summary  

Add a *Contract Status* column in Contract Management that:

* Is *automatically or manually updated* based on defined rules
* Controls *dashboard visibility*
* Triggers *system notifications (emails)* where applicable

Acceptance Criteria: 

* A *Status* column shall be displayed in the Contract Management dashboard.
* Status values shall include:
** Current
** Future
** Expiring
** Expired
** Renewed
** Terminated
** Contract Completed
** Rebidding
** Termination in Process
* Status shall be:
** *System-generated* for date-driven statuses
** *User-selectable* for manual statuses
* Status shall update automatically when *start date or end date changes*.
* Status color coding shall be applied consistently across the dashboard.

h2. 2. Status Rules & Acceptance Criteria (System Generated)

h3. 2.1 Current

*Criteria*

* Status is set to *Current* when:
** Today’s date is *within the contract start and end dates*.
* Status is assigned automatically after contract upload or date update.

*Dashboard Behavior*

* Visible in default dashboard view.

*Notifications*

* No email notifications are triggered.

h3. 2.2 Future

*Criteria*

* Status is set to *Future* when:
** Today’s date is *before the contract start date*.

*Dashboard Behavior*

* Visible in default dashboard view.

*Notifications*

* No email notifications are triggered.

h3. 2.3 Expiring

*Criteria*

* Status is set to *Expiring* when:
** Contract end date is within *90, 60, or 30 days*.
* System shall trigger notifications:
** 90-day notification if today’s date <=90 days
** 60-day  notification if today’s date <=60 days
** 30-day notification if today’s date <=30 days
** If the contract term is only 3 months still 90 days notification should sent.
** If the contract term is only one month, then it should not trigger all 3 mails, it should trigger only for 30 days reminder. 
* *Dashboard Behavior*
* Visible in default dashboard view.

*Notifications*

* Email notifications sent at *30 / 60 / 90 days* prior to expiry.

h3. 2.4 Expired

*Criteria*

* Status is set to *Expired* when:
** Contract end date has passed.

*Dashboard Behavior*

* After 15 days of expiry, it should move to the Archived tab. This tab should be placed after the existing tab. 
* In Archived tab with the same record should be added with all the same fields. 
* Records in Archived tab should be editable 
* *If the user changes the ocntract end date to future date(changing the expiration) then it should change the status to expiring or current based on the end date.* 
* *In edit page, contract start date and end date changes should reflect on the status side.* 
* if the statusfrom expired changes from any other status based on the end date, it should move from archived to existing contract tab.

* The table failed to load data.

*** *“No data available”*, or
*** *“No locations found for the applied filter”*
* Optionally provide a *Reset Filter* action.

* No message or indication is shown to explain the absence of data.

h4. *Impact*

* Poor user experience
* Users may assume the data failed to load

* Implement a standard empty state for the Location table:
** Show *“No data available”* when filtered result count = 0
** Maintain consistency with other tables in the application
* Ensure empty state is triggered for:
** Filters

* When filters return zero records, an empty state message is displayed.
* Message is visible and accessible.
* Table layout remains consistent.

column1: [TRELLO] Client Module Vendor Tab Restructure + CSV Upload & Matching Workflow
column31:
[https://trello.com/c/ScWoPw9W|https://trello.com/c/ScWoPw9W|smart-link] 

h3. Description

Edit

For *SRG and future clients*, we need to restructure how vendors are managed in the Client Module and introduce a new upload and matching workflow.

----

h3. *Requested Changes*

h4. *1. Rename Existing Tab*

* Change the tab title *“Current Vendors”* in the *Client Module* to:
*“Contract Vendors”*

This tab should represent vendors associated through contracts.

----

h4. *2. Create a New Tab – Current Vendors*

* Add a *new tab* specifically for managing a client’s *current vendors* (not contract-driven).
* Users should be able to *manually upload current vendors* into this tab.
* The *fields/columns should match* the existing vendor structure.

----

h4. *3. CSV Upload Capability*

* Provide a way to *bulk upload vendors via CSV* into the new Current Vendors tab.
* CSV should map to the same vendor fields used in the system.

----

h4. *4. Vendor Matching Workflow*

A workflow is required to validate uploaded vendors against the *existing vendor database*:

* When vendors are uploaded:
** System checks if vendor already exists in the master vendor database.

*If vendor already exists and is fully onboarded:*
→ Link them as current vendor to the client.

*If vendor exists but is missing required information:*
→ Route them to the *Vendor Draft section* for completion of onboarding details.

*If vendor does not exist:*
→ Create new vendor in *Draft* status on the vendor side.

----

h3. *Current Limitation (Context)*

Right now, vendors can only appear under Current Vendors by completing a contract in Contract Management. There is no direct client-side vendor management.

----

h3. *Expected Outcome*

* Clear separation between *Contract Vendors* and *Client Current Vendors*
* Ability to manage non-contract vendors
* Bulk upload support
* Automated validation against existing vendor records
* Proper onboarding flow for incomplete vendors

column1: Allow Multiple Documents (Policy + Endorsements) Under the Same Policy (CR from client)
column31:
# I added an endorsement and when I did, it replaced the original document. It has to be able to have the original document and the endorsement both viewable under the same policy.

*Description*
When an endorsement is added to an existing policy, the system currently replaces the original policy document. This is incorrect behavior. Both the *original policy document* and *all endorsements* must be retained and viewable under the same policy.

*Problem Statement*

* Adding an endorsement overwrites the original policy document.
* Users lose access to the original policy file, leading to data loss and audit issues.

*Requirements*

# *Document Retention*
#* Adding an endorsement must *not replace* the original policy document.
#* The system should retain the original document and all endorsements.
# *Document Association*
#* All related documents (original policy + endorsements) should be associated with the same policy.
# *UI Display*
#* Display multiple documents under a single policy.
#* Clearly distinguish between:
#** Original Policy Document
#** Endorsement(s)
#* Show document metadata (e.g., document type, upload date).
# *View & Access*
#* Users must be able to view and download each document independently.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* Original policy document remains available after adding an endorsement.
* Endorsements are added as additional documents, not replacements.
* All documents are visible under the same policy.
* Users can view/download each document.
* No regression to existing policy document flows.

column31:
h2. User Story

*Title:* Bulk upload of property insurance  documents using drag-and-drop

*As a* User managing properties
*I want* to bulk upload multiple property files using a drag-and-drop interface
*So that* I can efficiently add multiple documents to the Property module in a single action.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

h3. 1. Bulk Upload Availability

*Given* the user is on the Property insurance module
*When* the user accesses the bulk upload option
*Then* the system shall allow bulk uploading of property-related files.

h3. 2. Multiple File Drag-and-Drop

*Given* the bulk upload interface is open
*When* the user drags and drops files into the upload area
*Then* the system shall accept *multiple individual files* in a single action
*And* each file shall be queued for upload.

h3. 3. No ZIP File Support

*Given* the user attempts to upload a ZIP file
*When* the file is added via drag-and-drop or file selection
*Then* the system shall reject the ZIP file
*And* display a validation message indicating that ZIP files are not supported.

h3. 4. Supported File Types Validation

*Given* the user uploads files
*When* the files are validated
*Then* the system shall allow only supported file formats as defined for the Property module
*And* unsupported file types shall be rejected with an error message.

h3. 5. Individual File Handling

*Given* multiple files are uploaded
*When* the upload process starts
*Then* each file shall be processed *individually*
*And* failure of one file shall not prevent other valid files from being uploaded.

h3. 6. Upload Status Feedback

*Given* files are being uploaded
*Then* the system shall display:

* Upload progress for each file
* Success or failure status per file

h3. 7. Successful Upload Confirmation

*Given* one or more files are uploaded successfully
*When* the upload completes
*Then* the system shall display a success message
*And* the uploaded files shall be visible in the Property module.

h3. 8. Error Handling

*Given* one or more files fail validation or upload
*When* the process completes
*Then* the system shall clearly display:

* Which files failed
* The reason for failure

column1: Delete Required in the pending insurance tab
column31:
h2. User Story

*Title:* Delete functionality for records in Pending Insurance tab

*As a* Property/Insurance Administrator
*I want* the ability to delete insurance records from the Pending Insurance tab based on their status
*So that* invalid, incorrect, or unnecessary insurance records can be permanently removed from the system when allowed.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

h3. 1. Delete Availability Based on Status

*Given* an insurance record exists in the *Pending Insurance* tab
*When* the record status is evaluated
*Then* the *Delete* action shall be available for *all statuses:* 


* Pending for Approval
* Completed
* Pending Connexus
*except Pending status*  :

h3. 2. Delete Behavior  for Pending for Approval

*Given* a record is in *Pending for Approval* status
*When* the user views the record in the Pending Insurance tab
*Then* the *Delete* option will be displayed or enabled
*And* the record should able to  delete by any user action.

h3. 3. Delete Behavior  for Pending Connexus

*Given* a record is in *Pending Connexus* status
*When* the user views the record in the Pending Insurance tab
*Then* the *Delete* option will be displayed or enabled
*And* the record should able to  delete by any user action.

h3. 4. Delete Behavior for Completed Records

*Given* a record is in *Completed* status
*When* the user deletes the record
*Then* the system shall remove the *entire insurance record* from the *Property Insurance tab*
*And* the record shall no longer be visible anywhere in the application.

h3. 6. Completed Record with Endorsements

*Given* a record is in *Completed* status
*And* the policy has one or more *endorsements*
*When* the record is deleted
*Then* the system shall remove:

* The base policy
* All associated endorsements
*And* the entire record shall be permanently removed from the Property Insurance tab.

h3. 7. Completed Record with Reuploaded Data

*Given* a record is in *Completed* status
*And* the policy has *reuploaded insurance data*
*When* the record is deleted
*Then* the system shall remove:

* The original policy
* All reuploaded versions
*And* the entire insurance record shall be permanently removed from the Property Insurance tab.

h3. 8. No Partial Deletion

*Given* a delete action is performed on a *Completed* record
*When* the deletion is successful
*Then* the system shall not retain:

* Any endorsements
* Any historical uploads
* Any related policy references
*And* no partial data shall remain in the system.

h3. 9. Confirmation Before Delete

*Given* a user initiates a delete action for an eligible record
*When* the delete action is triggered
*Then* the system shall display a confirmation prompt
*And* the record shall be deleted only after user confirmation.

column1: Property insurance Dashboard
column31:
h2. User Story

*Title:* Dashboard status cards with color-coded counts and single-select filtering

*As a* User managing Property Insurance records
*I want* to view status-based dashboard cards with color codes and record counts
*So that* I can quickly understand record distribution and filter the grid to see exact records for a selected status.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

h3. 1. Status Cards Display on Dashboard

*Given* the user is on the Property Insurance dashboard
*When* the dashboard loads
*Then* the system shall display *status cards* for each supported status
*And* each card shall:

* Be displayed in a *distinct color* based on the status
* Show the *total count of records* for that status

h3. 2. Status Color Coding

*Given* status cards are displayed
*Then* each status shall have a consistent, predefined color (for example):

* Compliant
* Expiring
* Expired
* Non-Compliant
* Deficient

*And* the same color coding shall be used consistently across the application.

h3. 3. Single-Select Status Filtering

*Given* multiple status cards are visible
*When* the user clicks on a status card
*Then* the system shall apply a *single-select filter*
*And* only records matching the selected status shall be displayed in the grid
*And* no other status card shall remain active.

h3. 4. Accurate Record Filtering

*Given* a status card is selected
*When* the grid is filtered
*Then* the system shall display *only the exact records* that match the selected status
*And* the number of displayed records shall match the count shown on the selected status card.

h3. 5. Toggle Behavior – Remove Status Filter

*Given* a status card filter is already applied
*When* the user clicks on the *same status card again*
*Then* the applied status filter shall be removed
*And* the grid shall return to the *unfiltered default view*.

h3. 6. Interaction with Other Filters

*Given* a status card filter is applied
*When* the user applies additional filters (for example: search, column filters, or advanced filters)
*Then* the system shall apply the additional filters *in combination* with the selected status filter
*And* the grid shall reflect the combined filter results.

h3. 7. Status Card Click After Other Filters

*Given* one or more non-status filters are already applied
*When* the user clicks on a status card
*Then* the system shall:

* Apply the selected status filter
* Retain the other applied filters
*And* update the grid accordingly.

h3. 8. Visual Indicator for Selected Status

*Given* a status card is selected
*Then* the system shall visually highlight the selected card
*And* clearly indicate that the status filter is active.

h3. 9. No Multi-Select Allowed

*Given* a status card is already selected
*When* the user clicks on a different status card
*Then* the previously selected status filter shall be removed
*And* the newly selected status filter shall be applied.

*When a Status Card is selected and the user clicks on a file underneath, say to make an edit, when they have finished that edit, they should still have the view of that selected status*

column1: [TRELLO] Unable to Edit AI-Mapped Fields in Edit Location Due to Other Required Fields in Property Insurance module
column31:
[https://trello.com/c/0t9ZzD69|https://trello.com/c/0t9ZzD69|smart-link] 

In the *Property Insurance → Edit Location* screen, when AI maps data into certain fields, users are unable to update those fields unless all other required fields are completed — even when that information is not yet available.

This prevents users from correcting AI-mapped values in stages.

*Issue Observed:*

* AI auto-fills some location fields (e.g., Building Address, Building Limit).
* User attempts to edit or correct those fields.
* System blocks the update because other required fields (e.g., Business Limits, Deductibles) are empty.
* Users may not yet have that information.

*Expected Behavior:*
Users should be able to:

* Edit/update *individual fields* that AI mapped
* Save partial updates
* Complete remaining required fields later

*Actual Behavior:*

* Form validation forces completion of *all required fields* before any edits can be saved.
* Prevents correction of incorrect AI-mapped data.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Upload an insurance document so AI maps location data.
# Go to *Edit Location*.
# Try to modify one mapped field (e.g., Building Limit).
# Leave other required fields blank (e.g., Business Limits).
# Click *Update Location*.
# Observe validation error blocking the update.

column1: Build Vendor Invitation Flow
column31:
As a Connexus User, I want to invite vendors from Client or Vendor modules so that onboarding begins through an automated workflow for Vendor Insurance Compliance.

As a Client User, I want to invite vendors from the Client module to the Vendor Compliance flow.

*Acceptance Criteria:*

* User can enter:
** Vendor email
** Business name
** Service(s)
** State(s) of operation
* System sends secure tokenized invite link.
* If vendor is new → trigger Full workflow.
* If vendor already onboarded under another client for Insurance Compliance → trigger Partial workflow (skip KYB).
* If a vendor is already on the platform, the email will acknowledge this and explain that this process is to verify the business.  This is only done 1 time.
* Vendor-client relationship stored.
* Services and states captured and persisted.

column1: API Orchestration Engine (Full Workflow)

Endpoint: {{/api/v3/global/pep_nm_wls}}

If all pass → Status = {{KYB Approved}}

* Sequential API execution.
* Stop progression if any stage fails.
* Retry 5xx errors only.
* Audit log per API call:
** Endpoint
** Timestamp
** Response code
** Decision

h3. Module:

Property Insurance / Pending Insurance

h3. Environment:

Test Environment

----

h3. Description:

When a user reuploads a policy and deletes the original policy before the reuploaded policy reaches *Complete* status, the system enters an inconsistent state.

Additionally, the system breaks when the same scenario is performed while the reuploaded policy is in *Pending for Approval* status.

----

h3. Steps to Reproduce:

# Upload a policy → Policy appears in *Pending Insurance* tab.
# Select property and save → Status changes to *Complete* → Record moves to *Property Insurance* tab.
# Edit the policy and reupload a new file.
# The reuploaded policy appears in the *Pending Insurance* tab.
# Before the reuploaded policy reaches *Complete(in pending status)*, delete the original (old) policy from *Property Insurance* tab.
# or Allow the reuploaded policy to change  in *Pending for Approval* status.
# Open the reuploaded policy.

----

h3. Actual Result:

*  (If the reuploaded policy is in *Pending* ) The reuploaded policy moves to *Failed* status because there is no existing policy available to replace, as the original policy was deleted.
* If the reuploaded policy is in *Pending for Approval*, the system breaks when opening the policy.
* Property is not listed.
* Application becomes unstable.

----

h3. Expected Result:

* The system should *prevent deletion of the original policy* if a reuploaded policy is still in:
** Pending
** Pending for Approval
* Proper validation message should be displayed.
* Application should not break under any status condition.

----

h3. Suggested Fix:

Restrict deletion of the original policy until the reuploaded policy status is *Complete*.

Display error message:

{quote}Error Message Suggestion 1: "Unable to delete this policy. A linked reuploaded policy is currently in Pending/Pending for Approval status. Please complete the reuploaded policy before deleting the existing one."

Suggestion 2:
Deletion not allowed. A reuploaded policy is still pending completion. Please complete the reuploaded policy before deleting the existing one.{quote}

column618:
20/Feb/26 12:53 PM;61e900cef0ed0400689392d4;[~accountid:6200d7cd5d18ad0072987c6f] ,

* *Agency license number on the policy*: The license number is stored on the *InsuranceAgency* entity, not on the policy. The policy only stores *agencyId*. So the “agency license number” for a policy is always the one from the linked agency.

* *Policy edit*: The user changes the *agency* (via {{agencyId}}). The API does not accept a separate agency license field. When they select a different agency, the UI shows that agency’s name and license number from the API. Changing the agency is how the effective “agency license number” is updated.
* *Agency creation*: When we process AI-extracted property insurance data, we resolve the agency by checking if it already exists in our system (by name). If it does not, we create a new *InsuranceAgency* with the extracted name and license number. So agencies (and their license numbers) are created at extraction time when they’re not already in the system.

[https://trello.com/c/lcFJYo2h|https://trello.com/c/lcFJYo2h|smart-link] 

In policies where multiple coverages exist (including Underlying Coverages), the system is only displaying the Umbrella coverage. The Underlying Coverages are not being shown or identified properly in the UI.

There should be a clear way (such as tags or labels) to display all associated underlying coverages separately.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Upload or open a policy file that contains multiple coverages (Umbrella + Underlying Coverages).
# Navigate to the policy details page.
# Review the displayed coverage information.

*Current Behavior:*

* System only displays the Umbrella coverage.
* Underlying Coverages are not shown or distinguished.
* No tags or indicators are available for multiple coverages.

*Expected Behavior:*

* All coverages from the file should be captured and displayed.
* Underlying Coverages should be clearly labeled (e.g., as tags or separate entries).
column617:
20/Feb/26 1:24 PM;6200d7cd5d18ad0072987c6f; [~accountid:61e900cef0ed0400689392d4] , kindly confirm whether this issue requires a fix from our end or if it is entirely related to the AI logic.

column618:
20/Feb/26 3:28 PM;61e900cef0ed0400689392d4;[~accountid:6200d7cd5d18ad0072987c6f] 
We currently map policy coverage from the AI-extracted policyType field into our DB, so only one coverage (e.g. Umbrella) is stored and shown. To support multiple coverages (e.g. Umbrella + Underlying), we need clarification on:

* Which AI-extracted fields should map to our DB (e.g. otherCoverageLimits, or others) so we can persist and display all coverages.
* Whether we should map the AI field otherCoverageLimits to our DB — we receive it in the AI payload but need confirmation on how it should be used and stored.
* UI changes — how multiple coverages should be displayed (e.g. tags, separate entries, or another pattern) so we can align backend and frontend.

The *OtherCoverageLimits* value is currently being retrieved from the AI-extracted data.

column1: Add “Policy Limit” Field in Policy Edit Page
column31:
*Description:*
The *Policy Limit* field needs to be added to the *Policy Edit Page* on the Front End. Corresponding updates are also required in the Back End API to support this field.

----

h3. *Scope of Work:*

h4. *1. Front End (Policy Edit Page)*

* Add a new input field: *Policy Limit*
* Field should:
** Accept numeric values (with proper validation)
** Support currency format (if applicable)
** Be editable in the Policy Edit page
** Be displayed properly in alignment with existing policy fields
* Include validation (mandatory/optional – to be confirmed)
* Ensure value is retained after Save/Confirm action
* Add the same field in *Filter* 

h4. *2. Back End (API Changes)*

* Update existing Policy Create/Update API to:
** Accept {{policyLimit}} parameter
** Validate and store the value in DB
* Update GET Policy API to:
** Return {{policyLimit}} in response
* Ensure backward compatibility for existing policies

column31:
Summary : 

Connexus E-sign Refactoring 

*End-End Workflow*

h3. 1. Entry Points to E-Signature

Clients can initiate an e-signature workflow from *either*:

* *RFP Module* (for awarded RFP contracts), or
* *Connexus E-Sign Module* (for standalone contracts)

h3. 2. Contract Creation Paths

h4. A. Contract Creation via RFP 

# Client navigates to  Awarded RFP from RFP module
# Client selects the *Awarded RFPs* tab.
## The Awarded Tab should have the following information in this order:
### Client
### Property ID
### Property
### RFP Name
### Service 
### Vendor
### Date Awarded (DD/MM/YYYY) format.
### Status- The Status Fields are:
#### Awarded (first stage, once it is awarded on the RFP side).
#### Draft (in the contract creation process).
#### Sent (contract is in the sent stage).
#### Completed (the contract was completed and sent to the Contract Management Module).
#### Once completed, contracts will be archived from this screen so we have the history.
## The Awarded Tab should be sortable on each column, downloadable into Excel, and you should be able to filter by all of the headers.
# Client can select one of the record from the awarded property RFP.
# Client Chooses to *Generate Contract* for selected property RFP{color:#ff5630}.{color}
# System navigates to the contract template screen which list out all the contract templates under the client.
# System regenerates the selected template and opens the *Contract Editor*.  THis will show a preview screen where user can reopsition the standard RFP related values like : Client legal name,Property name, Property Legal name, property address,vendor name,Total cost. SOW cannot be populated as per the current time frame.
# Once the data is repositioned and click on confirm it will generate the tempalte and will automatically create a template and save it in the ocntract template module. After that it will navigate to the Editor page where user can edit the populated data and do neccessary changes
# When opening up the Editor- the top left document title should refer to the Name of the RFP (if the contract was created by an RFP) or the name of the document (if it was uploaded as a standalone).

h4. B. Contract via Connexus E-Sign (Standalone)

# Client navigates to *Connexus E-Sign → Sign Management*.
# Client uploads a contract document (PDF) by clicking an “Upload Contract” button.
# Client adds recipients and defines signing order.
# Client proceeds to send the document for signature.

*C. Contract Template Creation on the Client Side*

# This should be a tab for each client in the Client module.
# In this tab the Templates should have the same UX/UIe which exists today in the Connexus E-Sign for Templates.  
# These templates shall only be viewable by Clients and by Connexus.

h3. 3. Contract Editing & Configuration (RFP Flow Only)

# Once the tempplate is confirmred then user can click on confirm for adding recipients. 
# Add recipient should have name, email id field. Name should be combination of first name and and Last name, Email field should be a dropdown and should have an option to 
# User can add  multiple recipients in the system. it will appear as blank and user can add users by clicking on Add Reciepients
# User should able to reorder by changing the sequence along with that user should have the ability to reshuffle option which should automatically change the order 
# System displays a sidebar with available placeholders:
#* Signature
#* Date Field (MM/DD/YYYY format)
#* Text
# Recipients name will be displayed as color coded under recipients dropdown. user can select the user and once the place holder drag and drop it will display the same color.
# After adding the signature user can click on send for signature.
# Client confirms the contract setup and the contract can  Send for signature  or Save as a Draft.  
## Draft contracts are stored in the Esign module as drafts.

h3. 5. Signing & Status Management

# Recipients receive email notifications sequentially.  Meaning that the first signer receives it, then after the first one signs, then the contract is sent to the second signer.
## Once the contract is fully executed a copy of the contracts will be sent to all signatories.
# Each recipient 
#* Views the contract
#* Signs in order
#* {color:#bf2600}Save it{color}
#* {color:#bf2600}Download it.{color}
# System tracks all actions in real time:
#* Sent
#* Viewed
#* Signed
#* Completed- Completed means that the contract has been signed by all parties.
# If a contract needs to be cancelled or deleted, that can happen from the system 

h3. 6. Unified Tracking & Audit6. Unified Tracking & Audit

# All contracts RFP based and standalone appear in:
#* *Connexus E-Sign → Documents in Process*
# For each document, the system displays:
#* Client
#* Property (RFP only)
#* Vendor (RFP only)
#* Service (RFP only)
#* Document Name (RFP name for those contracts and Saved Doc Name for those which are Standalone).
#* Date Sent
#* Status
#* Sent by (user name)
#* Recipients email
#* Signer’s Status
#* # of reminders sent
#* Document Sent (view & download)
#* Audit
#* Certificate
# Upon final signature:
#* Document status updates to *Completed*
#* Document becomes read-only 
#* Audit trail is permanently preserved. (Please keep the current audit trail which has been captured as it has been vetted by Conexus' attorneys), except removing any JSON and replacing with text.Audit trail will ensure the IP address has been captured from those who have signed.
#* Certificate will be maintained as it is today, except removing any JSON and replacing with text.
#* Document is then moved to the Contract Management Dashboard.

h3. 7. Outcome

* Clients can:
** Generate contracts from awarded RFPs
** Send ad-hoc contracts without RFP dependency
** Track all signatures in one place
** Document is then moved to the Contract Management Dashboard.
** The system delivers a *consistent*, *compliant*, and *traceable* e-signature experience across Connexus.
