column1: Contract generation using Contract template
column31:
h3. 

_User Story:_
As a _Client or Connexus user_, I should be able to generate a contract from an awarded RFP property using an existing contract template, so that I can populate the required RFP values, preview the document, and edit the contract before sending it for signature.

h3. Acceptance Criteria

_AC-1: Generate Contract Navigation_

_ When the user clicks _Generate Contract* for an awarded property RFP,
_ The system should navigate to the _Contract Template Selection screen*.

* The screen should list all contract templates available under that client.
* it should not list the archived or deleted contracts 

_AC-2: Contract Template List_

* The template list should display only templates belonging to the selected client.
* User should be able to select one template.
* User should not proceed without selecting a template.Validation should be triggered

_AC-3: Template Regeneration & Preview Screen_

* When the user selects a template,
_ The system should regenerate the template and open the _Contract Preview screen*.
* The preview should show the contract with populated RFP-related values.

The system should show below tags avaialble to drag and drop:

* Client Legal Name
* Property Legal Name
* property Name
* Property Address
* Vendor Name
* Total Cost
_ _SOW  : System should show the SOW link after drag and drop. on click on the link it should open a dialog box which will show all the SOWs linked to that property and vendor for that RFP.* 
* It should have view button and should able to copy the sow and paste in the document. 
* Basic formatting should avaialble in the editor for the change

_AC-4: Repositioning RFP Values_

* In the preview screen, user should be able to reposition the populated values.
* User should be able to drag / move the fields to the correct location.
_ _AC-5: Confirm and Generate Template*
_ When the user clicks _Confirm*,
* The system should generate a new contract document.
_ The system should automatically create a new template entry in the _Contract Template Module*.

_AC-6: Navigate to Contract Editor_

* After confirming the preview,
_ The system should navigate to the _Contract Editor page*.
* User should be able to edit the generated document.
* User should be able to modify text and populated values.
* User should be able to add/remove fields if required.

_AC-7: Editor Document Title_

* When the Editor opens:
__ If the contract is generated from an RFP →
___ The document title (top left) should show the _RFP Name*.
__ If the contract is uploaded as standalone →
___ The document title should show the _Document Name*.

_AC-8: Data Source Validation_

* All populated values must come from the selected:
__ Client
__ Property
__ Vendor
__ RFP Award record
* If any value is missing, the system should still allow editing in the Editor.

_AC-9 : Action Buttons_

* There should be Save as Draft, cancel and confirm option
* Save as Draft action should create a draft version of the template and user should able to continue the draft from where they paused. 
* confirm should move to the next page
* Cancel should cancel the current actions and move back to the last saved change.

column1: [Medium] Contract Management – Remove "per units" Text from Cost/Unit/Year Column
column31:
*Description (Template):*

*What:*
When exporting contract data to Excel, the "Cost/Unit/Year" column incorrectly appends the text “per units” after each dollar value (e.g., {{$134.43 per units}}).

*Where:*
Excel export file generated from the *Contract Management → Existing Contracts* dashboard.

*Expected:*
The Excel export should display only the dollar values (e.g., {{$134.43}}) without the extra “per units” text.

*Impact:*

* The dashboard data is correct, but the exported Excel file introduces inconsistencies.
* This formatting issue makes the exported data harder to read, use in calculations, and integrate into other reports.
* The dataset is needed *urgently* for upcoming reporting, making this a *high-priority* fix.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Log in to the Connexus dashboard.
# Navigate to *Contract Management → Existing Contracts*.
# Apply any filters and generate the results.
# Click *Download Contract* to export the data.
# Open the exported Excel file and review the "Cost/Unit/Year" column.
# Observe that the column includes “per units” after the dollar values.

h2. User Story: Upload Contract from Sign Management Tab

h3. Acceptance Criteria

** File upload control

* The Contract Signing page displays:
** Document preview area : it should show the preview of the document
** Recipient management section 
** Field toolbox (Signature, Date, Text, Full name.)
** Save and Send actions
* The page loads without errors for both PDF and DOC files.

h2. User Story: Add Recipients

h3. Acceptance Criteria

* The user can add one or more recipients.
* User should able to add multiple users in the reciepients by clicking on Add recipient option. 
* System should provide an option to add users and thei emailid (those users may or maynot exists in db and should able to send these users outside connexus system)
* Each recipient requires:
** Recipient name
** Recipient email
* Email format validation is enforced.
* Recipients with invalid emails cannot be added.
* Added recipients are displayed in a recipient list.

h2. User Story: Assign Fields to Recipients

h3. Acceptance Criteria

* The user can select an active recipient from the recipient list.
* Fields added to the document are associated with the selected recipient.
* The system visually indicates which recipient a field belongs to.
* After confirmation it move to the drag and drop fields 

h2. User Story: Drag and Drop Fields onto Document

h3. Acceptance Criteria

* The field toolbox provides draggable fields such as:
** Signature
** Date
** Text
* Fields can be dragged from the toolbox and dropped onto the document preview.
* Dropped fields are placed at the selected location.
* it should not have any curly brackets in the documents. It should be represented in a more UI friendly format like a tag 

h2. User Story: Edit Field Placement

h3. Acceptance Criteria

* The user can move fields after placing them on the document.
* Field positioning should be enabled and user should able to move the fields manually 

h2. User Story: Validate Before Sending for Signature

h3. Acceptance Criteria

* At least one recipient must be added before sending.
* Required fields (e.g., Signature) must be present for each recipient.
* The system prevents sending if validation fails.
* Clear validation messages are displayed to guide the user.

h2. User Story: Save and Send Contract

h3. Acceptance Criteria

* The user can save the document configuration as a draft.
* Clicking *Send for Signature* sends the document to the first recipient in the signing order.
* The document status updates to *In Process*.
* The document appears in *Documents in Process*.

Got it. Here are *Acceptance Criteria in simple bullet points only (no Given/When/Then format)* for
*Sign Management → List tab after sending digital signature from E-Sign module*

*SIGN MANAGMENT LIST PAGE*
* The Sign Management tab should display all documents sent for digital signature from the E-Sign module.
* Each record should be shown in a tabular list view.
* The list should contain the following columns:
** Client Name
** Owner / Service
** Recipient
** Recipient Email(s)
** Status
** Signed Status
** Contract Signed
** Reminders Sent
** Documents
** Audit
** Actions (3-dot menu)
* Status column should show values such as:
** In Process
** Completed
** Cancelled
* Signed Status column should show signer-wise status with indicators:
** Signed
** Pending
** Declined / Failed (if applicable)
* Contract Signed column should display signer completion status for each signer.
* Reminders Sent column should show the number of reminders sent to each signer.
* Documents column should contain:
** View icon to preview document
** Download icon to download document
* Audit column should contain a button to open audit history of the signature process.
* Certificate column should contain a button to open the digital signature certificate.
* Clicking the 3-dot action menu should show:
** View Audit
** Cancel Sending (only when status is In Process)
* Cancel Sending option should stop the signing process and update status to Cancelled.
* Filters button should allow filtering based on:
** Client
** Status
** Owner / Service
** Recipient
** Signed status
* Upload Contract button should open the contract upload screen to send a new document for signature.
* Download CSV button should export the current list data.
* Pagination should be shown when records exceed the page limit.
* Column sorting should be avaialble

*DOCUMENT IN PROCESS TAB*

h3. 1. Data Visibility & Record Creation

* *Automatic Listing:* As soon as a digital signature request is initiated, a new row must automatically populate in the "Documents in Process" tab.
* *Core Information:* Each record must display the following identifying columns:
** *Client & Property Name:* Identifying which entity the document belongs to.
** *Vendor & Service:* The associated service provider and type of work.
** *Document Name:* The specific title of the file sent.
** *Owner:* The user/admin who initiated the signature request.

h3. 2. Recipient & Signer Tracking

* *Email Transparency:* The {{Recipients email}} column must list all participants involved in the workflow.
* *Signer Status (Visual Cues):* * *Signed (Green):* Must list names of individuals who have completed their signature.
** *Outstanding (Orange/Red):* Must list names of individuals who still need to sign.
* *Detailed Progress:* The {{Contract Signed}} column must show the specific date each signer completed the task or mark it as "Pending."

h3. 3. Status & Reminders

* *Workflow Status:* * Records should show *"In Progress"* (Blue) if at least one signature is missing.
** Records should transition to *"Complete"* (Green) once all recipients have signed.
* *Reminder Audit:* The {{No. of Reminders Sent}} column must track how many nudges have been sent to each specific signer to ensure accountability.

h3. 4. Timeline & Actions

* *Sent Date:* The system must record the exact date the document was first dispatched ({{Contract Sent Date}}).
* *Document Access:* A *Download* button must be available for each row, allowing users to pull the current version of the document (whether partially or fully signed).
* *Global Actions:* A top-level "Download" and "Filters" button must be functional to allow for bulk reporting and narrowed searches.

*AUDIT TAB*

h3. 1. Document Access (Integrity Section)

* *Original PDF:* * The system must provide a secure link to the "Original PDF" (the version before any signatures were applied).
** *Action:* Clicking the *Open* button must initiate a download or open the original document in a new tab for review.
* *Final PDF:*
** *Conditionality:* The Final PDF (the fully executed document) must *only* be available for download once *all recipients* listed in the workflow have signed.
** *Action:* Prior to full execution, the button should either be disabled, hidden, or show a "Not available yet" status (similar to the Certificate field).
* *Hashes:* The system must display the *SHA-256* hash for both the Original and Final documents to ensure data integrity and prove the files have not been tampered with.

h3. 2. Recipient Tracking & Signature Files

* *Sequential Listing:* Recipients must be displayed in their assigned signing order.
* *Status Details:* Each row must show:
** *Action:* The required task (e.g., "sign").
** *Timestamp:* The exact date and time the signature was applied (e.g., {{Thu, 05 Mar 2026 06:45:17 GMT}}).
** *Signature File:* A file path or link to the specific image file of the signature used (e.g., {{tmp/signatures/.../first_3.png}}).

h3. 3. Settings Audit

* *Configuration Visibility:* The page must display the logic used for the document request, including:
** *Auto Reminder:* Status (Enabled/Disabled).
** *Reminder Frequency:* (e.g., "Every 2 days").
** *Metadata:* Owner name and the exact "Created At" timestamp.

h3. 4. Audit Trail (Log History)

* *Event Logging:* Every significant action must be recorded as a line item in the Audit Trail table.
* *Data Points:* Each log entry must include:
** *Timestamp (UTC):* The precise time of the event.
** *Event Type:* (e.g., {{email_sent}}, {{request_created}}, {{document_viewed}}, {{document_signed}}).
** *Signer/IP:* Identification of who performed the action and from which IP address.
** *Meta Data:* JSON-formatted details showing the email subject line, recipient email, or total number of recipients involved.

h3. *User Flow:* _Admin clicks "Audit" from the Documents in Process tab $\rightarrow$ System redirects to the Audit Page $\rightarrow$ System fetches real-time signature status $\rightarrow$ If all signatures = Complete, "Final PDF" becomes clickable._

Implement the *Send for Signatures* page based on the provided Figma design. This page allows users to review contract details and configure recipients before sending a document for electronic signature.

The page should include a document preview, client and vendor information, and a recipients management section where users can define signing order, roles, and delivery methods.


h3. *UI Sections*

h4. *1. Page Header*

* Title: *Send for Signatures*
* Subtitle: *View and manage Send for Signatures*
* Action buttons:
** *Cancel*
** *Save Draft*
** *Confirm*

----

h4. *2. Document Preview*

* Display a preview thumbnail of the *Statement of Work* document.

----

h4. *3. Client Information*

Display the following details:

* *Name*
* *Address*
* *Legal entity*

----

h4. *4. Vendor Information*

Display the following details:

* *Name*
* *Vendor Parent Name*
* *Submitted By*

----

h4. *5. Recipients Section*

A table where users can configure the recipients involved in the signing process.

*Columns*

* Order
* Name
* Email Address
* Options
* Deliver Link
* Action

*Row Elements*
Each row should contain:

* Signing *order indicator*
* Name input field
* Email input/dropdown{color:#0747a6} {color}[~accountid:712020:4f8fb5fd-8f8d-4fe2-9070-80617e96a441]{color:#0747a6} Text only . Confirmed with {color}[~accountid:63c8e40fd579d7c687552750]{color:#0747a6} {color}
* Signing role dropdown with options such as:
** Need to Sign
** In-Person Signer
** Sign with Witness
** Manage Recipient
** Approver
* Delivery method dropdown (Email) -{color:#0747a6} {color}[~accountid:712020:4f8fb5fd-8f8d-4fe2-9070-80617e96a441]{color:#0747a6}  Not Required. Confirmed with {color}[~accountid:63c8e40fd579d7c687552750]{color:#0747a6} {color}
* Delete action

----

h3. *Recipients Functionality*

* Users can *add recipients* using the *Add Recipients* button.
* Users can *remove recipients* using the delete action.
* Users can *edit name and email* fields.
* Users can *select signing roles* for each recipient.
* Users can *select delivery method*.

*Signing Order Management*

* The *order of recipients is configurable*.
* Users should be able to change the order by:
** *Typing a number directly in the order field*, or 
** *Reordering rows using drag and drop*.

----

h3. *Acceptance Criteria*

* The *Send for Signatures page UI matches the Figma design*.
* Document preview is displayed.
* Client and vendor information sections are visible.
* Recipients table allows:
** Adding recipients
** Removing recipients
** Editing name and email
** Selecting signing roles
** Selecting delivery method

column1: Drag and drop functionality and its fields
column31:
h3. Objective

Deliver the contract template HTML editor on Remirror v3 with drag-and-drop for placeholder fields: Stage 1 standard contract fields from the sidebar, Stage 2 per-recipient signing fields, and repositioning of existing chips inside the document.

h3. Editor setup

* Use Remirror v3 with an HTML string handler so template HTML from the API loads and serialises correctly (not markdown).
* Implement a custom inline atom node for placeholders so merged tokens render as styled chips in the UI while saved HTML preserves the correct token strings.
* Preprocess HTML before editor load (tokens → structured markup); on save, walk the document and restore token strings in the exported HTML.
* Follow Remirror v3 constraints for custom nodes: extension constructors with an options argument, disable extra auto attributes on the custom node, and disallow marks on the placeholder node so text colour and highlight extensions do not wrap chip output on save.
* Use CSS custom properties for chip colours (especially Stage 2 per recipient) so styling does not collide with mark-based formatting.
* Present the editing surface in an A4-style layout with chip styling; suppress ProseMirror separator artefacts that affect layout where needed.
* Respect template stage: Stage 1 (standard fields only) vs Stage 2 (recipients + signing fields); supply recipient colour data in Stage 2 so chips round-trip on reload; wire save draft and confirm to the existing APIs, including recipient field metadata payloads for Stage 2.

h3. Drag and drop

_ _Stage 1 (sidebar → editor):* Draggable field cards carry structured JSON on drag; the editor handles dragover and drop, maps pointer position to a document position, inserts a placeholder atom inside a valid text block, sets selection after the new node, and focuses the editor.
_ _Stage 2 (recipient fields → editor):* Same flow with recipient identifier, colour data, a new unique instance id per drag, and composite token format so the same field type can appear multiple times for one recipient.
_ _Internal (reposition within editor):* Placeholder nodes are draggable; a plugin keeps the caret visible during dragover; after an internal move, replace node-only selection with a text caret immediately after the chip and refocus, using a short defer so the move transaction finishes first.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* While editing, users work with chips, not raw brace tokens; exported HTML contains the correct Stage 1 and Stage 2 token formats.
* External drag from the sidebar succeeds for both stages, with correct metadata on each chip and sensible cursor/focus after drop.
* Stage 2 chips show the active recipient’s colours; colours persist and reload with template data.
* Users can drag existing chips to new positions; the caret follows the pointer during drag-over; after an internal drop, behaviour matches a normal text cursor after the chip.
* Save draft, confirm, and navigation stay consistent with the contract template e-sign flow for both stages.

column1: Contract Template Workflow
column31:
*User Story — Contract Templates Tab in the Client Module*

As users begin working inside the *Client Module*, they encounter a dedicated space for managing contract templates. This area is organized under a *Contract Templates* tab designed to keep templates, drafts, and generated agreements clearly separated and easy to manage.

Inside this section, users see *three tabs*, each serving a different stage of the contract lifecycle:

* *Generated Contracts*- full contract- tagged with the data from the DB before sending signature with all property specifics 
* *All Templates-* The New Upload and all prior sent and formatted contracts
* *Formatted Contracts-* the Save As File with the tags- so future contracts can be pulled based on these fields

----

h3. The Flow of Contracts Through the Tabs

When a user first *uploads a contract template*, it does not immediately appear as a formatted template. Instead, it initially lands in the *All templates* tab. This tab acts as the entry point for newly uploaded templates. Contracts here are available for users to select and use when generating agreements, but they have not yet been structured or formatted with dynamic fields.

From this point forward, these templates remain usable until a user chooses to archive them.

Meanwhile, every contract that is created through the system is automatically captured in the *Generated Contracts* tab. This tab acts as a running history of all contracts that have been produced by the platform.

----

h3. Creating a Formatted Template

At some point, a user may want to convert a contract into a *Formatted Template* so that it can be reused in a structured way.

To do this, the user begins by *generating a contract from an RFP* and selecting an existing contract from either:

* *Generated Contracts*- full contract- tagged with the data from the DB before sending signature with all property specifics
* *All Templates- The New Upload and all prior sent and formatted contracts*
* *Formatted Contracts- the Save As File with the tags- so future contracts can be pulled based on these fields*

Once the contract is opened within the RFP workflow, the user eventually reaches the screen where *dynamic fields are mapped into the contract using drag-and-drop placeholders*.

At this stage, the system provides an option to *save the contract as a Formatted Contract template*.

The user selects *“Save As”*, assigns a *new template name*, (it has to be a unique name to that client) and saves the document. Once saved, the system moves this contract into the *Formatted Templates* tab, where it becomes a reusable template for future contract generation.

----

h3. Managing Templates

Within the *Formatted Templates* tab, users can see key metadata for each template, including:

* *File Name*
* *Date Formatted*
* *User Name* (the person who created the template)

Over time, templates may become outdated or no longer needed. When this happens, users can move them into the *Archived Templates* tab. Both *Formatted Templates* and *New Contracts* can be archived in this way, allowing teams to maintain a clean and organized template library.

----

h3. Generating Contracts

When a user generates a contract from an *RFP*, the system allows them to select the contract source from three available categories:

# *Formatted Templates*
# *Generated Templates*
# *All templates* 
This gives users flexibility to either reuse standardized templates, reuse an existing contract, or start from a newly uploaded template.

----

h3. Summary of Contract Lifecycle

# A contract is *uploaded → appears in All Templates*
# Contracts used in RFPs are *tracked in Generated Templates*.
# A contract can be *formatted during the RFP workflow and saved as a Formatted Template*.
# Templates that are no longer needed can be *moved to Archived Templates*.

This structure ensures contract templates evolve from *raw uploads → formatted reusable templates → archived history*, while maintaining full visibility into every contract created by the system.

Summary

Handle user authentication for the Signing View page where external recipients (signers) land via email link to sign a contract. Unlike the rest of the app which requires login-based authentication, the signing flow uses a token-based public route approach — no login is needed.

Implementation Details
## Public Route — The signing page is registered as a completely public route, placed outside all auth-guarded layouts. No login, session checks, or auth redirects apply.

2. Token Extraction — The signing token is extracted from the URL query parameter. If the token is missing or empty, a user-friendly "Invalid signing link" error screen is displayed.

3. Token-Based API Authentication — The token is passed as a query parameter in every signing-related API call (view document, sign document). The backend validates the token and identifies the recipient — no bearer token or session cookie is used.

4. Error Handling — If the API returns an error (invalid token, expired link, already signed, etc.), an error screen is rendered with the backend error message and a retry option.

What Was NOT Needed
* No login/registration flow for signers
* No token refresh mechanism (tokens are one-time use, managed by BE)
* No session storage or cookie management
* No auth context/provider wrapping for this route

*Summary:* Insurance Certificate Compliance Engine – Policy Requirement Validation & Notification System

*Description*

As a compliance administrator, I need the system to automatically compare a vendor or service provider's submitted insurance certificate(s) against the client-specific insurance requirements so that non-compliant submissions are flagged and stakeholders are notified without manual review. A vendor may satisfy compliance requirements through a single COI or through a combination of multiple COIs that collectively meet all required coverages, limits, and endorsements.



----



*Background*

The platform maintains a configurable library of insurance requirement rules across multiple policy types (e.g., Commercial General Liability, Automobile Liability, Workers Compensation, Excess Liability, Cyber Liability, etc.). Each client can define their own thresholds and required coverages per vendor or service type. When one or more Certificates of Insurance (COIs) are submitted, the system must parse each certificate, evaluate the full submission set collectively against the applicable rule set, and trigger notifications for any outstanding failures.

Connexus operates as the compliance management platform and must itself be named as Certificate Holder and Additional Insured on all vendor-submitted certificates. Individual clients on the platform may additionally require their own legal entity — or the legal entity of a specific managed property — to be named as Certificate Holder and/or Additional Insured, depending on how the client account is configured.



----



*Certificate Holder & Submission Requirements (Connexus Platform Standard)*

All vendor-submitted Certificates of Insurance must meet the following baseline requirements regardless of client configuration:

*Certificate Holder (Required on all COIs):*

Connexus 115 Willbrook Blvd. Ste S #2027 Pawleys Island, SC 29585

*Submission Channel:* Certificates may also be submitted via email to: [insurance@joinconnexus.com|mailto:insurance@joinconnexus.com]

*Additional Requirements (Applied to all policies):*

# *Additional Insured* – Connexus shall be named as Additional Insured on the General Liability policy where required by written contract.
# *Waiver of Subrogation* – A Waiver of Subrogation in favor of Connexus shall apply to all policies where permitted by law.
# *Notice of Cancellation* – Policies shall provide not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Connexus in the event of cancellation, non-renewal, or material change in coverage. Ten (10) days' notice applies for cancellation due to non-payment of premium.

These requirements are system-level defaults enforced on every COI evaluation, independent of any client-specific rule configuration.



----



*Multi-COI Submission & Aggregate Compliance*

A vendor's compliance requirement may be satisfied by a single COI or by multiple COIs submitted together. The system must treat the full set of submitted COIs for a given vendor/property pairing as a unified submission and evaluate compliance across the combined document set.

*Key rules for multi-COI evaluation:*

* Each required policy type must appear on at least one COI in the submission set. Coverage does not need to be consolidated onto a single document.
* Limit thresholds are evaluated per policy type against whichever COI carries that coverage — limits are *not* aggregated or summed across documents.
* Endorsement and coverage flag requirements (e.g., additional insured, waiver of subrogation) must be satisfied on the specific COI carrying the relevant policy. Meeting an endorsement requirement on one document does not satisfy it for a policy carried on a separate document.
* Global requirements (certificate holder name, carrier rating, cancellation notice) must be met on *each* COI in the submission set individually — these are not satisfied by one document on behalf of others.
* The system must track which COI in the submission set satisfies each individual rule, and surface that mapping in the audit log and any failure notifications.
* A submission is considered fully compliant only when all required rules are satisfied across the combined set of COIs with no outstanding failures remaining.



----



*Certificate Holder Architecture – Client vs. Property-Level Configuration*

The system must support two modes for certificate holder identity, configurable at the client account level:

*Mode 1 – Overarching Client Entity* The Certificate Holder and Additional Insured name reflects the client's top-level legal entity name as stored in the client account profile. This is the default mode.

*Mode 2 – Property-Level Legal Entity* Where a client manages multiple properties (e.g., a property management company), the Certificate Holder and Additional Insured name may be set to the individual property's legal entity name rather than the overarching client entity. This is configured at the property level within the client account.

*Architectural requirements for this feature:*

* The client account model must support a {{certificate_holder_mode}} field with two enumerated values: {{CLIENT_ENTITY}} and {{PROPERTY_ENTITY}}.
* When {{PROPERTY_ENTITY}} is selected, the property record must store a {{legal_entity_name}} field used in place of the client-level entity name during compliance evaluation.
* Compliance evaluations must resolve the correct certificate holder name dynamically based on which vendor/property pairing the COI set is associated with.
* The system must validate that each COI's {{certificate.certificate_holder_name}} field contains both the Connexus entity (always required) and the resolved client or property legal entity name (based on mode) when client configuration requires it.
* If {{PROPERTY_ENTITY}} mode is active but no {{legal_entity_name}} has been set for that property, the system must surface a configuration warning to the client admin and fall back to {{CLIENT_ENTITY}} mode until resolved.



----



*Acceptance Criteria*

*AC1 – Rule Configuration*

* The system supports configurable rules for all policy types defined in the rule library, including: Commercial General Liability, Automobile Liability, Workers Compensation, Excess Liability, Pollution Liability, Cyber Liability, Crime/Fidelity Bond, Technology E&O, Contractors Pollution Liability, Inland Marine, Liquor Liability, and Abuse & Molestation Liability.
* Global rules apply across all policy types and include: certificate holder name validation, cancellation notice period (days), carrier AM Best rating (minimum), and carrier AM Best financial size category (minimum).
* Each client can configure their own required values per rule type per vendor/service category.
* The Connexus platform-level defaults (certificate holder address, additional insured, waiver of subrogation, 30-day cancellation notice) are enforced on every evaluation and cannot be disabled by client configuration.

*AC2 – Certificate Holder Validation*

* The system must validate that every COI in the submission set lists Connexus (115 Willbrook Blvd. Ste S #2027, Pawleys Island, SC 29585) as Certificate Holder. A submission is non-compliant if any individual COI fails this check.
* If the client account is configured in {{CLIENT_ENTITY}} mode, the system must additionally validate that the client's top-level legal entity name appears on each applicable COI.
* If the client account is configured in {{PROPERTY_ENTITY}} mode, the system must validate that the associated property's {{legal_entity_name}} appears on each applicable COI.
* If {{PROPERTY_ENTITY}} mode is active but no property legal entity name is configured, the system must log a configuration warning and fall back to {{CLIENT_ENTITY}} mode for that evaluation.

*AC3 – Multi-COI Compliance Evaluation*

* The system must accept one or more COI documents as a single submission set for a given vendor/property pairing.
* Upon submission or re-evaluation, the system evaluates the full document set collectively and determines overall compliance status across all submitted COIs.
* For each applicable policy type, the system checks:
** *Coverage presence:* The required policy type exists on at least one COI in the set ({{is_present = true}}).
** *Limit thresholds:* The COI carrying the relevant policy meets or exceeds ({{>=}}) the client-configured minimum for each required limit field.
** *Endorsements:* The required endorsement is present ({{= true}}) on the COI carrying the relevant policy.
** *Coverage flags:* The required coverage flag is active ({{= true}}) on the COI carrying the relevant policy.
** *Self-insured retention:* SIR on the relevant COI does not exceed ({{<=}}) the client-configured maximum.
** *Global fields (per COI):* Each document in the submission set individually satisfies certificate holder name(s) per AC2, 30-day cancellation notice minimum (10 days for non-payment), carrier AM Best rating, and carrier financial size requirements.
* The audit log must record which COI in the submission set satisfied (or failed) each individual rule.

*AC4 – Failure Classification* Each compliance failure must be classified into one of three categories:

* *Missing Policy* – No COI in the submission set carries a required policy type.
* *Insufficient Limit* – A policy is present on one or more COIs but the applicable limit falls below the required threshold.
* *Missing Coverage or Endorsement* – A required endorsement, coverage flag, or certificate holder requirement is absent, incorrect, or false on the relevant COI.

*AC5 – Notification*

* When one or more compliance failures are detected across the submission set, the system must send an email notification to configured recipients (e.g., vendor contact, client or user who requested it).
* The notification must include:
** Vendor/service provider name
** Total number of COIs evaluated in the submission set
** A summary of each failure, including the rule type, field, required value, actual value found (or "not present"), and which COI the failure was found on (identified by document name or index)
** The resolved certificate holder requirement (Connexus + client or property entity, as applicable) if that validation failed
** A timestamp of the evaluation
** A copy of each original COI submitted
* If the full submission set is compliant, no failure notification is sent; a compliance confirmation event must be logged.

*AC6 – Audit & Logging*

* Located on the Vendor tab under "Audit Log."
* Every compliance evaluation must be logged with: timestamp, submission set ID, list of COI document IDs evaluated, vendor ID, client ID, property ID (if applicable), certificate holder mode used, rule set version, and a pass/fail result per rule — including which document in the set the result was drawn from.
* Logs must be queryable by client, vendor, property, policy type, and date range.



----



*Out of Scope*

* Manual override of compliance decisions (tracked separately)
* OCR/parsing of raw PDF certificates (assumed handled by upstream ingestion service)
* Rule set versioning and change history UI (tracked separately)



----



*Dependencies*

* Certificate ingestion and parsing service must return structured data mapped to the field paths defined in the rule library, and must support grouping multiple parsed COIs into a single submission set
* Client account model must support {{certificate_holder_mode}} and property-level {{legal_entity_name}} fields before AC2 can be evaluated
* Client rule configuration UI or API must be in place for rule values to exist at evaluation time



----



*Definition of Done*

* All AC items pass QA testing with representative test submissions including: single COI (compliant), single COI (non-compliant), multi-COI set (collectively compliant), and multi-COI set (partially non-compliant)
* Unit tests cover each rule type and operator ({{>=}}, {{=}}, {{<=}}), including certificate holder mode resolution and cross-document rule attribution
* Connexus platform-level defaults are verified as non-overridable in all test scenarios
* Email notification delivery confirmed end-to-end in staging, including correct per-document failure attribution and attachment of all submitted COIs
* Evaluation logs capture submission set ID, all document IDs, property ID, and certificate holder mode correctly
* Configuration warning for missing property legal entity name is surfaced to client admin in staging

column1: Ability to resend the invite by editing contact
column31:
h2. User Story

*As a* user managing vendor compliance, *I want to* resend an invite from the Vendor Compliance page with the ability to edit the original invite details, *so that* I can update the point of contact (POC) and reissue the invite when needed.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

h3. 1. General Behavior

* Selecting *"Resend Invite"* opens a dialog to update the vendor contact.
* The dialog contains the following fields: *First Name, Last Name, Email ID, Phone Number*.
* The user can either *select an existing contact* (e.g., existing first name) or *create a new contact*.
* Resend is supported for an existing vendor in two ways:
** Resend to the *same / existing contact* (same email again), or
** Resend to a *new contact*. 

Common flow for both paths: *Resend button → open form → edit contact → send email → recipient opens the mailed link.* 
After Resent the status of the record should change to email Send
from all the status,status should change to email send

h3. 2. Resend to an Existing Contact

* Same email will be triggered to the vendor contact.
* link will open the registeration page with prefill data, ssn and DOB blank ([~accountid:63c8e40fd579d7c687552750] technically this should be TIN, no?)
* The mail contains the previous link. When opened, it resolves to a *new link* and the *registration process starts fresh (newly).*

h3. 3. Resend to a New Contact

Behavior depends on where the vendor was in the process:

||Registration Stage||Link Behavior||Data Behavior||
|*Registration not completed*|Opening the mailed link generates a *new link*; registration restarts fresh.
recent status : need to have a resend status  from FE  :|Prefill from the client invite. *SSN and DOB blank*|
|*Payment not completed*|Opening the mailed link generates a *new link*; registration restarts fresh.
recent status : email sent if the intialstatus was email sent or Email opened|Prefill from the client invite. *SSN and DOB blank*|
|*Payment completed, KYB in process*|Opening the mailed link *continues the previous data* entered by the earlier contact and resumes the KYB process.|The new contact gets a *retry option* to change the existing data.count set it as zero|
|*Payment completed, KYB completed*|Hide Resend button|Hide resend button|

h3. 4. Resend Disabled

* The *Resend* action is disabled/hide when {{businessVerified = yes}} *OR* {{vendorInvited = no}},Business verified =Requirement not met and Exempt

h3. 5. Case 1 — Vendor Contact Edited (Name, Email, or Phone)

* When the vendor contact is changed, the updated invite is sent to the *new contact*.
* The link previously sent to the *earlier contact becomes inaccessible*.
* The *previous vendor contact still appears* under the Vendor Contact tab for registered vendor
* The user *can remove* the previous contact from the Vendor Contact page if it is no longer needed.
* The *newly added vendor contact is added* to the Vendor Contact page.
* Resend and invite send should be added in the Audit log.

column1: Vendor Compliance Flow: Vendor Invite workflow
column31:
User story

*As a* client user,
*I want* to invite a vendor to the platform by searching for an existing company or creating a new one,
*so that* I can onboard new vendors efficiently and ensure all relevant business details are captured before sending the invitation.

h2. *Vendor Invite Workflow*

When a client logs into the platform, they can access the Vendor Module. This module displays only vendors associated with that specific client.

The vendor list includes:

* Current and Draft vendors (from contract extraction)
* Preferred Vendors (predefined in the client module)
* *Vendor List View*

Each vendor record displays the following fields:

* Vendor Name
* Services
* State Serviced : - states belong to the propertie 
* 
* Business Verified
* Required License
* Compliance Status
* Vendor Status: Active,inactive,draft

h2. *Vendor Actions*

Each vendor row includes an action menu with context-based options:

Users can open vendor details by selecting the vendor name. Only client-specific data such as insurance and notes will be visible.

h2. *Vendor Invite Workflow*

When the user selects “Invite Vendor,” a form is presented to capture vendor details.

h3. *Fields*

* Company Name (Dropdown + manual entry, required)
** Existing vendors auto-populate
** New vendors can be created
* Company Legal Name (required)
* Services (required) : 
Client invited vendors >serivces should be visible in the list page. 
not invited vendors > default vendor services should be visible. 
* Property coverage : yes or NO 
* Property dropdown field
* Primary Contact Information
** First Name (required)
** Last Name (required)
** Email Address (required)
** Phone Number (required)

h3. *Actions*

* Send Invite
* Cancel

# *Navigation and Trigger*
#* When the client clicks the *“Invite Vendor”* button from the _Vendors_ page, the system navigates to the *Company Search* screen.
#* The screen displays a search bar labeled "Search Company".
# *Search and Existing Vendor Results*
#* As the client types in the search bar, the system searches existing vendors in the Connexus database.
#* If matches are found:
#** The system displays a list of suggestions showing:
#*** Company Name
#*** Legal Name
#*** Website
#*** Address
#** The user can select one vendor from the list.
#* Upon selecting an existing vendor:
#** Clicking *Continue* proceeds to the *Invite Vendor Details* page.
#** All vendor-related data (name, legal name, website, etc.) are *auto-populated*.
#** The user can review and modify optional fields (services, coverage, contact info, etc.).
# *Creating a New Vendor*
#* If no match is found in the search results, the client can create a *new vendor*.
#* The client can manually enter the company name in the text input under _“Create as a New Vendor”_ and click *Continue*.
#* The system navigates to the *Invite Vendor Details* page.
#* Only the *Company Name* field is prefilled; other fields (Legal Name, Website, Services, Coverage, Contact Info) remain blank for entry.
# *Invite Vendor Details Page*
#* The form includes the following fields:
#** Company Name (read-only if selected from search)
#** Company Legal Name
#** Website
#** Services Requiring Insurance (multi-select dropdown)
#** Property Level Coverage (Yes/No option)
#** Properties (multi-select)
#** Primary Contact Details: First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone Number
#* All mandatory fields are marked with an asterisk (*).
# *Validation Rules*
#* Required fields cannot be left empty.
#* Email and phone number must be in valid format.
#* The “Invite” button remains disabled until all required fields are completed.
# *Invitation Confirmation*
#* Clicking *Invite* validates all inputs.
#* If valid, an invitation is sent to the vendor’s primary contact email.
#* 
#* *Cancellation*
#* Clicking *Cancel* at any stage returns the user to the _Vendors_ page without saving any data.

*Definition of Done*

* The end-to-end flow supports both selecting existing vendors and creating new ones.
* All mandatory fields are validated with appropriate error handling.
* Invitations trigger correctly and the vendor list reflects updates upon completion.
* UI elements align with provided screens and interaction flow.

Functional Requirements

* If the Property Level Coverage is set to “Yes”, all properties under the client will be displayed, and the user should be able to select the required properties.
* The states corresponding to the selected properties should be automatically stored under State Coverage. This will be handled from the backend and will not be displayed or managed in the frontend UI

column1: FE - PDF template editor Phase 1 (viewer, overlays, mock recipients)
column31:
Parallel to the DOCX/HTML contract flow, we need a PDF-based template path where the PDF is read-only and recipient signing fields (Signature, Text, Date, Initials) are placed as overlays with page + percentage-based coordinates. Phase 1 is frontend-only: local/mock data and console payload; no BE integration (Phase 2).

Scope:
* Add PDF template editor route and register permissions (ClientManagement), e.g. /contracts/pdf-template-editor
* Render PDF with react-pdf (pdf.js worker configured for Vite)
* Per-page overlay: HTML5 drag-and-drop from FieldsSidebar (recipients mode) onto each page; compute xPercent/yPercent from overlay bounds; default chip sizes from pdfTypes
* Placeholder chips: recipient colour coding, reposition within page (mouse), delete on hover X
* Zoom toolbar (+/-/reset) with scale-independent chip positions (percentage coordinates)
* Orchestrator page: mock recipients, placeholders state, build PdfSavePayload (pdfPlaceholders + recipientFieldsUpdates with htmlFieldId pattern recipientId_fieldType_uniqueId)
* Save Draft / Send for Signature: log full payload to console (Phase 1); toast on send path as per existing header pattern
* Types in pdfTypes.ts (PdfPlaceholderPosition, PdfRecipient, PdfSavePayload, DEFAULT_CHIP_SIZES)
* Styles in pdfEditor.style.css for viewer, toolbar, page container, drop overlay, chips

Acceptance Criteria:
* User can open the PDF template editor route and see a PDF loaded from public static asset (sample.pdf for dev)
* User selects a mock recipient and drags Signature, Text, Date, and Initials from the sidebar onto any page; chip appears at drop position with correct recipient colours
* User can reposition a chip within its page and delete it via hover affordance
* Zoom in/out/reset keeps chips aligned with the page (percentage-based layout)
* Save Draft and Send for Signature output a payload in DevTools including pdfPlaceholders (id, recipientId, fieldType, pageNumber, x/y/width/height percents) and recipientFieldsUpdates consistent with existing Stage 2 grouping
* Implementation aligns with internal guide: src/features/contractSigning/PDF_TEMPLATE_EDITOR_GUIDE.md (Phase 1 sections)

* Subsequent signature fields:

column1: Phase 1: Support parent-child policy creation from new AI data model (Webhook Processing)
column31:
h2. Summary

ContextualAI has introduced a new structured data model for insurance policy extraction. Instead of producing a single flat policy per document upload, the new model introduces a mainPolicy object that can contain multiple childPolicies — each representing an individual coverage line (e.g., General Liability, Property, Umbrella, D&O, Crime).

This task implements the Phase 1 changes: the initial policy creation flow during webhook processing to support the parent-child policy structure.
h2. 

h2. Scope

h3. Database Schema Changes
* Add a self-referencing parentId column to InsurancePolicy (nullable FK to itself) to establish parent-child relationships
* Change the policyLimit column type from Float to Json to store raw AI-extracted limit data as-is
* Generate and apply the Prisma migration
* Verify existing data integrity — all existing policies should have parentId = null after migration
* Verify existing policyLimit Float values are properly migrated to Json format

h3. Coverage Type Enum Expansion
* Add new coverage type entries to the policy type enum mapping to support child-level values: Property, D&O, Directors & Officers Liability, Crime, Crime/Fidelity, Cyber Liability, Commercial Auto, Workers Compensation
* Extend the policy type mapping function to resolve child policy coverageType strings to the correct enum values

h3. Parent Policy Creation (from webhook)
* On receiving a completed insurance policy webhook with the new mainPolicy structure, create a parent InsurancePolicy record with:
  * Its own unique policy code
  * Policy type derived from the top-level document type
  * Policy limits and deductibles stored as raw JSON (no transformation or normalization)
  * Expiry date from the main policy object
  * parentId set to null
* Create the parent's CompliancesProperty record with extracted insured name and address
* Attach the uploaded compliance file to the parent's CompliancesProperty
* Create InsurancePolicyLocation records from the main policy's locations array

h3. Child Policy Creation (from webhook)
* For each child policy in the childPolicies array, create a child InsurancePolicy record with:
  * Its own independently generated unique policy code
  * Policy type derived from the child's coverageType field
  * Policy limits and deductibles stored as raw JSON (no transformation)
  * Its own expiry date (may differ from parent)
  * parentId linking to the parent InsurancePolicy
  * Independent version starting at 1
  * Shared fields inherited from the parent: policy number, compliance status, agency, annual premium, tenant, client, background job reference
* Create a CompliancesProperty record for each child with the same extracted name and address as the parent
* Attach the same compliance file to each child's CompliancesProperty
* Create InsurancePolicyLocation records from each child's locations array (if present)

h3. Deductibles and Limits Storage Change
* Stop normalizing/transforming deductibles for the new data model flow — store the raw AI output directly in the database
* Store policy limits as raw JSON for both parent and child policies
* Parent limits arrive as array-of-arrays format; child limits arrive as flat array format — both stored as-is

h3. Background Job Update
* After creating parent and all child policies, update the background job status to Pending for Approval
* Store only the parent policy ID as the background job's resultId (children are discoverable via parentId)

h3. Backward Compatibility
* If the webhook payload does not contain the new mainPolicy structure (older AI model output), fall back to the existing single-policy creation logic
* Ensure the old flat data model continues to work without any regression

h3. Property Matching Behavior
* Property matching is performed only on the parent policy
* When a parent policy is matched to a property, all child policies must also be finalized (set to non-draft) in the same operation

h3. Transaction Handling
* Wrap the entire parent + child creation flow (including CompliancesProperty, ComplianceFile, and location records) within a single database transaction to ensure atomicity
h2. 

h2. Verification & Testing
* Unit Tests for the updated policy creation method covering:
  * New data model with parent + multiple child policies
  * Old data model fallback (no mainPolicy in payload)
  * Edge case: mainPolicy present but childPolicies is empty or absent
  * Correct coverage type enum resolution for all new child-level values
  * Policy limits and deductibles stored as raw JSON without transformation
  * Each child gets its own unique policy code and independent version
* Data Model Comparison Verification — validate the mapping between the new AI output fields and the database columns for:
  * Parent policy field mapping (policy number, expiry, limits, deductibles, coverage type)
  * Child policy field mapping (coverage type, limits, deductibles, expiry, parent linkage)
  * Location records mapping for both parent and child
  * CompliancesProperty and ComplianceFile attachment for all policies
* Database Constraint Verification — confirm the unique(policyCode, version) constraint is not violated since each child has its own unique policy code
* Migration Verification — run migration on a copy of production data and verify:
  * All existing policies get parentId = null
  * Existing policyLimit Float values convert correctly to Json
  * No data loss on existing deductibles (already Json, shape change is forward-only)
* Integration / E2E Testing — test end-to-end with a sample webhook payload containing the new data model and verify the correct number of records are created with the right relationships
h2. 

h2. Out of Scope (Phase 2)
* API changes for list, edit, endorsement, reupload, delete, and export
* Property matching API updates for parent-child awareness
* Frontend changes to display parent-child policy hierarchy
* Detailed reupload handling for parent-child version coordination
h2. 

h2. Notes
* A single document upload can now produce 1 parent + N child policies (e.g., a Package Policy with 5 coverage lines produces 6 InsurancePolicy records)
* The parent-child relationship is established solely via parentId — policy codes are fully independent
* The compliance file is shared across all policies (parent and children) via separate ComplianceFile rows pointing to the same physical file

# User A receives the signing email.
# User A forwards the email to User B.
# User B opens the email and clicks the signing link.
# Observe whether User B is able to access and sign the contract.

h3. *Expected Result*

* Only the *intended recipient (User A)* should be able to sign the contract.
* Forwarded recipients (User B) should *not* be able to sign.

h3. *Actual Result*

* Forwarded recipient is  able to access and sign the contract using the same link.

column1: Phase 2: API endpoint changes for parent-child policy model
column31:
h2. Summary

Phase 1 ([CX-3087]) implemented the initial parent-child policy creation flow during webhook processing — creating parent + child InsurancePolicy records with the new structured data model from ContextualAI. Phase 2 covers all the API-level changes required for the existing property insurance endpoints to correctly handle parent and child policies across list, edit, delete, endorsement, property matching, and export flows.

Prerequisite: Phase 1 ([CX-3087]) must be completed first.

Plan Document: docs/PLAN-new-ai-data-model-phase2-api-changes.md

h2. Scope

h3. Delete Policy — Cascade to Children

* When deleting a parent policy by policyCode, also find and delete all child policies (via parentId) along with their compliance data, files, background jobs, and storage files
* Deleting a child policy by its policyCode deletes only that child — not the parent or siblings
* Call softDeletePoliciesByPolicyCode for each unique policyCode in the expanded deletion set (parent + all children)

h3. Delete Background Job — Cascade to Children

* When deleting a background job, find the parent policy via resultId, then find all children by parentId
* Soft-delete the entire policy tree (parent + all children) along with their compliance data, files, and background jobs
* Same cascade pattern as Delete Policy — collect all unique policyCode values and soft-delete each

h3. Get Policy by ID — Include Parent Reference

* Add parentId to the raw SQL SELECT statement so the frontend can identify whether a returned policy is a parent or child
* No inline childPolicies array — frontend fetches children separately via the list endpoint with parentId filter

h3. Compliance Status Counts — Parents Only

* Add parentId: null to the where clause in getComplianceStatusCounts() to avoid inflated counts
* Without this filter, a single document upload producing 1 parent + 5 children would count as 6 policies instead of 1

h3. Property Matching Data — Child Count Summary

* Include childPolicyCount in the property matching response returned by getPropertyMatchingByBackgroundJobId()
* Provides context to the user like "5 child policies will be matched with the selected property"

h3. List Background Jobs — Child Count Enhancement

* Optionally include the parent policy's child count in the background job list response so the UI can indicate how many child policies a job produced

h3. Main APIs and Helpers

* Submit Property Match: Reject match on child policy; cascade isDraft: false + match metadata to children; remove old policyCode demotion logic; soft-delete previous policy tree via prePolicyId
* buildNewPolicyData(): Carry forward parentId in edit/endorsement versioning
* Edit Policy: Preserve parentId; when editing a parent, update all children's parentId to point to new parent version
* Create Endorsement: Same as Edit Policy — preserve parentId + update children's parentId to new parent version
* List Policies: Add parentId to SELECT; default WHERE parentId IS NULL (parents only); remove policyLimit numeric filter/sort (type changed to JSON array-of-arrays); add _count.childPolicies correlated subquery; add optional parentId query parameter to GetInsurancePoliciesDto for listing children

h2. Key Decisions

||*#*||*Decision*||
|D2|Deleting a child by its policyCode deletes only that child — not the parent or siblings|
|D7|Compliance counts reflect only parent policies (parentId IS NULL)|
|D8|Get-by-ID returns flat response — no inline childPolicies array; frontend fetches children separately|
|D9|Property matching response includes child policy count summary|
|D10|Export behavior deferred — decision pending|
|D11|Child complianceStatus is independent from parent — no cascading|
|D13|Include _count.childPolicies in list response via correlated subquery|

h2. Verification & Testing

* Unit Tests:
* Delete Policy — verify deleting a parent cascades to all children; verify deleting a child does not affect parent or siblings
* Delete Background Job — verify cascade finds parent from resultId, discovers children via parentId, and deletes entire tree
* Get Policy by ID — verify parentId is included in response for both parent and child policies
* Compliance Status Counts — verify counts exclude child policies when parentId: null filter is applied
* Property Matching Data — verify childPolicyCount is correctly returned
* Edge Cases:
* Delete a parent with no children — should work identically to current behavior
* Delete a child whose parent has other children — siblings and parent must remain untouched
* Compliance counts with mixed parent/child policies — only parents should be counted
* Get Policy by ID for a child — should return the child with its parentId populated
* Integration / E2E Testing:
* End-to-end delete flow: create parent + children via webhook, then delete parent and verify entire tree is soft-deleted
* End-to-end delete flow: create parent + children, delete one child, verify parent and other children remain
* Verify compliance counts before and after parent-child policy creation

h2. Out of Scope

* Frontend changes to display parent-child policy hierarchy

column1: PDF signing apis
column31: {noformat}# E-Sign FE Signing Contract ## Overview Frontend signing uses two endpoints: 1. `GET /contract-signers/view?token=...` 2. `POST /contract-signers/sign?token=...` The `token` comes from the signer email link and must be sent as a query parameter on both requests. ## FE Flow 1. Read the signer link and extract the `token`. 2. Call `GET /contract-signers/view?token=...`. 3. Render the document from the response. 4. Render only the current signer's fields. 5. Capture user input for each field. 6. Echo `consentText` and `disclosureText` back exactly as received. 7. Submit the signing payload to `POST /contract-signers/sign?token=...`. ## View Response The `view` API gives FE the document plus the signing metadata needed to render the signing UI. Expected response shape: ```json { "documentHtml": "...", "documentUrl": "https://...", "signer": { "id": "signer-id", "fullName": "John Doe", "email": "john@example.com", "signingOrder": 1, "status": "VIEWED" }, "signedRecord": { "id": "signed-record-id", "status": "PENDING", "consentText": "Consent text...", "disclosureText": "Disclosure text..." }, "signers": [ { "id": "signer-id", "fullName": "John Doe", "email": "john@example.com", "signingOrder": 1, "status": "VIEWED", "signerFields": { "colour": { "bg": "#FFF7CC", "text": "#111111", "border": "#D4AF37" }, "fields": [ { "id": "signer1_signature", "fieldType": "signature", "htmlFieldId": "abc-123_signature_r7ncc", "pageNumber": 1, "xPercent": 10, "yPercent": 20, "widthPercent": 20, "heightPercent": 5 } ] } } ] } ``` ## Important Fields For FE From `signers[].signerFields.fields[]`, FE should use: - `id`: backend field identifier to send back in `customData` - `fieldType`: usually `signature` or `text` - `htmlFieldId`: field anchor for HTML documents - `pageNumber`: PDF page number - `xPercent`: PDF horizontal position - `yPercent`: PDF vertical position - `widthPercent`: PDF field width - `heightPercent`: PDF field height ## Sign Request Body Expected request body: ```json { "customData": [ { "id": "field-id", "value": "some value", "fieldType": "signature" } ], "consentText": "exact text from view response", "disclosureText": "exact text from view response" } ``` ## `customData` Rules - `id` must match the field `id` from the `view` response. - `value` is the entered or generated field value. - `fieldType` is optional at DTO level, but required for PDF signing. - For PDF, use `fieldType: "signature"` or `fieldType: "text"`. ## Signature Value Format ### PDF Documents For PDF signature fields, FE should send a base64 image data URL: ```json { "id": "signer1_signature", "value": "data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0K...", "fieldType": "signature" } ``` For PDF text fields: ```json { "id": "signer1_name", "value": "John Doe", "fieldType": "text" } ``` ### HTML Documents For HTML signature placeholders, FE should send an HTML image string: ```json { "id": "signer1_signature", "value": "" } ``` For HTML text fields: ```json { "id": "signer1_name", "value": "John Doe" } ``` ## Consent And Disclosure Rules - FE must send `consentText` exactly as returned by `GET /contract-signers/view`. - FE must send `disclosureText` exactly as returned by `GET /contract-signers/view`. - If either value changes, backend rejects the signing request. ## What FE Does Not Need To Send FE does not need to send: - IP address - user agent - signer ID - signed record ID Those are resolved by the backend from the token and request metadata. ## Sign Response Expected success response: ```json { "signatureEventId": "signature-event-id", "signedRecordStatus": "PARTIALLY_SIGNED", "isCompleted": false } ``` ## FE Checklist - Keep the `token` from the email link. - Call `view` before showing the signing form. - Use only the current signer's fields. - Send field `id` values exactly as provided. - For PDF signing, include `fieldType` on every `customData` item. - For PDF signature fields, send a base64 data URL. - For HTML signature fields, send an `` string. - Echo `consentText` and `disclosureText` without modification. {noformat}

column1: FE - PDF template editor Phase 2 (API integration, signing view, signed record)
column31:
Phase 2 wires the PDF template editor (Phase 1) to real backend APIs, adds the PDF signing view for recipients, and handles signed-record PDF viewing. The same endpoints used by the DOCX flow are reused — the backend detects PDF vs DOCX from the storageUri extension. No new API endpoints are needed.

Scope:
* Extend existing API types to support PDF fields: add position properties (pageNumber, xPercent, yPercent, widthPercent, heightPercent) to RecipientField, add documentUrl to view/signed-record responses, add PdfSignCustomDataItem with fieldType
* Build captureSignatureAsImage utility (signatureCapture.ts): render typed signature to hidden canvas using Alex Brush font at 3x scale, export as PNG base64 data URL
* Allow .pdf file selection in UploadContractModal (alongside .docx); same upload endpoint, BE detects type from extension
* Replace mock data in PdfTemplateEditorPage: real recipients from useGetESignTemplateByIdQuery, real PDF URL from documentUrl, templateId from URL params, loading/error states
* Wire Save Draft to API: send coordinate-based recipientFieldsUpdates (positions embedded inside recipientFields items — no separate pdfPlaceholders array, no htmlContent for PDF)
* Wire Send for Signature: call existing mutation, navigate to /connexus-e-sign?tab=1 on success
* Add PDF vs DOCX detection: check docTemplate.fileType on template details; check documentUrl vs documentHtml on view/signed-record responses
* Build PdfSigningView (new component set): PdfSigningView orchestrator, PdfSigningDocumentViewer (read-only PDF + signing chip overlays), PdfSigningChip (clickable chips for current signer only)
* PdfSigningView handles: field input via shared FieldInputModal, consent via shared ConsentModal, decline via shared DeclineSigning; at submit time convert signature fields to base64 PNG via captureSignatureAsImage, send fieldType on every customData item
* Build SigningViewPage orchestrator: detect PDF vs HTML from documentUrl, render PdfSigningView or HtmlSigningView accordingly
* Handle PDF in signed-record viewing (ViewDocumentModal): if documentUrl is present render PdfSigningDocumentViewer in readOnly mode; if html is present render RemirrorHtmlEditor as before
* Shared signing components extracted to signing-shared/: ConsentModal, FieldInputModal, DeclineSigning, ErrorView (reused by both HTML and PDF flows)

Acceptance Criteria:
* Admin can upload a .pdf file via UploadContractModal and the system creates a PDF template (no HTML conversion, documentUrl returned)
* Admin opens the PDF template editor with real recipients from API; PDF renders from pre-signed S3 URL (not local sample.pdf)
* Save Draft persists coordinate-based field positions via existing draft endpoint (no htmlContent sent for PDF); fields restore on re-open
* Send for Signature triggers signing emails; recipients receive valid signing links
* Signer opens signing link → SigningViewPage detects PDF → renders PdfSigningView with the PDF and positioned signing chips for the current signer only
* Signer can click chips to fill fields (FieldInputModal), see Alex Brush font preview for signatures, and see filled values on chips
* Signer completes consent checkbox, clicks Sign Document; signature fields are converted to base64 PNG at submit time; payload includes fieldType on every customData item
* After all signers complete, signed record is viewable: ViewDocumentModal detects PDF and renders stamped PDF in readOnly PdfSigningDocumentViewer (signatures baked into PDF by BE)
* Download PDF works for PDF-based signed records (same endpoint, no changes needed)
* All detection logic works: docTemplate.fileType for editor routing, documentUrl for signer/viewer routing
* Implementation aligns with internal guide: src/features/contractSigning/PDF_TEMPLATE_EDITOR_GUIDE.md (Phase 2 sections)

column1: Report Module — SRG Contract Report with Visibility-Based Property Filtering
column31:
h2. Overview

Build a *Report Module* within Connexus that serves as the platform's centralized reporting engine. The first report available in this module will be the *SRG Weekly Contract Report*, which is currently generated manually via a Claude Team Project workflow. This ticket covers productizing that workflow into the Connexus application itself.

----

h2. Background & Current State

Today, a team member (Tariq, or Jam/Janelle as backup) uploads a backend-exported Excel file every Tuesday morning into a Claude Team Project. That project then:

# Splits the data into individual reports per *VP* and per *Regional Manager (RM)*
# VP reports include all properties across all RMs under that VP
# RM reports include only properties assigned to that specific RM
# Prepares email drafts from reports@joinconnexus.com with the formatted reports attached
# Emails are sent at 10:00 AM EST with a standard subject line: _SRG Contract Update — [Date]_

This process needs to move into Connexus as a self-service report module.

----

h2. Core Requirements

h3. 1. Report Module (Platform Feature)

* Create a new *Reports* section/module in the Connexus application
* The SRG Contract Report will be the first report type available in this module
* Design the module to be extensible so additional report types can be added for other clients/use cases in the future

h3. 2. Visibility-Based Property Filtering (Critical Requirement)

* *Reports must only show properties that the logged-in user currently has visibility on in the system*
* A VP should see all properties across their assigned Regional Managers
* A Regional Manager should see only their own assigned properties
* Property visibility must be driven by the user's existing permissions/role assignments in Connexus — not by a separate configuration
* If a user's property assignments change, their report output should reflect that change immediately

h3. 3. Report Generation

* The report should pull from the same backend contract data that is currently exported to Excel
* Match the formatting, layout, and column structure of the original Excel export, including a title row with the current date
* Support on-demand generation (user clicks to generate their report) and/or scheduled weekly generation (Tuesdays)
* Handle name normalization — if a person's name appears inconsistently (e.g., trailing spaces, line breaks), normalize and treat as the same person

h3. 4. Email Distribution

* Support automated email distribution of individual reports
* Emails sent from *reports@joinconnexus.com*
* Subject line format: *SRG Contract Update — [Date]*
* Body: Professional note informing the recipient their weekly contract report is attached
* Footer line in every email: _For any questions or concerns about this report, please contact support@joinconnexus.com_
* Emails should be scheduled/sent at *10:00 AM EST* on Tuesdays
* CC logic: Support configurable CC recipients (initially Susan Whitney, Jason Gherardini, Meghan Shearer for first distribution, then removed)

h3. 5. Validation & Error Handling

* Never skip generating a report for any person found in the data
* Flag any anomalies — missing data, unrecognized names, or unclear assignments — before sending
* Provide a confirmation/review step showing how many reports were generated and how many emails are queued before sending

----

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* A Report Module section exists in the Connexus UI
* SRG Contract Report is available as the first report type
* Report output respects the logged-in user's property visibility — users only see properties they are assigned to
* VP-level reports aggregate all properties across their RMs
* RM-level reports show only that RM's assigned properties
* Report formatting matches the existing Excel export layout
* Automated email distribution works with correct subject, body, sender, and scheduling
* Name normalization handles inconsistent data entries
* Review/confirmation step before emails are sent
* Module is architected to support future report types beyond SRG

----

h2. Stakeholders

* *SRG Contacts:* Susan Whitney, Jason Gherardini, Meghan Shearer
* *Connexus Team:* Tariq (primary uploader), Jam, Janelle (backups)
* *Support:* support@joinconnexus.com

column1: Bulk Contract Download by Property – One-Click PDF Export with Status Filters
column31:
h2. Summary

Implement a one-click bulk contract download feature that allows users to download all contracts from a single property (or multiple properties) as PDFs, with the ability to filter by contract status via a multi-select dropdown.

h2. Background

Users currently lack a streamlined way to export contracts in bulk. When a client or property manager needs to review, audit, or archive contracts for one or more properties, they must download them individually — which is time-consuming and error-prone at scale.

h2. Functional Requirements

h3. FR-1: Single Property – Bulk Contract Download

* Add a "Download Contracts" button on the Property Detail / Contracts view
* Clicking the button opens a multi-select dropdown with contract status filters:
** All
** Current
** Expired
** Expiring
** Renewed
** Terminated
** Rebidding
** Archived
* Selecting "All" auto-selects every status; deselecting "All" clears the selection
* Clicking "Download" initiates the download for all contracts matching the selected statuses
* Output format: PDF (one PDF per contract, bundled as a ZIP archive)

h3. FR-2: Multi-Property – Bulk Contract Download

* Add a multi-select property picker (or checkbox selection on a properties list view) that allows selecting multiple properties
* Once properties are selected, the same status filter dropdown (FR-1) becomes available
* Downloads are organized in a folder structure inside the ZIP:
** {{/{Property Name}/}} → individual contract PDFs
* A summary manifest (CSV or PDF) should be included at the root of the ZIP listing all downloaded contracts with metadata (property, vendor, status, expiration date)

h3. FR-3: Download Size & Performance Considerations

* *Estimate & warn*: Before initiating download, show an estimated file count and approximate size (e.g., "47 contracts, ~120 MB")
* *Size threshold*: If estimated download exceeds 500 MB, warn the user and suggest narrowing filters
* *Async processing*: Downloads exceeding a configurable threshold (e.g., 100 contracts or 200 MB) should be processed asynchronously:
** Show a progress indicator / toast notification
** Send an email notification with a secure, time-limited download link when the ZIP is ready
** Download link expires after 24 hours
* *Compression*: Use standard ZIP compression; consider splitting into multiple ZIPs if total exceeds 1 GB
* *Server-side streaming*: For smaller downloads, use server-side ZIP streaming to avoid loading the full archive into memory
* *Rate limiting*: Limit concurrent bulk download requests per user to prevent server overload (suggest: 2 concurrent, 10 per hour)

h2. Non-Functional Requirements

* *Security*: All download links must be authenticated; no public access to contract PDFs
* *Audit trail*: Log all bulk download events (user, timestamp, property/properties, filters applied, file count)
* *Permission-based*: Only users with appropriate property-level access can download contracts for that property
* *Timeout handling*: If ZIP generation exceeds 5 minutes, notify user and offer retry
* *Browser compatibility*: Support Chrome, Edge, Safari, Firefox (latest 2 versions)

h2. UI/UX Specifications

* Download button placement: Property detail page → Contracts tab → top-right action bar
* Multi-property access: Properties list view → checkbox column + "Bulk Actions" dropdown → "Download Contracts"
* Status filter: Multi-select dropdown with checkboxes, "All" toggle at top
* Progress: Modal or toast with progress bar for async downloads
* Confirmation dialog before initiating large downloads

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* User can download all contracts for a single property with one click using status filters
* User can select multiple properties and download contracts across all selected properties
* Download produces a ZIP file with organized folder structure (by property)
* Status filter supports: All, Current, Expired, Expiring, Renewed, Terminated, Rebidding, Archived
* System estimates and displays download size before initiating
* Downloads exceeding threshold are processed asynchronously with email notification
* Download links are secure, authenticated, and time-limited (24h expiry)
* Audit log captures all bulk download events
* Permission checks enforce property-level access control
* Summary manifest included in ZIP with contract metadata

column1: Improve drag-and-drop performance in Template Editor for large documents
column31:
h3. Problem

When working with large HTML documents (50+ pages) in the Template Editor, dragging fields from the sidebar and dropping them into the editor causes severe lag (30–40 seconds). The editor freezes while trying to resolve the cursor position and insert the field.

h3. Root Cause

During drag, the editor was performing full HTML serialisation of the entire document on every mouse movement event (~60 times per second). Additionally, there were duplicate cursor-tracking handlers both running the same expensive position calculations.

h3. What Was Done

_Skipped unnecessary document serialisation during drag_ — The editor now detects when only the cursor position changed (no actual content edits) and skips the expensive full-document HTML conversion. This eliminates the majority of the lag.

_Removed duplicate cursor-tracking logic_ — Two separate handlers were both computing the cursor position on every mouse move. Consolidated to a single handler to halve the overhead.

_Throttled cursor position updates_ — Limited cursor position calculations to ~16 times per second instead of 60, which is visually smooth but significantly reduces work on large documents.

_Added "Placing field" loading indicator_ — A small visual indicator now appears at the top-right of the editor container while dragging a field over the editor, giving the user feedback that the operation is in progress.

Files Changed

* {{RemirrorHtmlEditor.tsx}}
* {{PlaceholderFieldExtension.ts}}
* {{TemplateEditorPage.tsx}}
* {{REMIRROR_EDITOR_GUIDE.md}} (developer docs updated)

FE only needs a thin *token-exchange page*.

Add a route at {{'/e-sign/document'}} because the backend now sends email links in that shape. That page should:

# Read {{token}} from the query string.
# If missing, show an “invalid link” state immediately.
# Call the public backend endpoint:
#* {{GET /contract-signers/document-url?token=<token>}}
# On {{200}}, read {{{ url }}} and redirect the browser to it.
# On failure, show a friendly state based on status.

The backend contract you need to consume is now:

* public endpoint: {{GET /contract-signers/document-url}}
* query param: {{token}}
* success response: {{{ url: string }}}

Useful error handling on FE:

* {{401}}: invalid or expired link
* {{404}}: document or token record not found
* {{410}}: link revoked or document voided
* {{409}}: PDF snapshot not ready yet The existing backend exception shape includes {{code}}, {{message}}, and {{retryAfter}}, so FE can show “document is still being prepared, try again in X seconds”.

What I’d build on the FE side:

* a simple loading screen while calling the API
* a success redirect with {{window.location.assign(url)}}
* an error screen with messages for the statuses above
* optional retry button for {{409}}

What FE does *not* need:

* no auth/session requirement
* no JWT verification client-side
* no long-term token storage
* no direct S3 signing logic
