column1: Vendor Compliance workflow for Sole Proprietor company type
column31:
Summary : 

h3. User Story: Vendor SSN Verification, EIDV Advance, and AML Workflow

As a invited vendor, I want to complete my company and owner verification process through SSN (US Tin Verification API) and AML verification so that my business can be verified and approved within the platform.

h4. Description

When a client invites a vendor, the vendor will receive an email invitation containing a verification link. Upon clicking the link, the vendor will be redirected to a verification form where they can enter or confirm the following- 
+ALL FIELDS ARE REQUIRED+

# Company Name- Add a tooltip, “Company Name or DBA”
# Company Legal Name
# Company Type. When the Company Type is:  Sole Proprietorships, the form will show the following fields:
# Checkbox: “We have a website”
#* If checked, a website field opens
# Website
# Business Street Address
# Business City
# Business County
# Business State — two-letter abbreviation
# Business ZIP Code —   5 digits
# Checkbox: “Residential address is different from business address”
# Residential Street Address
# Residential City
# Residential State — two-letter abbreviation
# Residential ZIP Code — 6 digits
# Owner Details — First Name
# Owner Details — Last Name
# Owner Email Address
# Owner Phone Number
# Owner Date of Birth — MM/DD/YYYY
# Owner SSN — encrypted- 9 digits in this format xxx-xx-xxxx

At the bottom of the form I can “Cancel” the action or Click the “Next” button.  

On the left I will be required to check a box that says, “I agree to the terms and conditions”.  This box will contain a hyperlink to the terms and conditions that I can view if I would like but I am not required to do so.

After clicking “Next”, I have to  I am redirected to Stripe to complete my payment through Stripe.  After successful payment, Stripe will initiate the EIDV advance  through Signzy API. The verification will validate the combination of First Name, Last Name, Date of Birth, SSN, and Residential Address (or Business Address if they are the same).

EIDV advance will verify the combinations and provide a match. 

If there is a Failure, an email notification will be triggered to the user and they will be able to click on the link to redirect to the same status board for reentering the data. 

The vendor will have a maximum of 3 retry attempts. If the verification fails on the 4th attempt, the vendor status will remain failed and the “Business Verified” field for the vendor will be set to “Requirements Not Met”.  On the retry, the following fields will be provided and will be mandatory, First and Last Name, SSN, DOB, and Address.

After a successful EIDV Verification, the system will trigger the Signzy AML API.  If the Vendor Passes, meaning they are no matches on the AML List, then the Vendor will be Approved as Business Verified.  It will be saved in the Dashboard as “Yes”.
- If the vendor has kept the window open, the screen will say the vendor’s Business is Verified.
- The System will trigger Trigger 'Business Verified' notification (Requirements for this email are outlined in []).

If the Vendor fails the AML screening, they will receive a notification on the screening stating they have failed the process. Trigger 'Verification Failed' notification (Requirements for this email are outlined in []).

All payment transactions, subscriptions, and billing workflows will be handled through Stripe. No Stripe transaction or subscription management UI will be developed within Connexus as part of this scope.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

h3. Invitation & Access

# When a client or Connexus user invites a vendor, the system shall send an email invitation containing a verification link to the vendor’s email address.
# When the vendor clicks the verification link, the system shall open the vendor verification form.

h3. Vendor Verification Form

# The verification form shall contain fields for:
#* +ALL FIELDS ARE REQUIRED+
#*# Company Name- Add a tooltip, “Company Name or DBA”
#*# Company Legal Name
#*# Company Type
#*# Checkbox: “We have a website”
#*#* If checked, a website field opens
#*# Website
#*# Business Street Address
#*# Business City
#*# Business State — two-letter abbreviation
#*# Business ZIP Code — 6 digits
#*# Checkbox: “Residential address is different from business address”
#*# Residential Street Address
#*# Residential City
#*# Residential State — two-letter abbreviation
#*# Residential ZIP Code — 6 digits
#*# Owner Details — First Name
#*# Owner Details — Last Name
#*# Owner Email Address
#*# Owner Phone Number
#*# Owner Date of Birth — MM/DD/YYYY
#*# Owner SSN — encrypted
# The vendor shall be able to enter and update all required company and owner information.
# All mandatory fields shall be validated before submission.
# The SSN field shall support full SSN entry with encryption and validation format.

h3. Payment Workflow

# When the vendor clicks “Continue and Pay”, the system shall redirect the vendor to the Stripe payment workflow.
# No Stripe management UI shall be developed within Connexus as part of this implementation.

h3. SSN Verification Workflow

# After successful payment, the system shall initiate SSN verification using the Signzy API.
# The SSN verification shall validate the combination of:

* First Name
* Last Name
* Date of Birth
* SSN
* Address : (Residential address will be used to validate the SSN)

# If the verification match, the EIDV advance Verification- SSN verification status shall be marked as “Passed”.  It then calls the API to the AML checks via AML Dashboard.   
# If it the result from the EIDV Advance is not matched   then it returns failed and retrty window will be opened. user will have 3 times to retry and it will fed to the EIDV advance, if its still failed, Business verified =NO    The vendor sees this on their dashboard and receives a notification email.  

h3. Retry & Failure Handling

 EIDV ADVANCE API (only)  

# The vendor shall be allowed to retry the verification process by re-entering the required information. If they are on the screen it shows a Failed Status.If the advanced verification fails, the system shall display the status “Business Verification Failed”.
# The vendor shall be allowed to retry the verification process by re-entering the required information.  The system shall allow a maximum of 3 retry attempts.
## First Name
## Last Name
## Date of Birth
## SSN- 9 digit encrypted XXX-XX-XXXX
## Address : (Residential address will be used to validate the SSN)
# If the verification fails on the 4th attempt:

* The verification status shall remain “Failed”.
* The “Business Verified” field for the vendor shall be set to “Requirements Not Met”.
* The vendor shall not be allowed additional retry attempts.
*  If the businesses passes, it will go to the AML Verification process.

h3. AML Verification

# Upon successful  US TIN verification flow (through the EIDV Advance Flow, or the Retry flow), the system shall proceed with AML verification.
# If its matched then it goes into the AML Dashboard. the vendor shall be marked as “Business Verified = Yes”.
# If its Fails,The process stops and the vendor receives a Failed Notification.  If they are on the screen it shows a Failed Status.
# There will be no additional attempt allowed.

column1: Remove ‘In Contract’ Status and Align with New Awarded RFP Workflow
column31:
*Description:*
As per the updated workflow, the *‘In Contract’* status is no longer valid. The contract lifecycle is now fully managed under the *Awarded RFP* flow.

h3. *Current (Issue):*

* Properties still display *‘In Contract’* status in RFP Detail.
* *Generate Contract* button is visible on the RFP Detail page.
* Legacy records exist with *‘InContract’* status in the database.
* This creates inconsistency with the new workflow.

----

h3. *Expected Behavior (New Workflow):*

# Once a vendor is awarded → Property moves to *Awarded RFP tab* with status *Awarded*.
# User generates & sends contract → Status becomes *Sent*.
# Once signed → Status becomes *Completed*.

----

h3. *Required Changes:*

h4. *1. Data Migration / Handling Existing Records*

* Identify all records with status *‘InContract’*.
* Update them as:
** Move to *Awarded RFP tab*
** Change status to *‘Awarded’* (or appropriate mapped status if already progressed)

----

h4. *2. UI Changes*

* Remove *‘In Contract’* status display from:
** RFP Detail page
** Property listing / status chips
* Remove *‘Generate Contract’* button from:
** RFP Detail page

----

h4. *3. Code Cleanup*

* Remove all references to:
** {{InContract}} status (constants, enums, conditions)
** Deprecated contract handling logic tied to old flow
* Ensure contract actions are only handled via:
** *Awarded RFP module*

----

h4. *4. Validation*

* Ensure:
** No new records can be created with *‘InContract’*
** Status transitions follow strictly:
*** Awarded → Sent → Completed

----

h3. *Impact:*

* Eliminates confusion from duplicate/legacy statuses
* Aligns UI and backend with the new workflow
* Improves data consistency and reporting accuracy

----

h3. *Acceptance Criteria:*

* No *‘In Contract’* status visible anywhere in UI
* All legacy records updated and visible under *Awarded RFP*
* *Generate Contract* button removed from RFP Detail page
* Contract flow works only via Awarded RFP
* No backend references to {{InContract}} remain

In the RFP module, when a property is in the *"In Contract"* phase, users may still need to use the "Cancel Award" button to change vendors. However, if a user cancels an award and selects a new vendor, the *E-sign contract* does not currently update. We need to ensure that the contract is refreshed so that the *Legal Name* in the e-sign document match the newly awarded vendor.

 

h3. *Expected Behavior*

* *Dynamic Contract Update:* Upon awarding a new vendor after a cancellation, the system must trigger an update to the linked e-sign contract.

h3. *Current Behavior*

While the "Cancel Award" button is visible and active for properties "In Contract," re-awarding a new vendor does not push the updated legal details into the e-sign document, leading to a mismatch between the system's active vendor and the legal contract.

column1: Add Status-Based Validation for “Cancel Award” Option in Bid Review
column31:
h3. *Description:*

Enhance the existing *Cancel Award* functionality in the *Bid Review* module by restricting or allowing the action based on the current contract status of the awarded property.

----

h3. *Business Rules / Scenarios:*

h4. *1. Status: Awarded*

* User *can cancel the award* from the *Bid Review* or the corresponding *RFP Detail* page.
* User should be able to *award another vendor* for the same property.
* The previous record should be *removed from the Awarded RFP tab* and replaced with a new record with *‘Awarded’* status.

----

h4. *2. Status: Draft (Contract Not Sent)*

* User *can cancel the award* from the *Bid Review* or the corresponding *RFP Detail* page.
* User should be able to *award another vendor* for the same property.
* The previous record should be *removed from the Awarded RFP tab* and replaced with a new record with *‘Awarded’* status.

----

h4. *3. Status: Sent (Contract Sent for Signature)*

* User *should NOT be able to cancel the award*.
* The *Cancel Award* button should be *disabled*.

*Tooltip (on hover):*

{quote}“This property contract has already been sent for signature.”{quote}

----

h3. *Acceptance Criteria:*

# *Cancel Award – Enabled* 
#* Given a property in *Awarded* status in *Awarded RFP* tab,
When the user clicks *Cancel Award*,
Then the award is cancelled successfully and the user can re-award another vendor.
#* Given a property in *Draft* status,
When the user clicks *Cancel Award*,
Then the award is cancelled successfully and the user can re-award another vendor.

----

# *Re-Award Flow*
#* When a user cancels an award and awarded a new vendor,
Then:
#** The previous awarded record is *removed from the Awarded RFP tab*
#** A new record is created with *‘Awarded’* status
#** No duplicate awarded records exist for the same property

----

# *Cancel Award – Disabled State*
#* Given a property in *Sent* status in *Awarded RFP* tab,
Then the *Cancel Award* button is *disabled*
And user cannot perform the cancel action.

----

# *Tooltip Validation*
#* When the *Cancel Award* button is disabled,
Then hovering over it shows:
“This property contract has already been sent for signature.”

----

# *Backend Validation*
#* System should *prevent cancel award action via API* when status is *Sent (or beyond, if applicable)*
#* No workaround should allow cancellation in restricted states

----

# *Consistency*
#* The behavior should be consistent across:
#** *Bid Review page*
#** *RFP Detail page*

column1: Manager Name Validation Missing in Bulk Upload (Accepting Non-Letter Characters)
column31:
h3. *Description*

In the *Property Bulk Upload* process, the fields *Manager First Name* and *Manager Last Name* are accepting values containing non-alphabetic characters (e.g., numbers, special characters).

However, in the *UI (Edit Property List screen)*, these fields enforce validation and display an error message:

* _“First Name should contain only letters”_
* _“Last Name should contain only letters”_

This creates inconsistency between manual entry and bulk upload data validation.

----

h3. *Steps to Reproduce*

# Prepare a bulk upload CSV file.
# Enter values with non-letter characters:
#* Manager First Name: {{First1}}
#* Manager Last Name: {{Last@123}}
# Upload the file via Bulk Upload.
# Observe that the record is successfully created.
# Navigate to Edit Property List screen for the same record.

----

h3. *Actual Result*

* Bulk upload allows invalid values (numbers/special characters).
* No validation error is triggered.
* Invalid data is persisted in the system.

----

h3. *Expected Result*

* Bulk upload should enforce the same validation as UI:
** Accept only alphabetic characters (A–Z, a–z).
* System should:
** Reject invalid records *OR*
** Flag them with appropriate error messages in the upload result file.

*ScreenRecord*

[https://jam.dev/c/456ec953-ec1e-4131-9dd4-639b555c9298|https://jam.dev/c/456ec953-ec1e-4131-9dd4-639b555c9298|smart-link] 

h3. *Acceptance Criteria*

* Validation for *Manager First Name* and *Manager Last Name* is implemented in bulk upload.
* Only alphabetic characters are allowed.
* Invalid records:
** Are rejected during upload *or*
** Clearly reported in error file with proper message.
* Validation behavior is consistent across:
** UI forms
** Bulk upload
* Existing valid uploads remain unaffected

column1: Validation Errors Not Prioritized by Field Order in Property Bulk Upload Failed File
column31:
h3. *Description*

In *Property Bulk Upload*, when a row contains only *Company Name* and all subsequent fields are empty, the system correctly identifies validation errors for multiple mandatory fields.

However, in the *failed file*, the errors are *not prioritized based on field sequence (left-to-right order)*.
Instead of highlighting the *first missing mandatory field (Property Name)*, the system displays errors for other fields such as *City, State, and County*.

While the errors themselves are valid, the lack of prioritization makes the output confusing and less intuitive for users trying to correct the file.

----

h3. *Steps to Reproduce*

# Prepare a bulk upload CSV file.
# Enter only:
#* Company Name = Valid value
# Leave all other fields blank.
# Upload the file.
# Download the failed/error file.

----

h3. *Actual Result*

* Failed file contains errors for fields like:
** City
** State
** County
* Errors are valid but *not shown in logical field order*.
* The first missing mandatory field (*Property Name*) is not prioritized.

----

h3. *Expected Result*

* Validation errors should be *prioritized based on field order (left to right)*.
* The first error shown should be:
** _“Property Name is required”_
* Subsequent errors (City, State, County, etc.) can follow in order.
* Failed file should be intuitive and guide users to fix errors efficiently.



h3. *Acceptance Criteria*

* Validation errors are displayed in *field sequence order*.
* First missing mandatory field is *prioritized in error reporting*.
* Failed file clearly reflects:
** Correct field-level errors
** Logical ordering of errors
* Behavior is consistent across all bulk upload scenarios.

*Sample File :* [^failed_records (21).csv]
column617:
22/Apr/26 3:08 PM;62b94087268cac6e31c32ca4;[~accountid:6200d7cd5d18ad0072987c6f] *Root cause:* Row validation in the property CSV import job does not follow spreadsheet column order; it follows a fixed code pipeline, and only the *first* error per row is written to the failed file’s *Failure Reason*.

* *First:* Required Services resolution (only errors if the cell lists invalid service names; empty is OK).
* *Then:* Geo resolution (*Country → State → City → County* required values, then DB lookups for each).
* *Then:* Do Not Use Vendors resolution (including “vendors only = Yes” requires vendor names).
* *Only after that:* {{mapPropertyCsvRowToCreateDto}} runs, which is where *Property Name* and the other property/manager fields are validated.
* *Finally:* {{createFromCsvImport}} / {{create}} can still fail on business/DB rules.

So for sparse rows, users often see *location (or vendor) errors before Property Name*, not because those fields are “more important,” but because *that step runs earlier and the first exception wins*—there is no pass that sorts errors by left-to-right column order.

Contracts approaching their end date are currently all labeled “Expiring.” However, contracts that auto-renew should instead be classified as *“Auto-Renewing Soon”* to accurately reflect their status. Use the criteria below to determine the correct label.
*Auto-Renewing Soon*
Use when the contract end date is approaching AND:

* *Renewal Term* has a value (e.g., 3yr, 1yr, MTM), AND/OR
* *Renewal Terms* specifies an auto-renewal condition (e.g., “auto-renew for same period,” “renew unless notification”)

*Expiring*
Use when the contract end date is approaching AND/OR:

* *Renewal Term* = N/A or blank, AND
* *Renewal Terms* = N/A, blank, or indicates the contract will simply end (e.g., “will end unless renewed,” “requires mutual agreement to renew”)

column31:

When an expired insurance policy’s end date is updated to a future date, the policy status does not automatically change from “Expired” to “Compliant.” The system continues to display the policy as expired even though the new end date is valid.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Edit the policy and update the end date to a future date.
# Save the changes.
# Observe that the policy status remains “Expired.”

*Expected Result:*
If the end date is updated to a future date, the policy status should automatically update to “Compliant.”

----

Scenarios needs to be considered for the solution: 

# If the status = Expired, change the Contract end date to future (Any Future date >=current date + 31) it should change the status to *Compliant.* 
# If the status = Expired, change the end date to future (Any Future date <=current date +30) , it should change the status to *Expiring*
# If the status = Expired, change the Contract end date to future (Any past date <=current date ) it should change the status to *Expired.*
# If the status = Compliant,change the end date to future (Any Future date <=current date +30) , it should change the status to *Expiring.* 
# If the status = Compliant,change the end date to future (Any Future date > =current date +31) , it should change the status to *Complaint* 
# If the status= Compliant, change the contract end date (Any past date <=current date ) it should change the status to *Expired.*
# If the status = Non-compliant,change the end date to future (Any Future date <=current date +30) , it should keep the status as *Non-compliant.*
# If the status = Non-compliant,change the end date to future (Any Future date <=current date +30) , it should keep the status to *Non-compliant.*
# If the status= Non-compliant, change the end date (Any past date <=current date ) to *Deficient.*
# If the status = Expiring,change the end date to future (Any Future date <=current date +30) , it should change the status to *Expiring*
# If the status = Expiring,change the end date to future (Any Future date > =current date +31) , it should change the status to *Compliant.*
# If the status = Expiring, change the end date (Any past date <=current date ) it should change the status to *Expired.*
# If the status = Deficient,change the end date to future (Any Future date > =current date +31) , it should change the status to *Non-Compliant.*
# If the status = Deficient,change the end date to future (Any Future date <=current date +30) , it should change the status to *Non-Compliant.*
# If the status = Deficient,change the end date to (Any past date <=current date )  , it should change the status to *Deficient.*  
# If Client Insured = No, and the policy is Non-Compliant and is changed to Yes then the status should change to *Compliant or Expirirng or Expired based on the expiration date*
# If Client Insured= No, and the policy is Deficient and it is changed to Yes then the status should change to *Expired.*

column31:
*Description:*

Currently, contract expiration email notifications are being sent only to *corporate contacts*. The requirement is to extend this functionality so that emails are also sent to *non-corporate contacts* who are associated with the respective properties, such as *Property Managers* or other assigned users.

h3. *Requirement Details:*

* Identify all contacts linked to the property (including non-corporate roles)
* Ensure email notifications for contract expiration are sent to:
** Corporate contacts (existing behavior)
** Property Managers and other assigned contacts (new requirement)
* Avoid duplicate emails if a user belongs to multiple roles
* Maintain existing email template and notification triggers

h3. *Acceptance Criteria:*

# Contract expiration emails are sent to both corporate and non-corporate contacts associated with the property
# Property Managers receive the email if assigned to the property
# No duplicate emails are sent to the same user
# Existing corporate contact email flow remains unaffected
# Email content and template remain unchanged

column1: Vendor Compliance workflow for All Other Companies (excluding sole proprietors)
column31:
Vendor KYB Verification for LLC and Other Business Types 

*As a* vendor representing an LLC or other business entity, *I want to* complete the identity and compliance verification process after payment, *So that* my business can be verified and onboarded onto the Connexus platform.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

h3. AC-OB-01 | Stripe Payment Gate

# The system shall trigger a Stripe payment of *$125/client/year* before calling any verification API.
# Verification APIs shall only be triggered after a successful Stripe payment confirmation is received.
# If Stripe payment fails, no verification API shall be called and the vendor shall be notified of the failure.
# All payment processing shall be managed entirely by Stripe. No payment UI shall be built within Connexus.

h3. AC-OB-02 | KYB V2 — Entry Point

# Upon successful Stripe payment, the system shall automatically call the *Signzy US KYB V2 API* as the first verification step.
# The API call shall pass the vendor's business data as input.
# If the KYB V2 confidence score is *greater than 0.8*, the system shall proceed to *US TIN Verification*.
# If the KYB V2 confidence score is *0.8 or less*, the system shall trigger the *EIDV Advance API* as a fallback.
# The KYB V2 verification status shall be set to *Pending* while awaiting the API response.

h3. AC-OB-03 | US TIN Verification — Happy Path

# US TIN Verification shall only be triggered when the KYB V2 score is than 0.8.
# The API call shall include the *Business Legal Name* and *TIN/EIN* as mandatory inputs.
# If US TIN Verification returns *Pass*, the system shall proceed to *AML CFT Screening*.
# If US TIN Verification returns *Fail*, the system shall:greater 
#* Immediately set *Business Verified = Requirement Not Met*.
#* Send a *Denial Notification* to the vendor's registered email.
#* Not trigger any further API calls.

h3. AC-OB-04 | EIDV Advance — KYB Fallback (Score ≤ 0.8)

# EIDV Advance shall only be triggered when the KYB V2 score is 0.8 or less.
# The API call shall include the vendor's *Name, SSN, DOB, and Business Address* as input.
# If EIDV Advance returns *Pass*, the system shall proceed directly to *AML CFT Screening*.
# If EIDV Advance returns *Fail*, the system shall display a *Retry Screen* to the vendor.
# SSN values passed to EIDV Advance shall *NOT be saved or persisted* in the Connexus database at any point.

h3. AC-OB-05 | Retry Screen — EIDV Fail

# The Retry Screen shall only be displayed after an EIDV Advance failure.
# The vendor shall only be permitted to re-enter the following fields on the Retry Screen:
#* EIN
#* Business Name (this data should be autopopulated) 
#* Business Address (This data should be autopopulated)
# No other fields shall be editable on the Retry Screen.
# Upon submission of updated data, the system shall re-run the *KYB V2 API* with the new information.
# If the retry KYB V2 score is *greater than 0.8*, the system shall proceed to *US TIN Verification*.
# If the retry KYB V2 score is *0.8 or less*, the system shall:
#* Set *Business Verified = Requirements Not Met.*
#* Send a *Denial Notification* to the vendor.
#* Not permit any further retries.

h3. AC-OB-06 | AML CFT Screening

# AML CFT Screening shall be triggered in the following cases only:
#* KYB V2 score > 0.8 *AND* US TIN Verification passed, *OR*
#* KYB V2 score ≤ 0.8 *AND* EIDV Advance passed, *OR*
#* Retry KYB V2 score > 0.8 *AND* US TIN Verification passed.
# The system shall call the *Signzy AML CFT Screening Global API*.
# If AML CFT Screening returns *Pass*, the system shall set *Business Verified = YES*.
# If AML CFT Screening returns *Fail*, the system shall:
#* Set *Business Verified = NO*.
#* Send a *Denial Notification* to the vendor.

h3. AC-OB-07 | Business Verified Status — Decision Matrix

||Path||Conditions||Business Verified||
|Happy path|KYB > 0.8 → TIN pass → AML pass|*YES*|
|Happy path|KYB > 0.8 → TIN fail|*NO + Denial*|
|Happy path|KYB > 0.8 → TIN pass → AML fail|*NO + Denial*|
|EIDV fallback|KYB ≤ 0.8 → EIDV pass → AML pass|*YES*|
|EIDV fallback|KYB ≤ 0.8 → EIDV pass → AML fail|*NO + Denial*|
|Retry path|KYB ≤ 0.8 → EIDV fail → Retry KYB > 0.8 → TIN pass → AML pass|*YES*|
|Retry path|KYB ≤ 0.8 → EIDV fail → Retry KYB > 0.8 → TIN fail|*NO + Denial*|
|Retry path|KYB ≤ 0.8 → EIDV fail → Retry KYB ≤ 0.8|*NO + Denial*|

h3. AC-OB-08 | General System Rules

# The system shall set verification status to *Pending* when any API call is initiated and awaiting a response.
# The system shall update verification status to *Passed* or *Failed* based on the API response received.
# *Denial Notifications* shall be sent to the vendor's registered email address for every outcome where Business Verified = NO/ Requirements Not Met.
# The vendor shall not be permitted to proceed past any failed step unless an explicit retry path exists as defined in AC-OB-05.
# Once Business Verified = NO is set after exhausting all retry options, the case shall be -flagged for- *-manual review-* -by the compliance team.- marked as “Requirements Not Met” in the Vendor Screen.
# SSN values shall never be stored or logged in any Connexus database or system at any point in the flow.

column1: Vendor Record- when clicking on the vendor name
column31:
----

*Summary:* Vendor Record — Connexus Verify Tab, Document Upload & Extraction, and Payments Dashboard

*Module:* Connexus Verify — Vendor Record- when clicking on the vendor name.

----

*User Story*

As a Connexus user or client user, I want to open a vendor record from the Vendor List, view and manage that vendor's compliance documents (insurance and business licenses), upload new documents for AI-assisted data extraction, review and save the extracted results, and see the vendor's payment status — so that all vendor compliance information is centralized, actionable, and role-appropriately scoped in one place.

----

*Background*

The Vendor Record is the primary workspace for managing a single vendor's information. It is accessed by double-clicking the vendor's name in the Vendor List. The record currently contains basic company details and an Insurance tab. This story replaces and significantly expands that structure to support the Connexus Verify compliance model, which tracks both Business Licenses and Insurance as separate compliance tracks, and adds a Payments tab to surface billing status.

The record is role-sensitive: Insurance data is scoped to the viewing client, while Business License data is platform-wide and not client-specific.

----

*Acceptance Criteria*

*AC1 — Vendor Record Entry & Layout*

* Double-clicking a vendor's name in the Vendor List opens the Vendor Record.
* The record displays a header with the vendor's name, Vendor ID, status badge, and an Upload Document button in the top right corner.
* The record contains four tabs: Vendor Details, Connexus Verify, Contacts, and Activity History.
* The Upload Document button is visible and accessible from any tab at all times.

*AC2 — Vendor Details Tab*

* The Vendor Details tab displays standard company information: Legal Name, DBA, EIN, Phone, Address, Website, Primary Contact, and Email.
* Above the Company Details section, a note must appear stating that Connexus Verify has replaced Insurance as the compliance tracking method, and directing the user to the Connexus Verify tab for coverage details.
* The words "Services" and "All Across USA" (and any similar legacy service/geography display elements) are removed from this tab.

*AC3 — Connexus Verify Tab — Structure*

* The Connexus Verify tab displays a Business Verified indicator (Yes / No toggle) at the top.
* Below the Business Verified indicator, three pill selectors allow the user to switch between sub-views: Business Licenses, Insurance, and Payments.
* Business Verified is a Connexus-managed field. Client users may view it but may not edit it.

*AC4 — Business Licenses Dashboard (Connexus Verify → Business Licenses pill)*

Dashboard columns in order: Service(s), Jurisdiction, Expiration Date (MM/DD/YYYY), Status, Download.

The Jurisdiction field displays a short code:

* For a state-issued license: the 2-letter state abbreviation (e.g., CT, FL).
* For a federally issued license: the prefix F- followed by the agency abbreviation (e.g., F-EPA).
* For a locally issued license: the 2-letter state abbreviation of the local jurisdiction's state.

*AC5 — Insurance Dashboard (Connexus Verify → Insurance pill)*

* The Insurance dashboard is client-specific. A client user sees only the COI records relevant to their account. Connexus internal users see all records and an additional Client column.
* Dashboard columns for client users: Property, Date Approved, Service(s) Approved, States Covered, Expiration, Status, Download.
* Dashboard columns for Connexus internal users: Client (additional, leftmost column), Property, Date Approved, Service(s) Approved, States Covered, Expiration, Status, Download.
* A Download link (labeled COI) renders on each Approved row.
* Clicking any row opens the saved Insurance record (see AC11 — Saved Record View).

*AC6 — Payments Dashboard (Connexus Verify → Payments pill)*
The Payments dashboard displays three fields: Date Paid, Amount, and Annual Renewal Date.

* *Date Paid* — Displays the date the vendor reached Business Verified = Yes. Beneath the date, a Delayed Charge sub-section is visible to Connexus internal users only. If a delay has been applied from the Vendor Invite screen, the delay date is shown here (e.g., "Delay – 12/01/2026") with an option to remove it. If no delay is active, a date input and Set button allow a Connexus user to apply one. When a delay is active, the Annual Renewal Date recalculates from the delay date automatically. This sub-section is not visible to client users or vendors.
* *Amount* — Displays the amount set at the time of the vendor invite. Read-only within the Payments dashboard; it is not editable here. The amount is determined upstream on the Vendor Invite screen.
* *Annual Renewal Date* — 12 months from Date Paid, or from the delay date if a delay is active.
* A "Send Renewal Reminder" placeholder renders as a disabled element labeled "Coming soon" — no send logic required in this release.

*AC7 — Upload Document Flow*

* Clicking the Upload Document button opens an upload interface.
* The interface supports selection of one or more PDF files in a single action (multi-file upload required).
* Maximum file size per document: 20MB.
* Each uploaded file is displayed in a staging list before processing. For each file, the user must designate the document type: Insurance or Business License. A file without a type designation cannot be submitted for processing.
* A Remove option allows individual files to be removed from the staging list before processing. Removed files are not retained.
* A Cancel option exits the upload flow entirely. No files are saved.
* A Process Documents action submits the staged files for AI-assisted data extraction.
* If multiple files are staged, each is processed individually and sequentially based on its designated type.

*AC8 — Insurance Extraction Screen*

* After a file is designated as Insurance and submitted, the system displays the AI-extracted insurance data for review.
* An AI attribution notice appears at the top of the screen indicating that fields were extracted by AI and should be reviewed before saving.
* Extracted fields displayed per policy row: Insurance Type (dropdown), Expiration Date (text input, MM/DD/YYYY format).
* Insurance Type dropdown options: General Liability, Auto Liability, Workers Comp, Umbrella Policy, Pollution, Professional, Cyber Policy, Inland Marine, Other. If Other is selected, an additional text input appears pre-populated with the AI-extracted value, which the user can edit.
* Each policy row is fully editable. Each row includes a Delete option to remove an inaccurate or unwanted policy from the set.
* An Add Policy option allows the user to manually add additional policy rows.
* Bottom action buttons:
** Cancel — exits the flow. The uploaded document is discarded and is not saved to the record.
** Save as Approved — saves all policy rows and creates a new Insurance record on the dashboard with status Approved.

*AC9 — Business License Extraction Screen*

* After a file is designated as Business License and submitted, the system displays the AI-extracted license data for review.
* An AI attribution notice appears at the top of the screen.
* Extracted fields:
_Business Name_
** Editable text input pre-populated with the AI-extracted value.
* _Issuing Authority_ — Three radial options: Federal, State, Local.
** If Federal is selected: a "Suggested: [Agency]" tag appears based on context, followed by a dropdown to confirm or change the agency (EPA, HUD, SBA, DOT, OSHA, USDA). The suggestion can be overridden.
** If State is selected: a single-select dropdown of 2-letter state abbreviations.
** If Local is selected: a "Local in which state?" label, followed by a state dropdown, followed by a free-text field for the jurisdiction name.
* The Jurisdiction code is derived automatically from the Issuing Authority selection and stored with the record: state abbreviation for State or Local, F-[Agency] for Federal.
_Expiration Date_ — Displayed in this order: Date radio button → date input (MM/DD/YYYY, active when Date is selected) → None radio button. If None is selected, the date input is disabled.
_Services_
** An editable text field pre-populated with the AI-extracted services text.
** A multi-select checkbox list from the platform's existing services list, allowing the user to map the extracted text to standardized service categories. Multiple services may be selected. Selected services are visually highlighted.
* _Notes_
** A free-text area at the bottom of the screen for any additional notes about the license.
* Bottom action buttons:
** Cancel — exits the flow. The uploaded document is discarded and is not saved to the record.
** Requires Review — saves the record to the Business Licenses dashboard with status "Requires Review".
** Draft — saves the record with status "In Draft".
** Approved — saves the record with status "Approved".
** Declined — opens a modal prompting the user to enter a reason for decline (required). On confirmation: the reason is saved to the record's Notes field, the record is saved with status "Declined", and a notification is generated to send to the vendor with the decline reason.

*AC10 — Post-Save Behavior (All Document Types)*

* After any save action (Requires Review, Draft, Approved, Declined), the user is returned to the Connexus Verify tab with the relevant pill pre-selected (Business Licenses for license saves, Insurance for COI saves).
* The newly saved record appears in the dashboard.
* Selecting a saved record in the future opens it in read-only view (see AC11).

*AC11 — Saved Record View*

* Clicking a row in either the Business Licenses or Insurance dashboard opens the saved record.
* The record opens in read-only mode by default. All fields display as static text.
* An Edit button is available. Selecting it switches the record into edit mode, converting all fields to editable inputs.
* A Done button (replacing Edit when in edit mode) saves changes and returns the record to read-only.
* Only the fields captured at time of submission are shown in the record. No extraneous fields are displayed.

----

*Out of Scope*

* Email-triggered COI submission flow (covered separately).
* Stripe payment processing and payment link generation (covered in Payments epic).
* Renewal reminder email send logic (placeholder UI only in this release).
* Vendor portal / vendor-side view of the record (separate story).
* Bulk upload or batch processing across multiple vendors simultaneously.

----

*Dependencies*

* Business Verified field must be writable by the Connexus internal user role.
* AI extraction service must accept PDF input and return structured field data for both Insurance and Business License document types.
* Role-based access controls must be in place to distinguish Connexus internal users from client users before the client-specific scoping of the Insurance dashboard and the Delay Charge control on Payments can be enforced.
* Platform services list must be finalized and accessible by the Business License extraction screen for the services multi-select.
* Audit logging service must be active to capture Amount edits on the Payments dashboard.

----

*Definition of Done*

* Double-clicking a vendor name in the Vendor List opens the Vendor Record with all four tabs rendered.
* Vendor Details tab displays the Connexus Verify note and no legacy Services/geography fields.
* Connexus Verify tab renders all three pills (Business Licenses, Insurance, Payments) and each dashboard loads correctly with its defined columns.
* Upload Document button is accessible from all tabs and launches the upload flow.
* A staged file without a document type designation cannot be submitted; validation fires correctly.
* Insurance extraction screen renders AI-extracted policy rows, all fields are editable, rows can be deleted, and Save as Approved correctly creates a record on the Insurance dashboard.
* Business License extraction screen renders all fields with correct input types; all five action buttons function correctly; Declined triggers the decline modal and saves the reason to notes.
* Payments dashboard correctly displays Date Paid, Amount, and Annual Renewal Date per the defined logic; the Delay Charge control is visible only to Connexus internal users.
* Amount is editable in the dashboard and the change is reflected going forward.
* Annual Renewal Date recalculates correctly when a delay date is set or modified.
* Saved records open in read-only mode with a functioning Edit toggle.
* Role-based visibility rules are enforced: client users do not see the Client column on Insurance, do not see the Delay Charge control on Payments, and cannot edit Business Verified.
* All behaviors verified in staging across Connexus internal user, client user, and (where applicable) vendor user roles.

----

*EPIC: Connexus Verify — Vendor Compliance & Business Verification Platform*

Component: Connexus Verify | Module: Vendor Compliance | Affects: Client, Vendor, Connexus Users

----

*SUMMARY*

Build and deliver the end-to-end Connexus Verify vendor compliance workflow, enabling client users and Connexus staff to invite vendors to credentialing, complete KYB (Know Your Business) verification, and manage COI (Certificate of Insurance) compliance — all within the Connexus platform.

This epic covers the full lifecycle: vendor discovery in the Vendor Module, invite and registration flows, KYB form submission (Sole Proprietor and Entity variants), Stripe-gated payment, third-party KYB API scoring, business license tracking, COI insurance review, and multi-trigger automated email communications.

----

*GOALS & SCOPE*

In scope: Vendor Module UI (client and Connexus views), vendor invite form, KYB registration flow (sole prop + entity), Stripe payment integration, KYB API integration, Business Verified status logic, business license and COI sub-tabs, automated email triggers (#1–#8), Connexus admin actions.

Out of scope: Trustlayer integration (placeholder until future epic), property-level Do Not Use list management, vendor-side account self-registration without an invite.

----

*CHILD STORIES*

Vendor Module — Client View

* Vendor List: display vendor table with status columns (Business Verified, Required Licenses, Next License Expiration, Next COI Expiration, Status). Client-side only; sources: contract extractions (Current Vendors) , preferred vendors, -Do Not Use-, and invited vendors.
* Vendor Record: double-click opens record with Vendor Details, Connexus Verify, and Contact List tabs. Client view omits Services and Service Area; Connexus view adds Upload Document and Vendor Insurance sections. See [CX-3301|https://neoito-team-connexus.atlassian.net/browse/CX-3301].
* Connexus Verify tab: Business Verified indicator, Business Licenses sub-view (platform-wide), and Insurance sub-view (client-specific). Insurance columns: Client, Property, States Covered, Date Approved, Service(s) Approved, Expiration, Status, Download.

Vendor Invite Flow

* Action button on vendor row surfaces two options: "Invite to Connexus Verify" and "Resend Connexus Verify Invitation."
* Invite form captures: Company Name (dropdown + Create New option), Company Legal Name, Services (required), Website, Portfolio/Property multi-select, and Primary Contact (First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone — all required). Actions: Send Invite, Cancel, Save as Draft. Connexus users only: "Delay Charge and Send" with MM/DD/YYYY date picker.

Email & Registration Routing

* Email routing logic based on vendor state: Email #1 for new or non-credentialed vendors; Email #2 for credentialed vendors who have not yet completed KYB; Email #3 for vendors already KYB-verified for another client (insurance requirements only). [Email Link.|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ncUK1TdMfgh9idLdHt39AHdbeiaOOumB/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=104208809598381798787&rtpof=true&sd=true]

KYB Verification Flow

* KYB form — Sole Proprietor variant: Company Name (tooltip: "Company Name or DBA"), Company Legal Name, Company Type, optional website checkbox + URL, Business Address (Street, City, County, State, ZIP), optional checkbox for separate Residential Address (Street, City, State, ZIP), Owner Details (First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone, Date of Birth MM/DD/YYYY, SSN encrypted), Service Area(s) multi-select. See [CX-3146|https://neoito-team-connexus.atlassian.net/browse/CX-3146].
* KYB form — Entity variant (Corp, LLC, Non-Profit, Partnership, S-Corp): TIN/EIN (format: 00-0000000, encrypted), optional website checkbox + URL, Business Address (Street, City, County, State, ZIP), Services Requiring Insurance (tooltip: "Services your company will perform that require proof of insurance"), Primary Contact (First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone format: +1 (555) 000-0000), Service Area(s) multi-select. See [CX-3297|https://neoito-team-connexus.atlassian.net/browse/CX-3297].
* Payment gate: Stripe integration triggered on "Continue and Pay." KYB API is called only after payment is confirmed. Stripe handles all receipts and declines. See [CX-2992|https://neoito-team-connexus.atlassian.net/browse/CX-2992].
* KYB scoring & outcome logic: Score ≥ 8.5 → Business Verified = Yes → [Email #5|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ncUK1TdMfgh9idLdHt39AHdbeiaOOumB/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=104208809598381798787&rtpof=true&sd=true] (if business license requirements exist) or manual Connexus outreach (until Trustlayer is integrated). Score < 8.5 → [Email #4|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ncUK1TdMfgh9idLdHt39AHdbeiaOOumB/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=104208809598381798787&rtpof=true&sd=true] requesting Corporation Certificate. Verification failed → [Email #7|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ncUK1TdMfgh9idLdHt39AHdbeiaOOumB/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=104208809598381798787&rtpof=true&sd=true]. KYB data is sent to the API and must not be stored in the Connexus system.

Connexus Internal Actions

* Connexus staff can perform all invite, verification, document upload, status check, and compliance update actions from the Vendor Menu.
* Upload Document button (Connexus users only): upload Insurance or Business License documents to a vendor record at any time.

----

*ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA*

# Client user can view their vendor list with all required columns and can open a vendor record via double-click.
# Client view does not expose Services, Service Area, Vendor Insurance, or Upload Document controls.
# Action button on each vendor row surfaces correct options; invite form validates all required fields before sending.
# Connexus-only "Delay Charge and Send" option is hidden from client users; date picker fires the invite on the selected date.
# Correct [email (#1, #2, or #3)|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ncUK1TdMfgh9idLdHt39AHdbeiaOOumB/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=104208809598381798787&rtpof=true&sd=true] is dispatched based on vendor's existing credentialing and KYB state.
# KYB form renders the correct field set based on selected Company Type (Sole Prop vs. all other entities).
# SSN and TIN/EIN fields are encrypted at rest and in transit; never displayed in plaintext post-submission.
# Payment is collected via Stripe before the KYB API is called; KYB data is not submitted until payment is confirmed.
# KYB score ≥ 8.5 sets Business Verified = Yes and triggers the appropriate Email #5 path; score < 8.5 triggers Email #4; failed verification triggers Email #7.
# KYB data is passed to the API and not persisted in the Connexus database.
# Business Licenses sub-tab is platform-wide (not client-specific); Insurance sub-tab is scoped to the viewing client.
# Connexus staff can perform all actions (invite, verify, upload, status update) from the Vendor Menu with no restrictions.

----

*LABELS*

column1: Business License Rule Engine - Automated State-Service Validation and Notifications
column31:
h2. *1. Description*

This ticket covers the implementation of the automated Business License compliance engine. The system determines license requirements by cross-referencing Service ID and Property State, manages collection via tokenized links, and handles unmapped services through a "Support Email" fallback. This replaces manual "Varies" assessments with a hard-coded, automated rule engine.

h2. *2. Core Logic (The Rule Engine)*

The backend must evaluate the *State + Service* inputs against three validation paths to determine the compliance "Pill" status:

* *Path A (Global Mandatory):*
** *Logic:* IF Rule ID is *R-01 through R-08* → Trigger for *ALL 50 States*.
** _Includes:_ Pest Control, HVAC, Fire Life Safety, Electrical, etc.

* *Path B (State-Specific Mandatory):*
** *Logic:* Trigger ONLY if the Property State is in the specifically mapped list below:
*** *R-11 (Security):* AL, AZ, AR, CA, CT, DE, FL, GA, HI, IL, KY, LA, MD, MA, MI, MS, MT, NV, NJ, NM, NY, NC, OK, OR, RI, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA, WV.
*** *R-16/17 (Construction):* AL, AK, AZ, AR, CA, CT, DE, FL, GA, HI, ID, IA, LA, MD, MA, MI, MN, MS, NV, NJ, NM, NY, NC, ND, OR, RI, SC, TN, UT, VA, WA, WV.
*** *R-101 (Landscaping):* AL, AK, AR, CA, HI, LA, MD, MN, MS, NV, NM, NC, OR, TN, UT, WA.

* *Path C (The Trap Door):*
** *Logic:* IF a service is selected that is NOT found in the existing catalog.
** *Action:* Display "Request Service Addition" button.
** *Trigger:* On click, system sends an automated email to  [*support@joinconnexus.com*|mailto:support@joinconnexus.com].
** *Dashboard Status:* Flag record as *"Internal Flag: Team Mapping Needed."*

h2. *3. Functional Requirements*

* *Data Ingestion:* System must ingest 2 inputs: *State + Service* (from Invite Vendor screen or RFP).

* *AI-Assisted OCR Interface:* Admin view must include fields for: License Number, State of Issue, Expiration Date, and a Boolean toggle: "Does Entity Name on License match Business Name?"
** _Note:_ Use AI to identify and pre-fill these fields for the Admin, but the final validation remains a manual human action.

* *Local Jurisdictional Rule:* Set local/city licenses as *Optional* (required: false); these should not block the overall "Verified" status.

* *Multi-License Support:* The vendor upload portal must allow for *multiple license uploads* in the event a vendor provides several services or operates in multiple jurisdictions.

* *Internal Review Trigger:* Each time a new license is uploaded, the system must trigger a platform-level notification/alert to the Connexus Admin team to signal a new item is ready for review.

* *Post-Verification Trigger (Trustlayer):* If the Rule Engine determines *N/A (No license needed)* OR once the Admin *Approves* the license, the system must trigger an internal notification/alert to the Admin team.
** _Strategic Note:_ This serves as the manual signal to initiate the Trustlayer insurance verification process.

* *Data Persistence:* Validated expiry dates must be saved and trigger a "Renewal Required" notification 30 days prior to expiration.

h2. *4. Notification & Email Lifecycle*

* *N1: Primary Request:* Email to Vendor with a tokenized link to the upload portal.
* *N2: Secondary Request (Invalid/Missing):* Triggered if Admin marks review as "Invalid." Content: List missing items (e.g., "Illegible," "Wrong State," "Name Mismatch").
* *N3: Final Failure:* Triggered after 3 failed attempts. Move status to "Hard Fail."
* *N4: Success Notification:* Notify Connexus User and Client: "New Approved Vendor."

h2. *5. Acceptance Criteria (AC)*

* *AC1:* System accurately triggers "Action Required" for Pest Control (R-01) in all 50 states.
* *AC2:* System triggers "Action Required" for Landscaping (R-101) only for the 16 states listed in Path B.
* *AC3:* Selecting an unknown service triggers an email to [support@joinconnexus.com|mailto:support@joinconnexus.com] instead of an API call.
* *AC4:* Internal Admin dashboard displays a notification alert immediately upon a new vendor upload.
* *AC5:* Admin interface successfully uses AI to pre-populate license fields for manual verification.
* *AC6:* If "No License Required" is determined, an automated alert is sent to the Admin team to initiate the Trustlayer process.
* *AC7:* The compliance "Pill" reflects Action Required, Optional, or N/A based on the Rule Engine result.
* *AC8:* Validated data (License # and Expiry) is successfully saved to the Vendor Dashboard.
* *AC9:* Tokenized upload links remain valid for 7 days or until a successful upload is registered.

h2. *6. Out of Scope*

* *Automated Validation:* While AI helps extract data, the final "Approved" status must be a manual toggle by an Admin.
* *Legacy Data Migration:* This logic applies to new onboarding and new RFP triggers only.

h2. *7. Technical Assets Attached*

* {{Flow Diagram.png}}
* {{Vendor Licensing Requirements.docx}}

column1: Vendor Profile — Introduce "Tax Documents" Tab, Migrate W9s, Deprecate Vendor Insurance Tab
column31:
Here you go:

----

Overview This story covers the full lifecycle of retiring the existing Vendor Insurance tab (after a data export prerequisite is satisfied), migrating W9 documents to a new dedicated Tax Documents tab, and introducing a permission-gated experience for viewing and managing those documents across Connexus Users, Client Users, and Vendor primary contacts.

----

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Pre-requisite / Data Migration

* All existing Insurance Certificates on the Vendor Insurance tab must be downloaded and archived before the tab is removed.
* All existing W9 documents currently stored under the Vendor Insurance tab are migrated to the new Tax Documents tab, preserving their associated vendor and upload date.
* The Vendor Insurance tab is removed from the Vendor profile UI in the same release once migration is confirmed complete.

Tax Documents Tab — General

* A new "Tax Documents" tab is added to the Vendor profile page.
* The tab displays a list of uploaded W9 documents with the following columns: Document name / file, Upload date, Status (Active / Inactive)
* Documents are stored and displayed by date, supporting multiple W9s per vendor (one per year), with the most recent displayed first.
* Upon upload, the most recent W9 is automatically set to Active; all previous W9s for that vendor are automatically set to Inactive.
* Users with appropriate permissions can view and download individual documents from this tab.

Permission: Tax Documents

* A single new permission called "Tax Documents" is added to the permissions framework.
* This permission is assignable to both Connexus Users and Client Users at the company level.
* The permission grants the ability to: view the Tax Documents tab and its contents, and download individual W9 documents.
* Users without this permission do not see the Tax Documents tab.
* Vendor primary contacts can see the Tax Documents tab on their own vendor profile without requiring this company-level permission.

column31:
User Story:

As a Connexus platform, I want to automatically trigger the correct email notification to vendors at each stage of the invite, credentialing, and KYB/KYC verification workflow, so that vendors receive timely, context-specific communications that guide them through onboarding, compliance checks, and any required remediation actions without manual intervention from the client or operations team.

*Acceptance Criteria:*

*AC1 - Email 1 - New vendor, outside RFP process*

* When a client invites a vendor that does not exist in the Connexus application, Email 1 is triggered.
* Vendor is not credentialed and has not gone through any KYB process.
* Invitation originates outside of the RFP process.

*AC2 - Email 2 - Existing vendor, but no KYB*

* When a client invites a vendor that already exists in Connexus and is but has not gone through the KYB process, Email 2 is triggered.
* Scenario A: Client uses the Invite Vendor button, searches, and selects an existing Connexus vendor - Email 2 fires.
* Scenario B: Client clicks the Invite button directly from the vendor record on the Vendor List page - Email 2 fires.
* Condition: Vendor credentialing status = Yes, KYB verified = No.

*AC3 - Email 3 - Vendor KYB-verified for one client, invited by another*

* When a vendor is already KYB-verified for Client A and a different client (Client B) invites the same vendor, Email 3 is triggered.
* KYB verified = Yes for at least one existing client relationship.
* New client relationship is not yet KYB-verified for the inviting client.
* System identifies the vendor as KYB-verified in platform context before sending.

*AC4 - Email 4 - TIN verification failed (non-sole proprietor)*

* When a vendor's business type is anything other than Sole Proprietor and their TIN verification fails, Email 4 is triggered.
* Business type = LLC, Corporation, Partnership, or other non-sole-proprietor entity.
* TIN verification result = Failed.
* Email instructs vendor to upload their Articles of Incorporation document.

*AC5 - Email 7 - Business verification failed (all business types)*

* When the business verification status is set to No, Email 7 is triggered regardless of whether the vendor is a Sole Proprietor or any other business type.
* Applies to: KYC = No, AML = No, KYB verified = No, Business verified = No.
* Vendor has failed the credentialing/verification process.
* Applies to both Sole Proprietor and all other business types.

*AC6 - Email 17 - SSN verification failed (sole proprietor retry)*

* When the vendor's business type is Sole Proprietor and SSN verification fails, Email 17 is triggered.
* Business type = Sole Proprietor only, not applicable to other entity types.
* SSN verification result = Failed.
* Email prompts vendor to re-enter or re-verify their SSN.

*General Conditions:*

* All email triggers are automated by the system with no manual action required from the client or ops team.
* Each trigger fires exactly once per qualifying event and re-triggering only occurs if the underlying condition resets such as vendor re-invited or new TIN submission.
* Email content must reflect the specific scenario context including client name, vendor name, and document type required.
* Business type classification of Sole Proprietor vs other must be verified before dispatching Emails 4 or 17.

Email Recipients: 

*Email Trigger Logic by Business Type*

*Sole Proprietor*

* The Invite email should be sent to the *primary contact* added by the client.
* Once the vendor receives the email and completes the registration form, all subsequent emails such as SSN verification failed and Business verification failed  should be triggered using the email address captured under the *Owner Details* tab.

*Other Business Types*

* The Invite email should be sent to the primary contact added by the client.
* Once the vendor receives the email and completes the registration form, all subsequent emails such as TIN verification failed and Business verification failed  should be triggered using the email address captured under the *Primary Details* tab.

As confirmed by Heather, the email will not be triggered to all vendor users under the organization.

column1: License Tracking — License Upload
column31:
h2. Overview

Build a License & Permit tracking module within the existing Contract Management area for a property. The module lives under a new {{Licenses}} tab alongside {{Contracts}}, {{Documents}}, {{E-Sign}}, and {{Notes}}. It consists of two screens: a property-level register (list view) and a per-license detail view with full history and notes.

Reference mockups are attached (see PDF).

----

h2. Data Model

*License Requirement* (per property)

* {{id}}, {{property_id}}, {{name}}, {{license_id_label}} (e.g. BL-2026), {{issuing_authority}}, {{renewal_cadence}} (annual / multi-year / one-time), {{cost}}, {{required_document}} (bool), {{expiry_threshold_days}} (default 60)

*License Record* (one per renewal cycle, linked to a requirement)

* {{id}}, {{requirement_id}}, {{year}}, {{date_issued}}, {{coverage_start}}, {{coverage_end}}, {{cost}}, {{document_id}}, {{is_current}} (bool)

*Document*

* {{id}}, {{requirement_id}}, {{file_name}}, {{file_url}}, {{size_bytes}}, {{uploaded_at}}, {{uploaded_by_user_id}}

*Note*

* {{id}}, {{requirement_id}}, {{author_user_id}}, {{body}}, {{created_at}}

*Computed status* per requirement: {{Compliant}} | {{Expiring Soon}} | {{Missing}} (see status rules below).

----

h2. Screen 1 — License Register (List View)

h3. Layout

* Page header: property name, property code, city, unit count (already present on sibling tabs — reuse).
* Tab bar: {{Contracts | Licenses (n) | Documents | E-Sign | Notes}}. Badge {{n}} = count of non-compliant licenses ({{Expiring Soon}} + {{Missing}}).
* Below tab bar: a banner shown only when one or more requirements have status {{Missing}}. Text: {{{n} licenses missing — upload documents or request from property manager to resolve.}}
* Top-right of register: two buttons — {{Upload for AI Review}} and {{+ Add Requirement}}.
* Table columns: {{License / Permit}} (name + ID label) | {{Issuing Authority}} | {{Date Issued}} | {{Expiration}} | {{Cost}} | {{Status}} | row action {{View >}}.

h3. Status Rules

* {{Compliant}} (green pill): document on file AND ({{expiration}} is null OR {{expiration}} > today + {{expiry_threshold_days}}).
* {{Expiring Soon}} (yellow pill): document on file AND {{expiration}} <= today + {{expiry_threshold_days}} AND {{expiration}} >= today.
* {{Missing}} (red pill): no current document on file, OR {{expiration}} < today.

h3. Interaction Flow

# User lands on the property page and clicks the {{Licenses}} tab. The register loads all requirements for that property with their computed status.
# Clicking {{View >}} on any row routes to Screen 2 for that requirement.
# Clicking {{Upload for AI Review}} opens the AI upload flow (see below).
# Clicking {{+ Add Requirement}} opens the Add Requirement modal (see below).

h3. Upload for AI Review Flow

# User clicks {{Upload for AI Review}}. A file picker opens (accept: PDF, JPG, PNG).
# After selection, show a processing state while the document is sent to the AI extraction service.
# Service returns extracted fields: {{license_type}}, {{issuing_authority}}, {{license_id_label}}, {{date_issued}}, {{expiration}}, {{cost}}.
# System attempts to match the extracted document to an existing requirement on this property (match on {{name}} + {{issuing_authority}}, fall back to {{license_id_label}}).
# Show a confirmation modal pre-filled with the extracted fields and the matched requirement (if any). User can edit any field or reassign to a different requirement.
# On confirm: persist a new License Record + Document, mark it {{is_current = true}}, demote any prior {{is_current}} for that requirement, and recompute status. Close modal and refresh the register.
# If no match is found and the user cannot select one, offer to create a new requirement inline using the extracted fields.

h3. Add Requirement Flow

# User clicks {{+ Add Requirement}}. Modal opens with fields: {{name}}, {{issuing_authority}}, {{renewal_cadence}}, {{cost}}, {{required_document}} (toggle).
# Scope selector at the bottom of the modal: {{This property only}} (default) | {{All properties in portfolio}}.
# On save:
#* If {{This property only}}: create one requirement for the current property.
#* If {{All properties in portfolio}}: create the requirement for every property the user has edit access to; skip properties where a requirement with the same name + authority already exists (return a summary of created vs skipped).
# New requirements appear in the register with status {{Missing}} until a document is uploaded.

----

h2. Screen 2 — License Detail View

h3. Layout

* {{< Back to License Register}} link at top.
* Header card: license name (large), issuing authority + ID label, status pill, cost, expiration, {{+ Upload New}} button on the right.
* Section: *License History* — table with columns {{Year | Date Issued | Coverage Period | Cost | Document}}. The current cycle row is tagged with a {{current}} badge.
* Section: *Documents* — table with columns {{File Name | Uploaded | Uploaded By | Size}}. File name links to download.
* Section: *Notes* — reverse-chronological list. Each note shows author avatar, name, date, and body. Input box at the bottom: {{Add a note...}}.

h3. Interaction Flow

# User arrives via {{View >}} from the register. Detail view loads the requirement plus all linked License Records, Documents, and Notes.
# Clicking a document file name downloads (or previews) the file.
# Clicking {{+ Upload New}} opens the same AI upload flow as Screen 1, but pre-scoped to this requirement (skip the matching step). On confirm: append a new License Record and Document, mark it current, demote the prior current record, recompute and refresh the header status.
# Typing in the {{Add a note...}} box and submitting creates a new Note. The new note appears at the top of the list immediately on save.

----

h2. Acceptance Criteria

*AC1 — Register loads per property.* Selecting the {{Licenses}} tab on a property renders all that property's requirements with the columns listed above.

*AC2 — Status computation.* Each row's status pill matches the Status Rules above, recomputed on every page load.

*AC3 — Missing banner.* When {{Missing}} count > 0, a banner appears at the top of the register with the count and CTA text exactly as specified.

*AC4 — Tab badge.* The {{Licenses}} tab shows a badge equal to the count of {{Expiring Soon}} + {{Missing}} requirements.

*AC5 — AI extraction.* Uploading a document via {{Upload for AI Review}} extracts the six fields listed in the flow, presents them in an editable confirmation modal, and persists the record on confirm.

*AC6 — Matching behavior.* The AI upload flow matches extracted documents to existing requirements by name + authority, with license ID label as fallback, and allows the user to override the match.

*AC7 — Add Requirement — single property.* Saving with scope {{This property only}} creates one requirement on the current property and it appears in the register with status {{Missing}}.

*AC8 — Add Requirement — portfolio.* Saving with scope {{All properties in portfolio}} creates the requirement on every eligible property the user can edit, skips duplicates, and returns a created-vs-skipped summary.

*AC9 — Detail navigation.* Clicking {{View >}} on a register row opens Screen 2 for that requirement; the back link returns to the register.

*AC10 — History table.* The History table shows one row per License Record with year, date issued, coverage period, cost, and a downloadable document link. The current cycle row carries the {{current}} badge.

*AC11 — Documents table.* Every Document linked to the requirement appears with file name, upload date, uploader display name, and human-readable size.

*AC12 — Notes.* Notes display in reverse-chronological order with avatar, name, date, body; submitting a new note inserts it at the top without a page reload.

*AC13 — Upload New (detail).* Using {{+ Upload New}} on the detail screen appends a record, promotes it to {{current}}, demotes the prior current, and refreshes the header status, expiration, and cost.

*AC14 — Permissions.* Users with read-only access on the property can view the register, detail view, history, documents, and notes, but cannot upload, add requirements, or add notes. Users with edit access can perform all actions.

*AC15 — Audit trail.* Every upload, requirement creation, and note records {{actor_user_id}} and {{timestamp}} for audit purposes.

----

h2. Out of Scope

* Automated renewal submissions to issuing authorities.
* E-signature workflow for license documents (handled by existing E-Sign tab).
* Email/SMS reminder configuration (separate story).
* Bulk re-classification of historical documents already stored under the existing {{Documents}} tab.

h2. Dependencies

* AI document extraction service (shared with the Contracts upload flow).
* Existing property context and permission model from Contract Management.
* File storage service used by the existing {{Documents}} tab.

h3. *Acceptance Criteria*

h4. *1. Initial Verification Trigger*

For newly uploaded contracts, the *Cost/Unit/Year* field is not calculated immediately and displays *$0.00*.

The Cost/Unit/Year should be calculated based only on:

* *Annual Cost*
* *Number of Units per Property*

If either of these two values is missing, the system should display *“N/A.”*

However, in the current behavior:

* Even when Annual Cost and Units are available, the field initially shows *$0.00*.
* The Cost/Unit/Year only calculates and displays correctly after updating unrelated fields such as:
** Service
** Renewal Term
** Contract Term

This indicates the calculation is not triggering on initial upload or save.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Upload a new contract with Annual Cost and Units per Property filled.
# Save the contract.
# Observe Cost/Unit/Year shows *$0.00*.
# Edit the contract and update fields like Service, Renewal Term, or Contract Term.
# Save again.
# Observe Cost/Unit/Year now calculates correctly.

*Expected Result:*

* Cost/Unit/Year should calculate immediately upon upload/save when Annual Cost and Units are present.
* If either value is missing, it should display *“N/A”*, not *$0.00*.

*Actual Result:*

* Initially shows *$0.00*.
* Calculation only triggers after editing other unrelated fields.

column31:
h2. Resend Business License Request

Resend the original business license request to the vendor if the vendor did not receive the initial request or if it must be sent to a different email address.

*User Story*

As a Connexus User or Client User, I want to resend the business license upload link from the Vendor Profile, so that I can prompt the vendor to complete their business license submission without manually generating a new request.

*Acceptance Criteria*

h3. 1. Resend Link Button

*Admin UI:*
Add a *“Resend Link”* button within the Vendor Profile for Connexus Users.

*Visibility:*
The button should be available when the vendor has an active or pending business license upload requirement.

*Permissions:*
The button should only be visible to users with permission to manage vendor onboarding or business license requirements.

h3. 2. Resend Action

*Action:*
When selected, the system sends a fresh email to the vendor with a valid tokenized link to the secure business license upload portal.

*Expected Behavior:*

* Before resending the link, the user should be able to choose whether the email is sent to the original vendor email address or to an updated email address.
* If the user selects an updated email address, the system should allow them to enter and validate the new email before sending.  
* If the user enters an updated email address, that email address should be used only for this resend action and should not automatically update the Vendor Profile. The user can update the Vendor Profile separately if needed.
* The resent notification should be sent to the selected email address.
* The confirmation message should clearly display which email address the notification was sent to.
* The resent email should include a new or refreshed tokenized link.
* The link should follow the configured expiration period, defaulting to 7 days.
* The vendor should not be required to login to the platform.
* The resent email should use the same email template, subject line, and content structure defined in *CX-3328*, with a new or refreshed tokenized link. [CX-3328|https://neoito-team-connexus.atlassian.net/browse/CX-3328]

h3. 3. Confirmation to User

*System Feedback:*
After the resend action is completed, the user should see confirmation that the email was successfully resent.

h3. 4. Error Handling

*Failure State:*
If the email cannot be sent, the system should display an error message and allow the user to try again.

column1: Business License Missing Information Notification
column31:
Build a manual trigger that allows a Connexus User to send a “Business License Updates Needed” notification to a vendor when the vendor’s business license submission has been reviewed but cannot be approved because information is missing, incorrect, expired, illegible, or otherwise unacceptable.

The Connexus User must be able to enter customized correction instructions before sending the email. Those instructions must populate the email section labeled *[Insert Required Corrections / Missing Items]*. The email must include a secure, secondary tokenized link that allows the vendor to upload corrected documents or provide the missing information.

*User Story*

As a Connexus User, I want to send a missing information notification to a vendor when their business license submission is incomplete or incorrect, so that the vendor knows exactly what needs to be corrected and can resubmit the required information through a secure link.

h2. Business Purpose

Connexus needs a controlled way to notify vendors when their business license submission cannot be approved as submitted. This prevents unclear back-and-forth communication, reduces onboarding delays, and ensures vendors receive a secure path to correct or upload the required information.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

h3. 1. Missing Information Trigger

*Given* a vendor has submitted business license information,
*When* a Connexus User reviews the submission and determines that the information is incomplete, incorrect, expired, illegible, or otherwise not acceptable for approval,
*Then* the Connexus User must be able to manually trigger the missing information notification,[Email #10|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ncUK1TdMfgh9idLdHt39AHdbeiaOOumB/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=104208809598381798787&rtpof=true&sd=true].

This trigger should be available only when Connexus has received at least partial business license information from the vendor but additional information, corrections, or updated documents are required before approval.

The trigger should not automatically approve, reject, or archive the business license submission. It is strictly a request for correction or additional information.



h3. 2. Flexible Correction Field

*Functionality:*
Before sending the notification, the Connexus User must be able to enter the specific corrections, missing items, or required updates that the vendor needs to provide.

*Text Area Requirements:*

* The field should display as a multi-line text area, not a single-line input.
* The field should support approximately 10 visible lines of text by default.
* The User should be able to type, paste, and edit free-form text.
* If content exceeds the visible area, the field should allow scrolling or expansion.
* This field should be required before the notification can be sent.
* Text entered in this field should populate the email section: *[Insert Required Corrections / Missing Items]*.

h3. 3. Required Field Validation

*Given* a Connexus User opens the missing information notification flow,
*When* the User attempts to send the notification without entering any text into this field
*Then* the system must prevent the email from being sent.

The system should display a clear validation message, such as:

*Please enter the required corrections or missing items before sending this notification.*

Whitespace-only entries should not be accepted.

----

h3. 4. Email Template Content

When triggered, the system must send the following email notification.

*Email Name:* Email #10 — Business License Updates Needed
*Subject:* Action Required: Business License Updates Needed

Hi [Vendor Name],

Thank you for submitting your business license information. There are items that require correction or additional information prior to approval.

The following must be provided, corrected, or updated:

[Insert Required Corrections / Missing Items]

Please use the secure link below to upload the requested documents or provide the missing information:

[Insert Secondary Tokenized Link Here]

Please submit the request as soon as possible to help avoid delays in your onboarding process.

If you have any questions, please contact us at [insurance@joinconnexus.com|mailto:insurance@joinconnexus.com] or reach out to us at 854-204-7298.

Thank you,
The Connexus Team

*Secure Tokenized Link Generation*

When the missing information notification is triggered, The system must automatically generate a unique, secure tokenized link and insert it into the email in place of [Insert Secondary Tokenized Link Here].

Token Requirements:

* The token must be unique per notification send event, not reused across vendors or submissions.
* The token must expire after 7 days from the time the email is sent.
* The link must route the vendor to a secure upload/submission page that is pre-scoped to their vendor record and the specific business license submission.
* Expired or invalid tokens must display an appropriate error page directing the vendor to contact Connexus.
* Tokens must be stored and associated with the vendor record for traceability.

# *Submission Status Update*

When the missing information notification is successfully sent, The system must automatically update the vendor's business license submission status to *Pending Correction*.

* This status must be visible to Connexus Users in the vendor record.
* The submission must remain in Pending Correction status until the vendor resubmits or a Connexus User manually changes the status.
* The status change must not constitute an approval, rejection, or archive of the submission.

# *Confirmation Modal*

When a Connexus User clicks the action to send the missing information notification, The system must display a confirmation modal before the email is sent.

The modal must:

* Summarize the action about to be taken (e.g., _"You are about to send a Business License Updates Needed notification to [Vendor Name]."_)
* Include a *Confirm* button and a *Cancel* button.
* Only send the email upon explicit confirmation.
* Cancel must dismiss the modal without sending the email or altering the submission.

# *Send Confirmation and Error Feedback*

After the Connexus User confirms and the notification is sent:

*Success:* The system must display a success message, such as: _"Business License Updates Needed notification has been sent to [Vendor Name]."_

*Failure:* If the email fails to send, the system must display a clear error message, such as: _"The notification could not be sent. Please try again or contact support."_

The submission status must not update to Pending Correction unless the email is confirmed as successfully sent.

# *Audit Log*

Each time a missing information notification is sent, the system must create an audit log entry on the vendor record containing:

* The name and user ID of the Connexus User who triggered the notification.
* The date and timestamp the notification was sent.
* The full text of the corrections entered at the time of send.
* The tokenized link generated for that send event.

Audit log entries must be read-only and must not be editable or deletable by any user.

----

*10. Multiple Notification Sends*

A Connexus User may send the Business License Updates Needed notification to the same vendor more than once. There is no cap on the number of times this notification can be sent.

Each send event must:

* Generate a new unique tokenized link (previous links may remain active until their individual expiration).
* Create a new audit log entry.
* Re-set or maintain the submission status as Pending Correction.
