*Epic: Business License Upload for Vendors*

*Goal* Enable vendors to upload business licenses against their serviced states directly from their Vendor Profile page. The system should automatically determine which licenses are required based on the services assigned by the client and the properties associated with those services, trigger the appropriate email notifications, and extract license details from uploaded documents for audit and tracking.

# *State Resolution Logic (Client Side — During Vendor Invite)*

* When a client invites a vendor, the client selects the services the vendor will provide along with the associated properties.
* If the client sets *Property Level = Yes* and specifies a property, the system must identify that property's state and add it to the vendor's serviced states table.
* If the client sets *Property Level = No*, the system must collect all states belonging to all properties added by the client and add them to the vendor's serviced states table.
* The resolved states are saved at the vendor-service level for downstream license checks.

# *License Requirement Check (System Logic)*

Once the serviced states and assigned services are available, the system checks the service-to-license mapping reference sheet to determine license requirements per service:

* *If License Required = No* → Do not trigger any email or upload prompt. No action required.Trigger notification for connexus application. 
* *If License Required = Yes* → Proceed to check the license type breakdown below before triggering the email.
* *If both State and Federal required = Yes or Possibly* → Trigger the email for both state license and federal license requirements.
* *If either State or Federal = No (and the other = Yes)* → Trigger the email only for the applicable license type (state only or federal only, based on what is available).
* *If State Required = Yes and scope is State-Specific* → Check whether the vendor's serviced states (resolved in Step 1) are included in the defined list of applicable states for that service. If yes, include state license in the email. If no, treat state license as not required.
* *If Federal Required = Yes (if pre-1978)* → Check the *Year Built* field from the property metrics. If the property was built before 1978, not including 1978, (so 1977 and before) trigger the email with the federal license requirement included. This check must re-run every time a client adds a new property or when property metric values (specifically Year Built) are updated.

# *Email Notification to Vendor*

* The email is sent to the vendor after payment is completed and the license check confirms one or more licenses are required.
* The email content is dynamic and lists only the specific state and/or federal licenses applicable to the vendor's assigned services and resolved states.
* The email includes a link to the Business License Upload page.
* Link should open the connexus application irrespective of all the users. (Small size or big size company)
* Registered Users should directly navigate to the Login page. 
* Unregistered Users should receive an invite while they click on the join connexus button(Basim needs to confirm whether we can redirect the user to set password page directly.)

* The dialog includes a *Business License Name* dropdown, which is dynamically populated based on the services assigned to the vendor by the client. For example:
** If the client assigned *Pest Control*, the dropdown shows *Pest Control / Pesticide Application*.

column1: [TRELLO] Accepted RFP position drops to middle/bottom after clicking "Accept" on multi-property lists
column31:
[https://trello.com/c/2dhtCghh|https://trello.com/c/2dhtCghh|smart-link] 

[Connexus - Request For Proposal - 22 May 2026|https://www.loom.com/share/6d2fd0f5dc784dccaa7047c8d5ae7977]

In the RFP module, when a vendor is navigating a project with a high volume of properties and is checking/accepting them property-by-property to submit a bid, the page scroll position behaves erratically. After clicking "Accept" or transitioning to the next paginated chunk of properties, the focus is lost, leaving the page stuck in the middle or bottom of the screen instead of snapping cleanly to the top of the new dataset.

This forces vendors to constantly scroll back up to see the top of the next list, causing significant UI friction—especially on mobile layouts.

*Proposed UI/UX Fix:* We need to handle the window/container scroll state during these transitions. When a user clicks "Accept" to save a row configuration or clicks to the next page of properties, the UI should execute one of the following:

* *Option A (Recommended):* Auto-scroll smoothly to the *Top* of the property container block so the user can immediately read the next set of rows from the beginning.
* *Option B:* Maintain absolute locked position relative to the active element wrapper so the vendor does not lose context.

Given previous feedback regarding scrolling fatigue from clients like Fitch Irick, snapping smoothly to the *Top* of the next section is the ideal behavior.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

* Prevent user from proceeding to the next step until a valid DOB is entered.

* Validate minimum age requirement based on business rules.
* Example: User must be at least 18 years old.

*Validation Condition:*

* DOB must be at least 18 years before the current date.
* If age is below the minimum allowed age, display validation error.

column1: Vendor Status Management and Action Handling
column31:
*User Story*

As a user, I want to view and manage vendors in the vendor list page — including their registration status, invitation status, and available actions — so that I can understand each vendor's current state and take appropriate actions based on their status.

*Acceptance Criteria*

*Vendor List Population*

# The vendor list must display vendors from all four sources: invited via the Invite Vendor button, preferred vendors from the client page, current vendors from the client page, and vendors created via contract management.

*Vendor Status Rules*

# A vendor invited via the Invite Vendor button must have a status of *Unregistered* until they complete registration, at which point their status automatically changes to *Active*.
# A vendor sourced from the preferred vendor list or current vendor list must have a status of *Active*.
# A vendor created via contract management must have a status of *Draft*.
# A vendor inactivated on the Connexus side for a client must appear in the vendor list with a status of *Inactive*.

*Vendor Invited Flag*

# When a vendor is invited via the Invite Vendor button, the _Vendor Invited_ flag must be set to *Yes*.
# Vendors sourced from the preferred or current vendor lists must have the _Vendor Invited_ flag set to *No* by default.

*Action Availability Rules*

# A vendor with _Vendor Invited = No_ must show an *Invite* option in the three-dot menu, allowing the user to invite them.
# A vendor with _Vendor Invited = Yes_ must not show the Invite option; instead, a *Resend* option must be available in its place.
# An *Inactive* vendor must not have the Invite option available — inviting an inactive vendor is not permitted.
# If a vendor's business is verified (_Business Verified = Yes_), the *Invite*, *Resend*, and *KYB* actions must all be disabled for that vendor.

[https://www.figma.com/design/3FPSHqsbMdKCxibVTjOadS/Connexus---February-2026?node-id=13704-20068&t=ent0NHGHjxjSg7L6-4|https://www.figma.com/design/3FPSHqsbMdKCxibVTjOadS/Connexus---February-2026?node-id=13704-20068&t=ent0NHGHjxjSg7L6-4]

[~accountid:712020:190cfc19-da73-4986-9756-ed90d8aedc7e] *Edge Cases:*


* If a vendor in Active, Draft , Unregistered is changed to Inactive before completing the verification process, the Resend Invitation and KYB Verification options should be hidden.

* If the vendor's Business Verified status is set to Yes without completing the verification process, the Send Invitation, Resend Invitation, and KYB Verification options should be hidden.

column1: Property insurance client Id addition
column31:
h2. Summary

Include the client identifier when submitting property insurance documents to the external AI extraction service.

h2. Background

When a property insurance document is uploaded, the system creates a background processing job and submits the file to an external AI service for data extraction. Currently, the submission payload includes the background job ID, file details, and (for re-uploads) the existing policy ID. However, the client identifier is not included in the payload sent to the AI service.

h2. What Changed

The system now resolves the client associated with the tenant (which is already provided during file upload) and passes the client ID through to the AI extraction service as part of the submission request. This allows the external service to have client context during document processing.

h2. Impact

* No changes to the frontend or public API contracts
* No database schema changes
* The client ID is derived server-side from the existing tenant information, so no additional input is required from users
* Applies to both new uploads and re-uploads of property insurance documents

column1: Vendor dashboard : landing Page of vendor
column31:
*User Story*

As a vendor, I want to land on a dashboard after logging in (via the email link from the business license page) so that I can quickly view my RFP summary, monitor business license upload requests from clients, and navigate to the relevant modules for further action.

*Acceptance Criteria*

# *Entry point & navigation*

AC1: The vendor is redirected to the dashboard immediately after logging in via the business license email link. No intermediate pages or redirects should appear between login and the dashboard.

AC2: The dashboard is the default landing page for any authenticated vendor session. If the vendor navigates away and logs back in, they should always return to the dashboard first.

AC3: The sidebar navigation is visible on the dashboard and allows the vendor to access other modules including Request for Proposal, Business License Uploads,contact management,Role managent. 

# *RFP overview section*

AC4: The RFP overview section is displayed prominently at the top of the dashboard and contains four metric cards — Total RFP, RFP Accepted, RFP Pending, and RFP Submitted - each showing its respective count.

AC5: Each metric card is visually distinct with a unique status color and icon to allow the vendor to differentiate between RFP states at a glance (e.g. pending shown in amber, accepted in green, submitted in blue).

AC6: Each metric card reflects the correct live count fetched from the backend, scoped to the logged-in vendor's data only.



# *Business license uploads section*

AC8: The business license uploads section is displayed below the RFP overview and contains two summary tiles - Pending and Uploaded -showing the respective counts of client upload requests.

AC9: The Pending tile is visually highlighted (e.g. amber) to draw the vendor's attention to requests that require action. The Uploaded tile uses a neutral or success color to indicate resolved items.

AC10: Below the summary tiles, a list of the most recent client requests is displayed. Each request row includes the client's Logo, a description of the request (e.g. "Client has requested a business license upload"), a status badge (e.g. "New"), and the time elapsed since the request was made (e.g. "2 minutes ago").

AC11: Each request row includes a "View Details" link. Clicking it navigates the vendor to the detailed view of that specific business license request where they can review and take action.

AC12: The section header includes a "View All" link. Clicking it navigates the vendor to the full Business License Uploads module where all pending and uploaded records are listed and can be managed.

AC13: If there are no pending requests, a meaningful empty state message is displayed (e.g. "No new requests at this time") so the vendor is not left with a blank section.

# *Data display & status*

AC14: Any business license request that has been submitted by a client but not yet acted upon by the vendor is counted and displayed under the Pending tile.

AC15: Any business license upload that has been uploaded is counted and reflected under the uploaded tile.

AC16: The dashboard counts and request list are updated to reflect the most current data on page load and on manual refresh. Stale data should not persist across sessions.

AC17: All data displayed on the dashboard is scoped to the logged-in vendor and does not surface records belonging to other vendors or clients outside their scope.

*Out of Scope*

Editing or approving RFPs directly from the dashboard · uploading documents directly from the dashboard · real-time push notifications or auto-refresh without manual reload · admin or role-specific dashboard variants.

column1: Vendor License Algorithm
column31:
h2. US: 1 State Resolution Logic (Client Side — During Vendor Invite)

*As a* system, *I want to* resolve and store the applicable states for a vendor-service assignment during the vendor invite flow, *So that* the vendor's serviced states table is accurately populated for downstream license requirement checks.

*Background:* When a client invites a vendor, they assign services and associated properties. The system must determine which states are in scope for each vendor-service assignment based on whether the client sets Property Level to Yes or No.

*Acceptance Criteria:*

* Given a client is completing a vendor invite and sets Property Level = *Yes* for a service,
** And the client selects a specific property,
** Then the system must look up the state associated with that property from the property record,
** And add that state to the vendor's *Serviced States* table, scoped to the specific vendor-service assignment.
* Given a client sets Property Level = *No* for a service during vendor invite,
** Then the system must retrieve all properties associated with that client,
** And collect all unique states across those properties,
** And add each unique state to the vendor's *Serviced States* table, scoped to the vendor-service assignment.
* If multiple properties share the same state, that state must appear only once in the serviced states table.
* If the property does not have a state on record, the system must surface a validation warning and prevent the invite from completing until the property's state is available.
* If any client property is missing a state value (Property Level = No scenario), the system must log a data quality warning but must not block invite completion (partial state coverage is acceptable in this scenario).
* Resolved states must be stored in a structured *Serviced States* table linked to the vendor-service record.
* The stored states must survive session termination and be readable by the license check engine at any later point.
* If a vendor is assigned multiple services, each service must maintain its own independent serviced states list (states are scoped per service, not shared across services for that vendor).
* A read-only audit log entry must be created recording: vendor ID, service, resolved states, resolution method (property-level yes/no), and timestamp.

h2. US 2 : License Requirement Check (System Logic)

*As a* system, *I want to* evaluate license requirements per vendor-service assignment based on the service mapping and resolved states, *So that* the vendor receives an accurate and targeted email containing only the license requirements that apply to them, or no email at all when none are required.

*Background:* Once the serviced states and assigned services are available, the system checks the service-to-license mapping reference sheet to determine license requirements per service. The system must evaluate Federal and State requirement levels independently and construct the email accordingly — or suppress it entirely when no license is required.

*Acceptance Criteria:*

* Given the system evaluates a vendor-service assignment and the Service Mapping record for that service has *License Required = No*,
** Then the system must *not* send any license-related email to the vendor,
** And must *not* present any license upload prompt to the vendor,
** And must *not* queue any license review task internally.
** The system must trigger a *Connexus application notification* confirming that no license action is required for this vendor-service pairing.
* Given a vendor-service assignment where *License Required = Yes*,
** The system must independently evaluate the *Federal Req Level* and *State Req Level* from the Service Mapping sheet before constructing the email.
** The system must not send a license email until both the serviced states (from Epic 1) and the service mapping data are available.
* Given *License Required = Yes*,
** And *Federal Req Level = Yes or Possibly*,
** And *State Req Level = Yes or Possibly*,
** Then the license email sent to the vendor must include *both* state license and federal license requirement details.
** "Possibly" is treated as an active trigger and must be included in the email — it is not treated as optional or suppressible.
* Given *License Required = Yes*,
** And *Federal Req Level = No* while *State Req Level = Yes or Possibly*,
** Then the email must include *state license requirements only* — no federal section.
* Given *License Required = Yes*,
** And *State Req Level = No* while *Federal Req Level = Yes or Possibly*,
** Then the email must include *federal license requirements only* — no state section.
* Given *License Required = Yes* and *State Req Level = State-Specific*,
** The system must retrieve the vendor's *Serviced States* (resolved in Epic 1) for this service,
** And compare those states against the *Which States Specifically* list defined in the Service Mapping sheet for that service.
** If *one or more* of the vendor's serviced states appear in the applicable states list → include the state license requirement in the email and specify the relevant states.
** If *none* of the vendor's serviced states appear in the applicable states list → treat the state license as not applicable; do not include it in the email.
** Where the *Which States* column is marked *"All"* (not "State-Specific"), this check does not apply — the state requirement is universal and must always be included when triggered.
* Given *License Required = Yes* and *Federal Req Level = Yes (if pre-1978)*,
** The system must retrieve the *Year Built* value from the property metrics record for each property associated with this vendor-service assignment.
** If *Year Built < 1978* (i.e., 1977 or earlier) for any associated property, AND the federal license is marked as *No* in the Service Mapping sheet for that service → include the federal license requirement in the email.
** If *Year Built ≥ 1978* for all associated properties, AND the federal license is marked as *No* in the Service Mapping sheet for that service → do not include the federal license requirement in the email.
** If *Year Built is null or missing* → treat as unknown; flag for data completeness review and do not trigger the federal requirement until the value is confirmed.
** This check must *re-execute automatically* when a client adds a new property to an existing vendor-service assignment, OR when the *Year Built* field in property metrics is updated for any property already linked to this vendor-service assignment.
** If a re-run results in a changed outcome (e.g., a pre-1978 property is now linked where previously none existed), the system must send an updated or supplemental license notification to the vendor.
* The email must clearly distinguish state from federal requirements and present each in its own clearly labelled section.
* The system must never include a license section in the email when its corresponding requirement level is "No."
* All outcomes must be recorded in the audit log with: vendor ID, service name, outcome, and timestamp.

h2. Summary: Decision Matrix

||License Required||Federal Req Level||State Req Level||Action||
|No|—|—|No email. Trigger Connexus notification only.|
|Yes|Yes / Possibly|Yes / Possibly|Email with both State + Federal requirements.|
|Yes|No|Yes / Possibly|Email with State requirement only.|
|Yes|Yes / Possibly|No|Email with Federal requirement only.|
|Yes|NO (if pre-1978)|Any|Check Year Built. Include Federal only if any property built < 1978.|
|Yes|Any|State-Specific|Check vendor's serviced states vs. applicable states list. Include State only if match found.|

*Summary* 

A vendor was previously invited by *Client A* and successfully completed the onboarding process, including *Business Verification* and *Payment*.

When *Client B* attempts to invite the same vendor, the invitation is blocked with a conflict error stating that the vendor has already been invited. This prevents the vendor from being onboarded by additional clients.

Per the expected business process, a vendor who has already completed verification should not be required to complete verification again until the verification expires (1 year validity). The vendor should be able to proceed directly to payment (and have verification automatically recognized and skipped) when invited by another client.

h3. Preconditions

* Vendor has already been invited by Client A.
* Vendor has completed:
** Business Verification
** Payment
* Vendor verification status is still valid (within 1 year).

h3. Steps to *Replicate*

# Login as *Client A*.
# Invite a vendor and complete the entire onboarding flow.
# Confirm the vendor is successfully verified and onboarded.
# Login as *Client B*.
# Navigate to *Invite Vendor*.
# Enter the same vendor legal name and details.
# Click *Invite*.

h3. Actual Result

The invite request fails with *HTTP 409 Conflict*.

Error displayed:

"A vendor with this legal name has already been invited to the system."

The second client is unable to invite the vendor.

h3. Expected Result

The system should allow multiple clients to invite the same vendor.

If the vendor already has a valid verification:

*  The invitation should be created successfully. 
*  The vendor should not be required to complete Business Verification again. 
*  Verification status should be reused across clients. 
*  The vendor should proceed directly to Payment

column1: Notes Section Implementation for Compliance Records

*Summary* Add Notes Section to Compliance Record Detail View

----

*Story* As a property manager or compliance reviewer, I want to add and view notes on individual compliance records so that I can document review activity, flag issues, and maintain a clear audit trail of record-level decisions.

----

*Description* When a user clicks into a compliance record from the Compliance and Records dashboard, the record detail view should include a Notes section. This section allows users to log timestamped, attributed notes tied to that specific record.

Notes are intended to be there for the Client Users to keep notes for these as required.

----

*Acceptance Criteria*

* [ ] A "Notes" section is visible on the compliance record detail view, accessible by clicking a row from the Compliance and Records dashboard
* [ ] Users can add a new note via a text input within the detail view
* [ ] Each note captures and displays: username (auto-populated from logged-in user), date/time entered (auto-populated on save), and note body text
* [ ] Notes are displayed in reverse chronological order (most recent first)
* [ ] Notes are read-only once saved (no editing or deletion by end users)
* [ ] Notes persist as part of the record and are retrievable on subsequent views
* [ ] Notes are included in the audit trail / activity log for the record
* [ ] Empty note submission is prevented (validation on save)

----

*Out of Scope*

* Note editing or deletion by end users (admin-only consideration for future story)
* Tagging or categorizing notes
* Notifications or mentions within notes

----

*Dependencies / Notes for Dev*

* Username should pull from the authenticated session, not be a free-text field
* Date/time should be stored in UTC, displayed in user's local timezone
* Confirm whether notes live in a separate {{compliance_record_notes}} table or as a JSON array on the record — recommend separate table for query/audit flexibility

----

column1: Individual License Data Detail View
column31:
*Summary* Individual License Detail View — Accessible from Compliance & Records Dashboard

----

*Story* As a Client user or a Connexus user, I want to click into any compliance record from the Compliance and Records dashboard and view a complete detail record so that I can see all data, issuing authority information, contact details, historical records, and internal notes in one place without navigating away or exporting.  I can also view additional details which include a website field, a username field and an encrypted password field.  This information 

----

*Description* When a user clicks a row on the Compliance and Records dashboard, a detail view (modal or dedicated page — TBD by design) should open for that record. The detail view is organized into five distinct sections mirroring the Individual License Data structure, and serves as the single source of truth for a given compliance record.

All sections below should render in a read-only display state by default, with an Edit mode available for all fields.

----

*Acceptance Criteria*

*Section 1 — Record Identification*

* [ ] Displays: Property, Compliance Category, Record Type, License / Record #, Issue Date, Expiration Date, Total Cost, Status
* [ ] Status field uses a color-coded badge (e.g., Active, Expiring Soon, Expired, Pending)
* [ ] Issue Date and Expiration Date display in the format (MM/DD/YYYY)

*Section 2 — Issuing Authority*

* [ ] Displays: Authority Name, Property Account #, Website URL, Username, Password
* [ ] Password field is masked by default with a show/hide toggle
* [ ] Website URL renders as a clickable hyperlink

*Section 3 — Primary Contact at Issuing Authority*

* [ ] Displays: First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone
* [ ] Email renders as a clickable mailto link
* [ ] Phone renders as a clickable tel link

*Section 4 — Comments & Notes*

* [ ] Notes table displays columns: Username, Date, Comment
* [ ] Username is auto-populated from the authenticated session (not a free-text field)
* [ ] Date is auto-populated on save (stored UTC, displayed in user's local timezone)
* [ ] Notes are displayed in reverse chronological order
* [ ] Notes are read-only once saved — no editing or deletion by end users
* [ ] Empty note submission is blocked with inline validation
* [ ] New note entry is available via a text input + "Add Note" button within the section
* [ ] Notes are included in the record's audit trail / activity log

*Section 5 — Prior Records (Same Compliance Category — Historical Archive)*

* [ ] Section renders a table with columns: Record Type, Issuing Authority, Issue Date, Expiration Date, License / Record #, Total Cost, Status
* [ ] Rows are scoped to the same Compliance Category as the current record (historical archive only — not the active record)
* [ ] Rows are sortable by Issue Date (default: most recent first)
* [ ] Prior Records allow the file to be downloaded
* [ ] New prior records can be manually added by authorized users via an inline row entry or form

----

*Layout & UX Notes*

* Sections render in order: Record Identification → Issuing Authority → Primary Contact → Comments & Notes → Prior Records
* Detail view must be accessible via row click from the Compliance & Records dashboard
* Entry point behavior (modal vs. dedicated route) to be confirmed in design — recommend modal with full-screen expand option for usability
* On mobile/narrow viewports, sections should stack vertically

----

*Out of Scope*

* Automated renewal workflows triggered from this view (separate epic)
* Bulk editing of prior records
* Note editing or deletion by end users (admin story to be created separately)

----

*Dependencies / Dev Notes*

* Confirm data model: does {{prior_records}} live as a child table of {{compliance_records}} keyed on {{compliance_category}}? Recommend a separate {{compliance_record_history}} table for query flexibility
* Password storage for issuing authority credentials must use encryption at rest — confirm approach with Dom/NeoITO before building
* Notes should write to a {{compliance_record_notes}} table (not a JSON blob on the record) to support audit queries

*User Story* As a Connexus Admin , I want a dedicated Connexus Verify >Vendors section with comprehensive compliance status management, inline status editing, and a structured vendor invite workflow, so that I can efficiently monitor, manage, and onboard vendors while maintaining full compliance visibility and audit traceability.

# *Navigation — Side Nav Restructure - Varun & ramesh*

1.1 Rename Nav Item — Rename the existing "Vendors" side navigation item to "Connexus Verify."

1.2 Dropdown Sub-Items — Add a dropdown under "Connexus Verify" in the side nav containing at minimum: Vendors (links to vendor list) and any additional sub-items as defined by the product roadmap. 

# *Vendor List Page — Column & Header Changes* 

2.1 Capitalize Column Header — The column header "Vendor Name" must be capitalized.-Ramesh

2.2 Vendor Name Hyperlink — Vendor names must be rendered as hyperlinks in both Client and Connexus Admin views. Client View: opens vendor profile in a new tab in read-only/view mode. Connexus Admin View: opens the full vendor profile page in a new tab with edit access. -Ramesh

2.21 Vendor permission handling for client user (both vendor profile and vendor contacts) -Varun

All status will be handled on in another Ticket.

2.7 Name change from KYB verification to Business verification for the three dot action item

# *Inline Status Editing*

3.1 Inline Dropdowns (Connexus Admin View) — All status columns (Compliance Standing, Business Verified, Business Licenses, Insurance Compliant) must support inline dropdown editing directly from the vendor list table in the Connexus Admin view. Each dropdown must reflect only the valid status values defined per column.

# *Row Action Menu (Three-Dot / Kebab Menu)*

4.1 Client View Actions — The three-dot menu per row in the Client view must include: Invite to Connexus Verify, Resend Invitation, Business Verification,View Details

4.2 Connexus Admin View Actions — The three-dot menu per row in the Connexus Admin view must include: Audit Log (opens a tabular audit log for that vendor record), Upload Document (grayed out/disabled for all records), Invite Vendor (triggers the Invite Vendor workflow), Resend Email (resends the last invitation email to the vendor),view details

# *Invite Vendor Workflow (Connexus Admin) - Vysakh and Ramesh* 

5.1 Entry Points — Connexus Admin can initiate the Invite Vendor flow from: the "+ Invite Vendor" button in the top-right of the vendor list page, or the "Invite Vendor" option in the row-level three-dot action menu.

5.2 Client Pre-Mapping — When a Connexus Admin initiates an invite from the vendor list page, the currently selected client (from the "Client Legal Name" search/filter box) must be automatically pre-populated in the invite workflow. The admin should not need to re-select the client.

5.3 Step 1: Company Search & Selection — Display a "Search Company" input to search existing vendors in the system. Show results as a 2-column card grid, each card displaying: company name, company legal name, website URL, and address. Allow the admin to select one card via radio button. Display result count (e.g., "6 results found!"). If the desired company is not listed, provide a "Create as a New Vendor" option with a text input pre-filled with the searched company name. Bottom actions: Cancel and Continue.

5.4 Step 2: Vendor Invite Form — After selecting or creating a vendor, display a form with the following sections:(same invite form from client )



# *Change Status Modal (Exempt Override)*

7.1 Access — Accessible from the "Audit Log" option in the Connexus Admin row-level action menu.

7.2 Display — Must render as a conversation modalwith at minimum the following data : Date/Timestamp, Action/Event, Changed By (user), Previous Value, New Value, Notes.

8.1 Business Verified Notification — When a vendor's Business Verified status changes to "Yes" (auto-triggered post-KYB and payment), Connexus Admin users must receive an in-platform notification identifying the vendor by name.

9.1 The public-facing vendor registration/onboarding page must include client brand assets (logo, colors) so vendors experience a branded registration flow tied to the inviting client.

column1: vendor compliance Status
column31:
*User story*

As a *Connexus User*, I want to view and manage the real-time compliance status of each vendor across all four verification categories :  Business Verified, Business License, and Insurance Requirements  from a single inline dashboard, so that I can quickly assess vendor readiness, apply exemptions where needed, and ensure all status transitions are fully audited.

*GLOBAL ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA*

* All four status fields must display as dropdowns with only the valid values defined per category
* Every status  change must log: Updated By (name), Type (Client or Connexus), and Timestamp
* Every exemption override must capture: User, Date, Who Approved, and a mandatory Notes field
* Overall Compliance Standing must auto-recalculate whenever business license and insurance compliance status changes
* All status changes  manual and automated  must appear in the audit log

*SUB-STORY 1 — COMPLIANCE STANDING* 
As a compliance manager, the system shall automatically derive a single *Compliance Standing* for each vendor by combining the *Business License* status and the *Insurance Compliance* status, so I can see one consolidated status without checking each requirement separately.

h2. Functional acceptance criteria

*Single derived value.* Every valid combination of Business License status and Insurance status shall produce exactly one Compliance Standing. No combination may return blank, null, or more than one value. All 77 combinations (11 license × 7 insurance) must be covered.

*Priority rule.* The Compliance Standing shall equal the status with the *higher priority* of the two inputs, where priority (highest → lowest) is: Expired > Requirements Not Met > Pending > Not Started > Under Review > Expiring > Request Sent > Compliant.

 *Compliant only when both are clear.* A standing of *Compliant* shall be returned only when both inputs resolve to Compliant (or to a non-applicable license status — see AC6).

 *Inprocess mapping.* A license status of *Inprocess* shall be treated at the *Under Review* priority level.

*Non-applicable license statuses.* When the license status is *Exempt – Notes Mandatory* or *None Required*, the Compliance Standing shall be driven entirely by the Insurance status (the license side does not contribute). _Note: Exempt requires a note — see AC9._

*Tie handling.* When both inputs resolve to the same priority level, the standing shall be that shared status (e.g., Not Started + Not Started → Not Started).

 *Exempt note enforcement.* A license status of *Exempt – Notes Mandatory* shall not be savable/valid unless an accompanying note is present.

h2. Scenario examples (Given / When / Then)

||#||Given Business License||And Insurance||Then Standing||
|1|Not Started|Not Started|*Not Started*|
|2|Compliant|Expired|*Expired*|
|3|Level 1 Pending|Compliant|*Pending*|
|4|Expiring|Requirements Not Met|*Requirements Not Met*|
|5|None Required|Compliant|*Compliant*|
|6|Exempt – Notes Mandatory|Under Review|*Under Review*|
|7|Inprocess|Compliant|*Under Review*|
|8|Compliant|Compliant|*Compliant*|
|9|Request Sent|Expiring|*Expiring*|
|10|Expired|Compliant|*Expired*|

h2. Edge / negative cases

 When a source status changes, the Compliance Standing shall recalculate (real-time or on the defined refresh cycle — specify which).



*SUB-STORY 2 — BUSINESS VERIFIED* 

As a Connexus User, I want to view the real-time Business Verified status for each vendor so that I can confirm the KYB outcome, track email invitation progress, and apply or review exemptions as needed.

Acceptance Criteria:

* *Blank* — default state when vendor has not been invited; system generated 
* *Yes* — set automatically after KYB/KYC passes and vendor payment is complete; system generated only, no manual trigger
* *Email Sent* — set automatically once the invite is dispatched and SES confirms delivery; system generated
* *Email Opened* — set automatically when vendor opens the invitation email; system generated
* *Requirements Not Met* — set automatically when vendor fails KYB/KYC, EIDV, KYB2, or AML checks; system generated
* *Exempt* — set manually by Connexus User only; applicable for client-level exemptions only; requires User, Date, Approver, and Notes; once set to Exempt for a specific client, 
** From Email send,Email opened, Requirement not met,connexus user can change the status to exempt with mandatory notes. 
** If the business verified is blank or yes, inline edit will be disabled.
** If the vendor status is changed to exempt,it will applicable only on the client level. 
** if another client invites the same vendor, it will go through the normal process. 
** If payment is completed before exempt, then it should display in the vendor proile page and should track from the system side.
* Audit log must show Updated By name AND type (Client or Connexus) for every change
* Notes field must be available and mandatory when Connexus User changes status to Exempt
* IF vendor invited =NO, business verifed inline edit should be disable
* Payment and related process should be skipped, if the business veriified status is changed to Exempt. 
* As connfirmed by [~accountid:712020:4a69d865-c1a6-4c27-aa30-6a8766fe1bc6] the payment link at the intial stage will be done offline and store the data. Later stage this should be added to our current system (Especially next year as subscription should be inplace.)
* As confirmed by [~accountid:712020:4a69d865-c1a6-4c27-aa30-6a8766fe1bc6] even business veirifed =exempt for one client, payment should be applicable for another client but will not skip the business verified. Exempt will be specific for each client.



*SUB-STORY 3 — BUSINESS LICENSE* 

As a Connexus User, I want to track and update the Business License verification status for each vendor so that I can confirm license compliance across all required services, manage the Level 1 and Level 2 review workflow, and apply exemptions where applicable.

Acceptance Criteria:

* *Not Started* — default system-generated state; should be triggered when vendor invited =yes and business license required as per the business license algorithm.(this logic will be implemented once the business license module is implemented)
* *Compliant* — set when all required licenses are on hand and none are expiring within 30+ days; manual by Connexus User
* *Level 1 Pending* — set when license data has been extracted and is visible but not yet approved; manual by Connexus User
* *Level 2 Pending* — set by Level 1 Reviewer when supervisor review is required; manual by Connexus User
* *Requirements Not Met* — set when vendor does not have the required licenses; cascades to overall Compliance Standing = Requirements Not Met; manual by Connexus User
* *Inprocess*— set when multiple files in federal or state are not fullly compliant 
* *Request Sent* — set when a license request has been sent to the vendor; manual by Connexus User
* *Exempt* — set when all licenses are waived by the client; requires User, Date, Approver, and Notes; manual by Connexus User.Notes and audit log are mandatory 
* *Expiring* — set when 1 or more licenses are within 30 days of expiration; must trigger a notification; manual by Connexus User.As of now no emails wil be triggered [~accountid:712020:4a69d865-c1a6-4c27-aa30-6a8766fe1bc6] 
* *Expired* — set when all required licenses have expired
* *None Required* — set when no licenses are required based on the vendor's service type(s); manual by Connexus User
* Audit log for Business License status changes is required.

*SUB-STORY 4 — INSURANCE REQUIREMENTS* 

As a Connexus User, I want to track the insurance compliance status for each vendor across all invited properties and services so that I can confirm full coverage, manage under-review items, apply exemptions where appropriate, and receive timely notifications for expiring or lapsed policies.

Acceptance Criteria:

* *Not Started* — default system-generated state before the insurance process begins
* *Compliant* — set when vendor is fully compliant on all services for all invited properties; manual by Connexus User
* *Invited* — set when vendor has been invited to the insurance process; triggers In-Process at the Compliance Standing level; manual by Connexus User
* *Under Review* — set when items are outstanding and the vendor must address them; triggers In-Process at the Compliance Standing level; manual by Connexus User
* *Expiring* — set when policy is approaching expiration; must trigger a notification; cascades to Compliance Standing = Expiring; manual by Connexus User
* *Expired* — set when policy has expired; cascades to overall Compliance Standing = Requirements Not Met; manual by Connexus User
* *Exempt* — set when no insurance is required; requires User, Date, Approver, and Notes; manual by Connexus User
* *Requirements Not Met* — set when vendor does not have the required insurance coverage; cascades to overall Compliance Standing = Requirements Not Met; manual by Connexus User
* Audit log for Insurance Requirements status changes is required (open item — confirm implementation scope.

column1: Phase 1 : Common Orchestration Layer
column31:
Build the common orchestration foundation required to support Temporal-based background workflows for RFP-related operations.

This story covers the shared workflow infrastructure used by all orchestration flows, including workflow run tracking, execution tracking, batch tracking, stage configuration, outbox signaling, recovery handling, manual retry support, status/admin APIs, observability, and a dummy workflow for end-to-end validation.

The implementation should establish a reusable orchestration layer where:

* PostgreSQL stores durable workflow, execution, batch, configuration, and outbox state.
* Temporal controls orchestration and workflow progression.
* SQS dispatches batch execution work to background workers.
* Workers process batches safely using idempotent claim, heartbeat, transaction, and outbox patterns.
* Outbox publisher reliably sends completion signals back to Temporal.
* Recovery sweeper detects and repairs stuck or missed workflow states.
* Manual retry and admin/status APIs are available for operational support.
* Metrics, alerts, dashboard, and runbook are added for monitoring.
* Dummy workflow validates the full orchestration lifecycle before enabling real RFP workflows.

The goal of this story is to complete the reusable common orchestration layer so that Vendor Draft Generation and RFP Sending can be built on top of the same reliable workflow foundation.

Acceptance Criteria:

* Common workflow schema, enums, models, indexes, and migrations are implemented.
* Shared workflow types, validation schemas, idempotency helpers, retry helpers, completion rules, and stage progression helpers are implemented and tested.
* Stage configuration service supports defaults, database config, environment overrides, validation, and immutable run snapshots.
* Common repositories support workflow runs, executions, batches, and outbox events.
* Temporal worker app is created with workflow/activity registration and local startup support.
* Common Temporal activities are implemented with retry policies, timeouts, and idempotency tests.
* SQS dispatch layer is implemented with validation, queue abstraction, persistence, and idempotency checks.
* Common batch worker framework supports message parsing, batch claiming, heartbeat, chunk processing, final transaction, outbox insertion, and safe SQS deletion.
* Outbox publisher sends Temporal signals reliably and handles retries, stale locks, duplicate signals, metrics, and integration tests.
* Recovery sweeper detects missing Temporal execution, stuck batches, stale heartbeat, missing/unsent outbox, stale processing outbox, and due failed outbox events.
* Manual retry foundation is available through API, DTOs, validation, permissions, audit fields, and retry execution support.
* Status and admin APIs expose run, batch, outbox, and failure details with pagination and permission checks.
* Dummy workflow validates success, partial failure, system failure, retry, manual retry, Continue-As-New, and end-to-end behavior.
* Observability includes required metrics, alerts, dashboard, and runbook.
* Phase 1 validation confirms migration, Temporal worker, dummy SQS worker, outbox delivery, missed signal recovery, duplicate SQS handling, worker crash recovery, Continue-As-New, recovery sweeper, status API, and metrics.

column1: Phase 2 : Vendor Draft Generation Scaling
column31:
Implement the Temporal-based Vendor Draft Generation workflow on top of the common orchestration layer.

This story covers the changes required to move large-scale vendor draft generation into an orchestrated background workflow. The workflow should create and track vendor draft generation runs, split work into batches, process draft inserts through workers, support retries and manual review, preserve draft snapshots, and validate the full flow through integration and load testing.

The implementation should ensure that each generated vendor draft row is tied to a specific {{draftGenerationRunId}}, so repeated draft generation for the same RFP does not conflict and a completed draft run can later be selected as the source snapshot for Send RFP.

Acceptance Criteria:

* Schema changes are implemented for {{RfpVendorDraft.draftGenerationRunId}}, including FK, indexes, migration, Prisma client generation, and legacy read compatibility.
* Stage configuration is added for {{RFP_VENDOR_DRAFT_GENERATION:DRAFT_INSERT}}, including batch size, chunk size, max attempts, retry backoff, active batch limits, SQS visibility timeout, heartbeat intervals, and config tests.
* API changes are implemented to support orchestrated vendor draft generation behind a feature flag.
* {{pottential-vendors.service.ts}} branches to the orchestration path when enabled.
* API validates the RFP, validates input size threshold, creates {{BackgroundWorkflowRun}} with type {{RFP_VENDOR_DRAFT_GENERATION}}, snapshots stage config, starts {{RfpDraftWorkflow}}, and returns {{202}} with {{workflowRunId}}.
* Legacy small vendor draft generation path remains available behind the feature flag.
* {{RfpDraftWorkflow}} is implemented to load run state, load config snapshot, calculate draft batch ranges, create initial {{DRAFT_INSERT}} batches, dispatch draft batches to SQS, wait for {{batchCompleted}} signals, track handled batch ids, create retry batches, apply Continue-As-New thresholds, and finalize the draft run.
* Draft batch worker is implemented to parse batch execution messages, claim batches, load run metadata, build draft insert records, set {{draftGenerationRunId = workflowRunId}}, insert drafts idempotently, classify row-level failures where available, update batch status, insert outbox events, and delete SQS messages after commit.
* Retry and manual review behavior is implemented for failed or exhausted draft batches.
* Admin failed draft batch view is available.
* Draft cleanup compatibility is handled safely by disabling hard deletes for orchestrated draft runs, adding snapshot-aware cleanup, avoiding cleanup while active send runs reference the draft run, and using {{isRemoved = true}} where audit is required.
* Integration tests validate API response, workflow batch creation, worker insert behavior, duplicate SQS handling, outbox-to-Temporal progression, and recovery sweeper repair.
* Load tests are completed using realistic vendor and property counts.
* DB CPU, DB connections, batch size, chunk size, and concurrency are measured and tuned.
* Phase 2 validation confirms vendor draft generation works end to end locally and in staging.
* Draft rows are tied to {{draftGenerationRunId}}.
* Repeated draft generation for the same RFP does not conflict.
* Draft run can be selected as Send RFP snapshot.
* Failed draft batches retry correctly.
* Manual retry works for draft failures.
* Cleanup does not remove active snapshots.
* Load test results are accepted.

!image (11).png|width=1356,alt="image (11).png"!

Over these two phases, we built and tested a new, reliable system for handling large RFP jobs in the background.

Phase 1 set up the "engine" that runs these jobs safely. We confirmed it can start jobs, automatically retry them if something goes wrong, and pick up exactly where it left off even if the system crashes or restarts,  without ever doing the same work twice or losing anything. If a job repeatedly fails, it's automatically flagged for a person to review instead of failing silently. We also added live status tracking and health monitoring so we can always see what's happening.

Phase 2 used that engine to power one real feature: creating RFP vendor drafts in bulk. We confirmed that submitting a large request kicks off the job correctly, all the records get created accurately, nothing gets duplicated, and the system recovers on its own if a step is interrupted. We also ran it under heavy, real-world-sized loads to make sure it stays fast and stable, and tuned its settings for the best performance.

In short: RFP jobs that used to be risky at large scale are now automatic, self-healing, fully trackable, and proven to work under load.

column31:
Implement the Temporal-based RFP Sending workflow on top of the common orchestration layer and Vendor Draft Generation snapshot.

This story covers the changes required to move Send RFP into an orchestrated background workflow. The workflow should create and track send runs, use a completed vendor draft generation run as the source snapshot, prepare recipients, create vendor responses, generate documents, send emails, finalize the RFP business state, support retries and manual review, and validate the full flow through integration, chaos, and load testing.

The implementation should ensure that large RFP sends return quickly from the API with a {{202}} response while the actual heavy processing is handled asynchronously through Temporal, SQS, ECS workers, and PostgreSQL state tracking.

Acceptance Criteria:

* Schema changes are implemented for {{RfpSendLog.backgroundWorkflowRunId}} and RFP send recipient execution tracking fields.
* Required indexes are added for recipient preparation, vendor response creation, document generation, email send execution, retry eligibility, and manual review lookup.
* Migration is added, Prisma client is generated, and existing send recipient reads continue to work.
* Send stage configuration is added for {{RFP_SEND:RECIPIENT_PREPARATION}}, {{RFP_SEND:VENDOR_RESPONSE_CREATION}}, {{RFP_SEND:DOCUMENT_GENERATION}}, {{RFP_SEND:EMAIL_SEND}}, and {{RFP_SEND:FINALIZATION}}.

* Send RFP API is updated behind a feature flag to support orchestrated sending.

* Legacy small-send path remains available behind the feature flag.
* {{RfpSendWorkflow}} is implemented to load run state, send log, source draft run, and config snapshot.
* Workflow creates {{RECIPIENT_PREPARATION}} batches, dispatches initial batches, handles {{batchCompleted}} signals, deduplicates signals, creates retry batches before next-stage batches, fills next-stage concurrency windows, creates stage batches for eligible recipients, creates the {{FINALIZATION}} batch when email stage quiesces, applies Continue-As-New thresholds, and finalizes the run.
* Recipient preparation worker is implemented to claim batches, load send run, load {{sourceDraftWorkflowRunId}}, query {{RfpVendorDraft}} by {{draftGenerationRunId}}, query unregistered vendors, build and deduplicate recipient rows, insert recipients idempotently, update recipient preparation status fields, record failures, update batch summary, insert outbox event, and delete SQS message after commit.
* Vendor response creation worker is implemented to claim eligible recipients, use {{RfpVendorResponseWriterService}}, use {{ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING}}, update vendor response creation status fields, record retryable and permanent failures, update batch summary, insert outbox event, and delete SQS message after commit.
* Document generation worker is implemented to claim eligible recipients, attach shared RFP template PDF for v1, update {{attachmentPdfUrl}}, update document generation status fields, record retryable and permanent failures, update batch summary, insert outbox event, and delete SQS message after commit.
* Email send worker is implemented to claim eligible recipients, generate deterministic {{emailSendAttemptId}}, check existing provider message and outcome fields, send registered and unregistered vendor emails through the SES pattern, store SES provider message id, update email execution fields, update existing {{sendStatus}}, handle SES success with DB uncertainty, move unknown duplicate-risk outcomes to manual review, record retryable and permanent failures, update batch summary, insert outbox event, and delete SQS message after commit.
* Finalization worker is implemented to claim finalization batch, re-query run state and email success count, verify no active email batches remain, apply signed-off {{OPEN_FOR_BIDS}} rule, update RFP status idempotently, update property statuses idempotently, dispatch notifications idempotently, update batch summary, insert outbox event, and delete SQS message after commit.
* Retry and manual review behavior is implemented for recipient preparation, VPR creation, document generation, and email send failures.
* Email send retries are allowed only when duplicate risk is acceptable.
* Exhausted retry failures and permanent failures are marked correctly.
* {{manualReviewRequired}} is set where needed.
* Failed recipient list API, manual retry by recipient ids, manual retry by batch id, audit fields, alert for manual retry failure, and tests are implemented.
* Draft cleanup for Send RFP is safe by removing unconditional draft delete from orchestrated send path, keeping legacy cleanup behind feature flag, adding cleanup after terminal send run, cleaning only the selected {{draftGenerationRunId}}, skipping cleanup when active manual retry batches exist, skipping cleanup when active send run references the same draft run, and supporting soft archive with {{isRemoved}}.
* Unit tests validate send stage progression, retry-first batch creation, completion rules, and email idempotency.
* Integration tests validate send API response, exact draft snapshot usage, recipient preparation, VPR creation, document generation, email stage, finalization, partial success behavior, and retry batch behavior.
* Chaos tests validate duplicate SQS handling, worker crash before final commit, worker crash after final commit, outbox signal failure, SES success with DB failure, and manual retry new execution.
* Load testing is completed for large RFP sends.
* Recipient batch size, VPR batch size, email concurrency, and DB pool limits are tuned.
* Phase 3 validation confirms orchestrated Send RFP works locally and in staging.
* Large send returns {{202}} quickly.
* Recipients are created from the exact draft snapshot.
* VPRs, documents, and emails are idempotent.
* Emails do not duplicate under retry.

column1: Previously Verified Vendors Are Incorrectly Shown a Verification Failure Screen on Reopening the Verification Link
column31:
*Summary* 

After a vendor successfully completes the business verification process, reopening the same business verification email link incorrectly redirects the vendor to a *"Verification Failed"* screen and displays the *retry verification form*. This behavior is misleading, as the vendor has already completed the verification process successfully.

The system should recognize that the verification associated with the invitation has already been completed and prevent the vendor from accessing the retry workflow.

*Steps to Replicate:*

# Send a business verification invitation email to a vendor.
# Open the email and complete the business verification process successfully.
# Ensure the vendor's verification status is updated successfully in the system.
# Reopen the same business verification email.
# Click on the original verification link again.

*Actual Result:*
The vendor is redirected to a *"Verification Failed"* page, and the *retry verification form* is displayed, allowing the vendor to proceed as though the previous verification had failed.

*Expected Result:*
Once business verification has been completed successfully, accessing the same verification link again should not display a verification failure message or the retry form. Instead, the system should display an appropriate status page indicating that the verification has already been completed successfully (for example, *"Business verification has already been completed for this invitation."*) and restrict access to the retry workflow.

* *Client users*: See their own vendor list immediately without any extra selection
* *Admin/Internal users*: Presented with a client search dropdown to select which client's vendors to view
* Auto-selects the first available client for admin users on page load

* Clicking a vendor name in the list opens a dedicated vendor detail page
* Shows vendor header information and company info tab
* Displays vendor contacts section for client users

* Includes a "Back" button to return to the list

* "Connexus Verify > Vendors" is hidden from vendor-type users
* Vendor list query only fires when a valid client is selected (prevents empty/errored state)
* Vendor detail components safely handle scenarios where vendor-specific workspace data is unavailable

h3. 5. Removed Legacy Behavior

* Removed "Update Client Vendors" action from the client list action menu
* Client vendors are now accessed directly from the sidebar instead of via the client list

column1: BE - Add bid readiness status to vendor property responses list
column31:
h2. Summary

Add a computed {{bidStatus}} field to each row returned by the vendor property responses listing API ({{GET /vendor-property-responses}}). This status helps vendors quickly identify the completion state of each property bid without needing to inspect individual fields.

h2. Background

Currently, the vendor property responses list returns property-level bid data (cost, documents, etc.) but does not provide a clear at-a-glance indicator of whether a bid row is ready for submission. Vendors need to manually check each property to determine readiness.

h2. Requirements

Each property response row should include a {{bidStatus}} field with one of the following values:

||Status||Condition||
|*Submitted*|The bid for this property has already been submitted|
|*Ready*|The vendor has entered a {{totalCost}} value — the bid is ready to be submitted|
|*Incomplete*|No {{totalCost}} has been entered and no documents have been uploaded — the bid is not ready|

h2. Acceptance Criteria

# The {{GET /vendor-property-responses}} endpoint returns a {{bidStatus}} field in every row
# If the property response status is {{SUBMITTED}}, {{bidStatus}} = "Submitted"
# If {{totalCost}} is populated (not null), {{bidStatus}} = "Ready"
# If {{totalCost}} is null and no documents are attached, {{bidStatus}} = "Incomplete"
# This field is computed at response time — no new database column is required
# Existing filters, sorting, and pagination behavior remain unchanged

column1: BE - Add batch processing to vendor property response bulk operations
column31:
h2. Summary

The bulk update and copy operations in the Vendor Property Responses service currently process all records in a single unbatched pass. When the number of vendor property responses exceeds 1,000+ rows, this leads to:

* *Database parameter limit exhaustion* -- Postgres supports ~65,535 parameters per statement; a single {{INSERT}} or {{UPDATE}} with 1,000+ rows can exceed this.
* *Prolonged lock durations* -- A single massive query holds row/table locks for the entire duration, blocking other concurrent operations.
* *Transaction timeouts* -- Large single-pass operations are likely to exceed Prisma's default transaction timeout.
* *High memory pressure* -- Materializing thousands of parallel promises in Node.js spikes memory usage.

h2. Scope

Introduce batched processing (batch size: 500) to the following operations in {{VendorPropertyResponsesService}}:

h3. 1. Bulk Update -- Individual Row Updates

* *Current behavior*: All update items are fired as parallel DB queries (1 read + 1 write per row) inside a single transaction with no concurrency limit.
* *Expected behavior*: Updates are split into sequential batches of 500. Items within each batch run in parallel, but the next batch only starts after the current one completes.

h3. 2. Bulk Update -- Submit Status Change

* *Current behavior*: A single {{updateMany}} is called with all submitted IDs in one {{WHERE IN (...)}} clause.
* *Expected behavior*: The submitted IDs are chunked into groups of 500 and each chunk is updated sequentially.

h3. 3. Bulk Update -- Status History Creation

* *Current behavior*: A single {{createMany}} inserts all status history records at once.
* *Expected behavior*: Status history records are created in batches of 500 to stay within DB parameter limits.

h3. 4. Copy to Other Properties

* *Current behavior*: All target property responses are processed in a single unbounded {{Promise.all}}, each performing updates and document copies in parallel.
* *Expected behavior*: Targets are split into sequential batches of 500. Each batch processes its targets in parallel, then the next batch begins.

h3. 5. Mark Batch as Ready to Submit

* *Current behavior*: A single {{updateMany}} with all IDs.
* *Expected behavior*: IDs are chunked into groups of 500 and updated sequentially.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* All five operations listed above process records in batches of 500.
* Batches execute *sequentially* (not in parallel) to bound database lock duration and connection usage.
* Progress is logged per batch (e.g., "processed batch 2/5") for observability.
* Functional behavior remains unchanged -- the same validations, error collection, status transitions, notifications, and response payloads are preserved.
* No regressions in existing unit/e2e tests.

h2. Affected Service

{{apps/sow-rfq/src/services/vendor-property-responses/vendor-property-responses.service.ts}}

h2. Reference

This pattern is already established in the codebase:

* {{insert-rfp-vendor-drafts-in-batches.util.ts}} (batch size 500)
* {{RfpVendorResponseWriterService}} (dynamic batch size with {{chunkArray}})
* {{InsuranceExpiryService}} (cursor-based batching, batch size 100)

This reduces data entry, improves consistency, and aligns Division with where it logically belongs (the property itself).

_ _Property CSV Upload:* Add Division column mapping in CSV template and upload parser
_ _Property Export:* Add Division as a new column in exported data

h3. 3. Property Insurance Module - Remove Division Writes

* Remove division field from Update Policy and Create Endorsement DTOs
* Remove division write logic from submitPropertyMatch and buildNewCompliancePropertyData
* Division is no longer written to CompliancesProperty from any insurance operation

* List and detail raw SQL queries now source division and externalPropertyId from the matched property (ClientProperties) join instead of CompliancesProperty
* Division filter/sort updated to reference matched property table

column1: Track and store each user's last login date and time
column31:
h2. Background

We need a reliable way to know when each user last signed in to Connexus. This helps with user activity visibility, account oversight, and audit needs.

Until now, the system did not store when a user last logged in.

h2. What was done

The system now records the date and time of a user's _most recent genuine sign-in_.

_ Each user has a _Last Login* value stored on their account.

* It updates when the user signs in again (password or single sign-on).
_ It does _not* update on every page refresh or routine app use — only on a real new sign-in.
* Existing users who have not signed in since this change went live will show no last login until their next sign-in.
* No changes were required on the frontend; sign-in continues to work as it does today.

h2. Why this matters

* Admins and internal teams can see when a user was last active via sign-in.
* Supports audit and accountability (who signed in and when).
* Gives a foundation for future reporting or inactive-user workflows if needed later.

h2. What is not included in this release

* Full login history (only the most recent login is stored).
* Changes to the sign-in screen or user experience.
* Automatic alerts or account actions based on inactivity.

h2. Acceptance criteria

_ When a user signs in successfully, their _Last Login* is saved on their account.
_ _Last Login* reflects the time of the actual sign-in, not routine app usage afterward.
_ Signing in again updates _Last Login* to the new sign-in time.

* Users who have never signed in since this feature launched show no last login until they sign in.
_ Sign-in via password and single sign-on (e.g. Microsoft) both update _Last Login*.
_ A failed or blocked sign-in does not update _Last Login*.
_ Normal use of the app after sign-in does not incorrectly change _Last Login*.

column1: Change current service property mapping to individual service and property mapping
column31:
h2. User Story

*As a* client / Connexus user, *when* I open the invite (Resend Vendor) form, *I want to* map each property to its own set of services via the _Service Property Mapping_ section, and optionally copy one property's service mapping to all or to specific properties, *so that* every property carries its own distinct services, with a quick way to reuse a mapping across properties instead of re-entering it each time.

h2. Context

* The mapping is *property-centric*: properties are the rows, and each property holds one or more services.
* The current setup uses a single shared service–property mapping; the goal is per-property service mapping.
* Because many properties often share the same services, the user needs a way to *apply one property's mapping to all* properties or to *specific* ones.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

h3. 1. Opening the section

* On the Resend Vendor form, clicking *"Add Services and Locations"* reveals the *Service Property Mapping* section.
* The section header shows an *info tooltip* explaining the vendor approval scope (_"Where should this vendor be approved to work?"_).

h3. 2. Adding properties and mapping services

* The section has a required *Properties* field with a *Search Properties* input and an *"+ Add Property"* button.
* Property selection from dropbox will be multi select 
* Selecting/adding a property creates a *row* in the mapping table, with the property name in the *Properties* column.
* Each property row can hold *multiple services*, shown as *removable chips* (e.g. _Landscaping ✕, Snow removal ✕, Pesticides / pest control ✕_) across the service columns.
* A property with no services yet shows an *"+ Add"* action in its service cell to attach services to that property.
* Each selection of service is a single select.
* Along with property, its city and state also should be added.

h3. 3. Row actions — Apply and Remove

Each property row has a *3-dot (⋮) menu* with:

* *Apply to All Property* — copies this property's service mapping to *every* property row in the table.
* *Apply to Specific Property* — opens a picker to choose *one or more target properties*, and copies this property's service mapping only to those selected.
* *Remove property* — removes the property (and its mapped services) from the table.

h3. 4. Managing the mapping table

* *Filters* are available on the columns (property name, service name) via the *Filters* control.
* *Search* by *property name* & Service name is available (search box in the table header).
* *Sorting* is available on the columns (sort arrows on Properties headers).
* The table is *paginated* when there are many properties (e.g. _Page 1 of 10_). it should be custamizable and user can choose the number of records in one page 10,2030,50,100.

h3. 5. Saving

* Clicking *confirm* persists all property→service mappings.
* Clicking *clear All* discards changes and closes the section without saving.

h3. 6. After submitting the invite

* On the *View Details* (Connexus Vendor Detail) page, all mapped properties and their services are displayed.
* The grid can be *filtered by Service Name* (dropdown) and *searched by Property name*.
* The grid shows each property's *State, Compliance Standing, Business Licenses,* and *Insurance Compliant* status.
* A service that was later removed appears in the Service Name dropdown flagged as *"Removed"* (greyed/disabled), consistent with the resend/edit behavior.

*Validations to be handled :* 

# Already added property should be disabled from the property search. 
# Already added service for the specific property should be disabled for the next service selection field
# Service will be single selection for each property 
# Apply to All property will be applicable to the properties added from property selection field 
# Apply to specific property should remove the mapped property

column1: Add/Modify existing Service- property mapping after KYB verification =yes
column31:
*_User story_*

*As a* Connexus admin, *I want* to add a modify to a vendor's existing service-property record, and assign a new contact, *so that* I can modify or add service locations and update the Request 

*Acceptance Criteria:*

h2.  Case :  Adding New  service/property in the existing request.

* *Given* a vendor with Business Verified = Yes, *when* the user clicks "Add/Modify service-property mapping", *then:*
** *Property appended to an existing service (same or different contact):* The Vendor Detail page shows a new row for that property, along with its mapped services.
** *New service mapped to an existing property:* The Vendor Detail page appends the new service to the service dropdown, along with its mapped property/properties.
** *Service removed from one property's mapping (while still active for other properties):* The property record is deactivated for that service on the Vendor Detail page. The user can reactivate it via the "Reactivate" button, which restores the property under that service.
** *Service removed from all property mappings:* The service itself is deactivated in the service dropdown. The user can reactivate it via the "Reactivate" button, which restores all previously mapped properties.
** *Connexus Verify Vendors list page:* A separate record is created showing the newly appended property and service, along with "Requested By" and "Requested Date."
** *Notifications:* An email notification is sent to the existing contact or the different contact specified in the request form. All future notifications for this vendor route to this new contact.



h2. All Requests Page  Acceptance Criteria

# *Navigation*

* *Given* a vendor with Business Verified = Yes, *when* the user clicks the overflow menu (⋮) next to "Add/modify service-property" on the Vendor Detail page, *then* an option "View All Requests" is shown alongside "History" and "Download."
* *When* the user clicks "View All Requests," *then* the user is navigated to a new standalone page (not a modal), titled "All Requests," scoped to the current vendor.

# *Page Layout & Columns*

* *Given* the user is on the All Requests page, *then* the table displays the following columns in order: *Type, Item, Action, Primary Email, Requested By, Requested Date.*
* *Type* displays either "Property" or "Service," styled consistently with the tag/pill treatment used elsewhere with color code added in the figma
* *Item* displays the specific property or service name (e.g., "Property 1," "Service 2").
* *Action* displays either "Added" (green) or "Removed" (red), matching the color conventions used for status pills elsewhere in Connexus.
* *Primary Email* displays the email address of the contact associated with that specific request.
* *Requested By* displays the name of the user who submitted the request.
* *Requested Date* displays the date the request was submitted, in the same date format used elsewhere (e.g., "Aug 13 2026").

# *Sorting*

* *Given* the user is on the All Requests page, *when* the user clicks any column header, *then* the table sorts ascending/descending by that column (indicated by the ↓/↑ icon), matching sort behavior on the Vendor Detail page.

# *Data Population*

* *Given* a user submits an Add/Modify service-property request (addition or removal, for property or service), *then* a new row is created on the All Requests page reflecting that action — resolving prior ambiguity: *both additions and removals must generate a row*, not just additions.
* *Each row is atomic* — i.e., if a single request adds 2 properties and removes 1 service, this results in 3 separate rows (one per Type/Item/Action combination), not one combined row.

# *Filters*

* *Given* the user is on the All Requests page, *when* the user clicks "Filters," *then* the user can filter by Type (Property/Service), Action (Added/Removed), Requested By, and Requested Date (range),primary email,item

# *Pagination*

* *Given* the All Requests page has more rows than fit on one page, *then* pagination controls are shown at the bottom 

# *Empty State*

* *Given* a vendor has no requests submitted yet, *when* the user navigates to the All Requests page, *then* an empty state message is shown (e.g., "No requests yet") instead of an empty table.

# *Back Navigation*

* *Given* the user is on the All Requests page, *when* the user clicks "Back," *then* the user returns to the Vendor Detail page they came from, preserving prior filters/search state (e.g., Service Name = Landscaping).

# *Read-only Page*

* *Given* the user is on the All Requests page, *then* all rows are read-only (view-only log) — no inline edit, approve, or reactivate actions are available on this page.

h2. Scenarios

||#||Scenario||Precondition||Action||Expected Result||Notes/Edge Case||
|1|Append property to existing service — same contact|Vendor Business Verified = Yes; service already mapped to  property|Add new property under same service, same contact|New row appears on Vendor Detail page with mapped service,Same vendor contact will recieve the email notification|Baseline case|
|2|Append property to existing service — different contact|Vendor Business Verified = Yes; service already mapped to ≥1 property|Add new property under same service, different contact|New row appears on Vendor Detail page; contact updated per rule below
New vendor contact will receive the notification and this new vendor will be cerating as primary contact|Verify which contact becomes "future notification" owner|
|3|Map new service to existing property|Property already exists on Vendor Detail page|Add a new service to that property|New service appended to service dropdown; property shown under it|Service dropdown doesn't duplicate if service already exists elsewhere|
|4|Remove service from one property (service still active elsewhere)|Service mapped to >2 properties|Remove service from Property A only|Property A's record deactivates for that service; Property B unaffected|Verify Service  isn't fully hidden if it has other active properties(Gap #7)|
|5|Reactivate a single deactivated property-service mapping|Scenario 4 completed|Click "Reactivate" on Property A|Property A restored under that service|Confirm restored state matches prior mapping exactly|
|6|Remove service from all properties|Service mapped to N properties|Remove service from every property|Service deactivated in dropdown entirely|Confirm service disappears from dropdown vs. shows "inactive" tag|
|7|Reactivate a fully deactivated service|Scenario 6 completed|Click "Reactivate" on the service|All previously mapped properties restored| |
|8|View Record option|Any add/modify request submitted|Submit request|Separate record created with Type,item, primary email, Requested By, Requested Date|This will be a page and show all the records.|
|9|Email notification — existing contact|Request submitted, same contact|Submit|Email sent to existing contact|Confirm trigger point: on submit vs. on approval (Gap #6)|
|10|Email notification — new/different contact|Request submitted, new contact specified|Submit|Email sent to new contact;| |
|11|Future notification routing|New contact set per Scenario 2/12|Trigger any future notification event|Routes to new contact only|Confirm no notifications leak to old contact|
|12|Concurrent requests from different contacts|Two in-flight requests for same vendor, different contacts|Both submitted near-simultaneously|Last updated data will be populated| |

column1: Refreshing the Business Verification Retry Page Incorrectly Decrements Retry Count
column31:
*Summary* 

On the *Business Verification Retry* page, refreshing or reloading the page triggers the business verification API again. Each page reload is incorrectly treated as a new retry attempt, causing the available retry count to decrease. After 3 refreshes, the retry count reaches *0*, preventing the vendor from completing and submitting the retry form even though no actual retry submission was made.

*Steps to Replicate:*

# Trigger a business verification failure for a vendor.
# Open the *Business Verification Retry* page.
# Refresh the browser (F5/Ctrl+R) multiple times.
# Observe the API calls and the remaining retry count.
# Continue refreshing until the retry count reaches *0*.

*Actual Result:*

* The business verification API is invoked on every page reload.
* Each reload decrements the remaining retry count.
* The retry attempts are exhausted without the vendor submitting the retry form.
* The vendor is eventually prevented from completing the retry process.

*Expected Result:*

* Refreshing or reopening the retry page should *not* consume a retry attempt.
* The retry count should only be decremented when the vendor *submits* the updated business verification details for processing.
* Page reloads should simply reload the existing form without affecting the retry count.

column1: Enhancement: Allow RFP Resend to Updated Vendor Email and Maintain Email Audit History
column31:
h3. Background

Currently, once an RFP has been sent to a vendor, the *Manage Vendor Invite* page continues to display the original email address even if the vendor's email is updated later. As a result, users can only resend the RFP to the old email address.

h3. Current Behavior

* RFP is initially sent to *Email A*.
* Vendor email is updated to *Email B*.
* The *Manage Vendor Invite* page still displays *Email A*.
* Resend functionality sends the RFP to *Email A*.
* No audit record is created for the updated email.

*Expected Behavior* (Enhancement)

# If the vendor's email address has been updated after the RFP was initially sent, the system should detect the updated email when the user clicks *Resend*.
