column1: Compliance Records Notification
column31:
h2. Notification Summary Table

||Notification Name||Trigger Event||Included Records||Excluded Records||Recipient||
|Expiring #1|Date of Expiration ≤ Today + 30 Days|All records except N/A, N/A anymore, or Archived|N/A, N/A anymore, Archived|Property Manager and users linked to the property — *excluding* Corporate Contacts|
|Expiring #2|Date of Expiration ≤ Today + 60 Days|All records except N/A, N/A anymore, or Archived|N/A, N/A anymore, Archived|Property Manager and users linked to the property — *excluding* Corporate Contacts|
|Expiring #3|Date of Expiration ≤ Today + 90 Days|All records except N/A, N/A anymore, or Archived|N/A, N/A anymore, Archived|Property Manager and users linked to the property — *excluding* Corporate Contacts|
|Expiring #4|Date of Expiration < Today (Expired)|All records except N/A, N/A anymore, or Archived|N/A, N/A anymore, Archived|Property Manager and users linked to the property — *excluding* Corporate Contacts|

h2. User Story

*As a* Property Manager or user linked to a property *I want to* be automatically notified as a compliance record approaches its expiration date, and again once it has expired *So that* I have advance warning to renew the record before it lapses and remain aware once it has

h2. Acceptance Criteria

h3. 1. 30-day advance notice

* *Trigger:* The notification fires when a compliance record's Expiration Date is *less than or equal to Today + 30 days*.
* *Included:* All compliance records whose current status is *not* N/A, *not* N/A anymore, and *not* Archived.
* *Excluded:* Any record currently in *N/A*, *N/A anymore*, or *Archived* status must never trigger this notification.
* *Recipient:* The Property Manager and any user linked to the property associated with the record.
* *Recipient exclusion:* Corporate Contacts must *not* receive this notification, regardless of their association with the property.
* *Data/Variables needed:* Expiration Date value, evaluated against "Today + 30 Days" at the time the check runs.

h3. 2.  60-day advance notice

* *Trigger:* The notification fires when a compliance record's Expiration Date is *less than or equal to Today + 60 days*.
* *Included / Excluded / Recipient / Recipient exclusion:* Identical rules to Expiring #1 (see above).
* *Data/Variables needed:* Expiration Date value, evaluated against "Today + 60 Days" at the time the check runs.

h3. 3.  90-day advance notice

* *Trigger:* The notification fires when a compliance record's Expiration Date is *less than or equal to Today + 90 days*.
* *Included / Excluded / Recipient / Recipient exclusion:* Identical rules to Expiring #1 (see above).
* *Data/Variables needed:* Expiration Date value, evaluated against "Today + 90 Days" at the time the check runs.

h3. 4.  Expired notice

* *Trigger:* The notification fires when a compliance record's Expiration Date is *strictly less than Today* (i.e., the record has already expired).
* *Included / Excluded / Recipient / Recipient exclusion:* Identical rules to Expiring #1 (see above).
* *Data/Variables needed:* Expiration Date value, evaluated against "Today" at the time the check runs.

h3. 5. Cross-cutting rules applicable to all four notifications

* A record with a blank Expiration Date can never trigger any of these four notifications, since such records are always in *N/A* status (consistent with the parent epic's rule that N/A/N/A anymore records carry no Expiration Date).
* Once a record's status changes to *N/A*, *N/A anymore*, or it is moved to *Archived* (via Renew/Replace), it must be immediately excluded from all four notification checks going forward, even if it previously qualified.
* Each of the four notifications is evaluated independently — a single record could theoretically be eligible for more than one threshold check within the same run window In that case last notification should be trigerred instead of all(e.g., a record newly created with an Expiration Date 25 days out would only match Expiring #1, not #2 or #3, in this case it should triger the notification for 30. 
* Notifications are scoped *per record*, not per file or per property  each qualifying compliance record generates its own notification event.

h2. Dependencies

* This ticket depends on the compliance record *Status Lifecycle* ticket for the precise definitions of N/A, N/A anymore, and Archived states used in the exclusion logic above.
* Recipient resolution depends on existing *Role Management* / property-user linkage data to correctly identify "Property Manager and those linked to the property" versus "Corporate Contacts."

column31:
h1. User Story : 

As a Connexus user I want to upload one or more compliance files from the File Upload tab So that compliance documents can be captured and processed into the system

h2. 1. View the File Upload grid with all columns

*As a* Connexus or Client user *I want to* view all uploaded files in a single structured grid *So that* I can quickly see what has been uploaded, by whom, and its current processing status

*Acceptance Criteria:*

* The File Upload grid displays the following columns, in order: *Property Name, File Name, Uploaded By, Uploaded Date, Status*.
* *Property Name* :  the property the uploaded batch belongs to.
* *File Name*  :  one or more file links per row (e.g., File.1, File.2, File.3). Each file name is a download link.
** When a row contains more files than can be displayed inline, an overflow indicator (e.g., *"+4"*) appears next to the visible file names.
** Hovering over the overflow indicator expands a preview showing the names of the remaining files in that row (e.g., File.11, File.9, File.14, File.15), will be displayed
* *Uploaded By* :  identifies the source of the upload (e.g., "Vendor", "RFP").
* *Uploaded Date* :   the date the file batch was uploaded.
* *Status:*  shows either *Processing*, *Pending Review* or *Pending Completion* or *Approved* as a colored badge with an info icon. Hovering the info icon displays the corresponding tooltip:
** Pending Review → _"Read by AI and needs approval"_
** Pending Completion → _"Not read by AI & require Approval"_
** Processing - If files are processing after passing through AI 
** Approved : if all files are approved.

h2. 2. Sort the File Upload grid

* *Property Name*, *Uploaded By*, *Uploaded Date*, and *Status* columns each display a sort arrow in the column header (Screens 1 and 2).
* Clicking a column header's sort arrow toggles that column between ascending and descending order.
* The active sort column and direction are visually indicated by the arrow's orientation.
* Sorting re-orders the full grid, not just the current page.

h2. 3. Filter the File Upload grid

* Clicking *Filters* opens a filter panel/dropdown.
* The user can filter by,: Property Name, Status (Pending Review / Pending Completion), Uploaded By, and Uploaded Date (range) , Uploaded date (range ),Uploaded by(all users in the list ), 
* Applied filters are reflected in the grid results and can be cleared/reset.

h2. 4. Search the File Upload grid

* A *Search* box is available at the top-right of the grid (Screens 1 and 2).
* Entering a search term filters the grid to rows matching the Property Name and File Name.
* Clearing the search restores the full, unfiltered grid (respecting any active filters/sort).

h2. 5. Row-level actions on the File Upload grid

* Clicking the row's kebab (⋮) menu opens a contextual menu containing: 
*Review For Approval*, *Download*, *Delete* 
* *Review For Approval* navigates the user into the Compliance Record Review table containing the AI-extracted records generated from that file's upload.
* *Download* downloads the file(s) associated with that row.
* *Delete* removes the uploaded file entry from the grid.
* Files which are in Status *Pending Review* or *Pending Completion* can be removed. All the other status delete will be hidden

h2. 6. Upload files via the File Upload modal

* Clicking *Upload* opens the File Upload modal with *Select Client* and *Select Property* fields.
* If the upload is initiated by a Client user, the *Select Client* field is not visible.
* The user can drag-and-drop files into the upload area or browse to select them.
* The modal supports uploading up to *20 files* per batch, with a combined size limit of *1GB* (based on the browser's available memory), as noted in the modal's helper text.
* Each selected file displays its own upload progress bar with a percentage indicator (Screen 1).
* The user can *Cancel* to discard the batch or click *Upload* to submit all selected files for processing.
* Immediately after a file finishes uploading, it is queued for OCR extraction followed by AI data extraction — no manual trigger required.
* The user is not required to take any action to initiate processing.
* Any file exceeding 80MB is not sent through AI processing.
* Such files are routed directly to the "Pending Completion" status
* If AI processing fails, or the file is flagged as unreadable, suspicious, or low-confidence, it is not passed to AI extraction,automatically it will go through pending completion
* Such files are routed to the "Pending Completion" status 
* Files that fail the size check or the AI processing/flagging check are marked with status *Pending Completion*.
* Hovering over the status shows a tooltip: _"Not read by AI & require Approval"_.Files that pass the eligibility check and are successfully processed by AI are marked with status *Pending Review*.
* Hovering over the status shows a tooltip: _"Read by AI and needs approval"_.

h3. 7. Re-uploading a file for the same client/property

* The Upload action remains available for the same client/property combination at any time.
* Re-upload follows the same upload modal flow 

h3. 8. Duplicate file warning

*As a* user uploading a file *I want to* be warned if I am uploading a duplicate file for the same property *So that* I don't accidentally create redundant records, while still retaining the option to proceed

*Acceptance Criteria:*

* When a file is uploaded that matches an existing file for the same property, the system displays a warning that a duplicate file exists.
* The user can dismiss the warning and continue with the upload (bypass allowed).
* The duplicate upload is processed through the same OCR/AI pipeline as any other file.le per row in the File Upload grid with a tooltip/info icon

h1. Compliance Record Review

h2. User Story

*As a* Connexus or Client user *I want to* review, edit, and approve every field of an AI-extracted compliance record in detail *So that* only accurate, complete data is published to the Compliance & Records dashboard

h2. Acceptance Criteria

h3. A. Compliance Record Review grid 

# The grid header displays the *Property Name* the records belong to (e.g., "Property name : Colliers").
# The grid includes a *Filters* control and a *Download* action at the top of the table.
# The grid displays the following columns, in order, each sortable via a header arrow:
#* *Compliance Category*
#* *Record Type*
#* *Issuing Authority*
#* *Issue Date*
#* *Expiration Date*
#* *License / Record #*
#* *Frequency*
#* *Total Cost*
#* *File name*
#* *Additional Files*
# Any field the AI could not confidently determine displays as *"Unmatched"* (e.g., Issuing Authority, Frequency in the reference screenshot).
# *File name* is a clickable link to the primary uploaded source file for that record.
# *Additional Files*, if present, are shown as clickable links alongside the primary file.
# Each row has an *Approve* button and a kebab (⋮) menu with *Edit*, *Download*, and *Inactive* actions.
# The grid is paginated (e.g., "Page 1 of 10") with page number controls and a next-page arrow.

h3. B. Record Review form — Record Identification 

# *Property* — read-only/disabled field; pre-populated from the property selected during upload and cannot be changed on this form.
# *Compliance Category* — a searchable dropdown field. Values are mapped against the *predefined Compliance Category dataset* provided in the shared reference document; the AI-extracted value must resolve to one of these predefined categories (e.g., "Permits & Certificates", "Fire & Life Safety Inspections / Testing"). If no confident match is found, the field is flagged as "Unmatched" and the user must manually select the correct category from the predefined list.
# *Record Type* — a text/dropdown field whose valid values are dependent on, and mapped against, the *predefined Record Type dataset* tied to the selected Compliance Category (e.g., "Occupancy Permit", "Certificate of Occupancy", "Final Certificate of Occupancy", "Signage Permit"), as per the shared reference document. If the AI-extracted value does not match a predefined Record Type for the selected Compliance Category, it is flagged as "Unmatched" and must be corrected manually.
# *License / Record #* — free-text field capturing the license/record identifier (e.g., "GL-58493595.154").ALphanumeric field. maximum characters allowed 60
# *Issue Date* — date field with a calendar picker; format displayed as "Mon DD YYYY" (e.g., "Sep 21 2025").
# *Expiration Date* — date field with a calendar picker, same format as Issue Date. This field directly drives the file extraction
# *Frequency* — dropdown field  : 
     a.Monthly
     b.Bi-Monthly
     c.Quarterly 
     d.Semi-Annually
     e.Annual
     f.Other (Other should allow them to type in what the frequency is but it is not required to be an option in the dropdown going forward)

# *Total Cost* — numeric currency field, formatted with a "$" prefix (e.g., "$ 68,000").minimum char 1 to max : 12 digits + 3 decimal points
# *Add Additional Documents* — a "Choose file(s)" control allowing the user to attach one or more supplementary documents to the record. Attached files display as removable chips/tags below the control (e.g., "File x", "File 1 x", "File 2 x", "File 3 x", "File 4 x").All file type should be supported except media files

h3. C. Record Review form — Issuing Authority & Primary Contact (Screens 2 and 4)

# *Authority Name* — a searchable dropdown/typeahead field.
#* If the typed/extracted value does not match an existing Authority record, the field displays *"No result"* along with the typed value and a *"Create as new"* link, allowing the user to create a new Issuing Authority entry inline.This will be a global field and any client created issuing authority name will be populated in the list
# *Property Account #* — free-text field for the account/reference number tied to the issuing authority. min 1 to max 50
# *Website URL* — free-text field for the authority's website. vlaidation should be triggered for invalid website
# *Username* — free-text field for login credentials associated with the authority account.
# *Password* — masked free-text field (displayed as dots/asterisks) for the associated login credentials. min 8 and max 64
# *Primary Contact at Issuing Authority* section includes:
#* *First Name* — free-text field.
#* *Last Name* — free-text field.
#* *Email* — free-text field, validated as an email address format.
#* *Phone* — phone number field with a *country code selector*. 

h3. D. History / Notes 

# A collapsible *History* panel contains a *Notes* table with columns: *Username*, *Date*, *Notes*  each sortable via header arrow.
# If no notes exist, the panel displays an empty state: an icon, *"No notes yet"*, and the caption *"Optional notes and comments."* .
# A *+ Add Note* action opens the *Add Notes* modal , which contains:
#* A *Brief Description* text area, limited to *500 characters*, with a live character counter (e.g., "0/500 characters").
#* *Cancel* and *Submit* actions.
# On Submit, the new note is appended to the Notes table with the current Username and Date populated automatically 
# Notes are read-only once submitted; there is no edit/delete action on individual notes within this scope.

h3. E. Saving edits

# The Record Review form provides *Cancel* and *Save* actions at the bottom of the form.
# *Cancel* discards any unsaved changes and returns to the Compliance Record Review grid.
# *Save* persists all edited field values and updates the corresponding row in the Compliance Record Review grid immediately.
# As per the parent epic, all fields are editable on Save *except* the *Property* dropdown and the primary *File Upload* field.

h3. F. Approving a record 

# Clicking *Approve* on a record row  opens an *Approve Request* confirmation modal titled *"Approve Request"* with the message: _"Are sure you want to approve this file?"_
# The modal provides *Cancel* and *Confirm* actions.
# Clicking *Confirm* approves the record, removing it from the Compliance Record Review grid and moving it to the Compliance & Records tab under its property, per the parent epic.
# Clicking *Cancel* closes the modal with no change to the record's state.

h3. G. Pending Completion Review

# Clicking on a *Pending Completion* record from the File Upload grid opens the record in a grid/form view where all fields are initially blank, each displayed with a dash (*"–"*) as a placeholder, since no data could be extracted by AI.
# The user can manually edit each field to enter the correct compliance data, then approve the record once complete.
# Because this is a fully manual entry (not AI-assisted), every field is presented as an empty input styled with a *dotted border/underline*, visually distinguishing it from AI-extracted fields.
# Once approved, the record moves into the *Compliance & Records* tab under its property, following the same approval flow as AI-extracted records.
# All action buttons (Edit, Download, Inactive, Approve, etc.) remain consistent with those available on a *Pending Review* record.

h2. Dependencies

* *Compliance Category* and *Record Type* dropdown values must be sourced from and validated against the *predefined master dataset document* shared for this module. Any category/type extracted by AI that does not exist in this dataset must be flagged as "Unmatched" rather than auto-created.

h2. Out of Scope

column31:
h2.  Compliance & Records Tab (Grid)

*As a* Connexus or Client user *I want to* view all approved compliance records organized by property *So that* I can monitor the compliance status of my portfolio at a glance

*Acceptance Criteria:*

# The tab provides a *Client Name* dropdown and a *Search Property* box at the top to locate a specific client/property (Screen 1).
# Records are grouped under a collapsible *property header* (e.g., "Property 1 | 123 Main Street, Hartford, CT") showing a *Download* action and an expand/collapse chevron for that property's record table.
# Properties not currently expanded are listed below as collapsed rows (e.g., "456 Elm Avenue, New Haven, CT") and can be expanded independently.
# Each expanded property table includes a *Filters* control and displays the following sortable columns: *Compliance Category, Record Type, Issuing Authority, Issue Date, Expiration Date, License / Record #, Frequency, Total Cost, Status*.
# *Status* is shown as a colored badge with one of the following values: *Active* (green), *Expiring* (yellow/orange), *Expired* (red), *N/A* (gray), *N/A anymore* (gray), per the status rules defined in the parent epic.
# Each row has a kebab (⋮) menu offering: *View Details*, *Edit*, *Renew*.
# Both the expanded property's record table and the overall list of properties are paginated (e.g., "Page 1 of 10").

h2. B. View Details (View Compliance Record)

*Acceptance Criteria:*

# Selecting *View Details* from the row menu opens the *View Compliance Record* modal 
# The modal displays, under *Record Identification*: Property, Compliance Category, Record Type, License / Record #, Issue Date, Expiration Date, Frequency, Total Cost, Add Additional Documents, *Archived By*, and *Archived Date* (the latter two populated only if this record has since been superseded by a renewal/replace).
# The modal displays the *Issuing Authority* section (Authority Name, Property Account #, Website URL, Username, Password) and *Primary Contact at Issuing Authority* section (First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone), consistent with the Record Review form.
# The *History > Notes* table displays all notes logged against this record (Username, Date, Notes), matching the data captured during initial review and any subsequent edits.
# A *Prior Records* table is displayed below History, with its own *Filters* and *Search* controls, and columns: *Record Type, Issuing Authority, Issue Date, License/Record #, Expiration Date, File name, Additional File, Total Cost, Archived By, Archived Date*.
# Each Prior Record row includes a kebab menu with a *View Details* action that opens the full archived snapshot of that specific version, showing all Record Identification, Issuing Authority, and Primary Contact fields as they existed at the time of archival, plus its own Archived By/Archived Date.
# If no prior versions exist, the Prior Records table shows an empty state: an icon, *"No Prior Records"*, and the caption *"There are no prior records to display"* 
# The modal provides *Cancel* and *Submit*/close actions; this view does not persist any data changes.

h2. C. Edit Record

# Selecting *Edit* from the row menu opens the *Edit Compliance Record* form , pre-populated with the record's current data.
# All fields are editable *except* the *Property* field and the primary uploaded file, consistent with the parent epic's edit rules.
# The form includes a manually editable *Status* field/dropdown, allowing the user to override the current status to *Active*, *Expiring*, *Expired*, *N/A*, or *N/A anymore* regardless of what the system-calculated status currently is, per the parent epic's status rules.
#* Setting Status to *N/A* or *N/A anymore* clears/disables the Expiration Date requirement, consistent with the rule that these two statuses never carry an Expiration Date.
# The user can upload *Add Additional Documents* and add *Notes* via *+ Add Note*, the same as during initial record review.
# The form provides *Cancel* and *Save* actions.
#* *Cancel* discards changes and returns to the Compliance & Records grid.
#* *Save* persists the changes and immediately updates the corresponding row in the Compliance & Records grid.
# Editing a record does *not* create a Prior Records entry  archiving only occurs through the Renew/Replace flow (see Section D). The Prior Records section on this form reflects the same read-only history described in Section E.

h2. D. Renew / Replace

*Acceptance Criteria:*

# Selecting *‘Replace or Renew Record’* from the row menu opens the *Renew Compliance Record* modal (with two mutually exclusive options:
#* *Renew current record* — _"Use this option when the current record has expired or is nearing expiry, to replace it with the renewed document."_
#* *Replace current record* — _"Use this to replace the current document with a different compliance document, unrelated to renewal."_
# The modal provides *Cancel* and *Continue* actions; Continue is enabled once an option is selected.
# Both options proceed to a *blank Record Review form* where the user must enter new Record Identification data (Compliance Category, Record Type, License/Record #, Issue Date, Expiration Date, Frequency, Total Cost), upload a new primary file, and optionally update Issuing Authority and Primary Contact details.
# Upon *Save*, the newly entered data and file become the record's active/current version, visible on the Compliance & Records grid.
# The *previous* version of the record (data + file(s) that were active immediately before the renewal/replacement) is automatically moved into *Prior Records*, with:
#* *Archived By* — the user who performed the Renew/Replace action, populated automatically.
#* *Archived Date* — the date the Renew/Replace action was completed, populated automatically.
# Neither Archived By nor Archived Date is manually editable.
# The newly active record's *Status* will be active by default  and user can change the status based on the file. 
# Reupload will not gothrough AI processing 

h2. E. Prior Records

# Prior Records are created *only* as a result of a Renew or Replace action (Section D) — never from a standard Edit (Section C).
# Each Prior Record entry is a full, read-only snapshot of that version's data at the time it was archived, including its own License/Record #, Issue Date, Expiration Date, Total Cost, File name, and Additional Files.
# The Prior Records table supports *Filters* and *Search* to locate a specific historical entry.
# Each Prior Record row provides a *View Details* action (via kebab menu) to open the full archived record form (Screen 4), showing all original Record Identification, Issuing Authority, and Primary Contact data as it existed at that time.
# Prior Records have *no Edit, Renew, or Delete/Inactive actions* — they are permanent, immutable historical entries.
# If a compliance record has never been renewed or replaced, its Prior Records table is empty, displaying: an icon, *"No Prior Records"*, and the caption *"There are no prior records to display"* (Screen 2).

h2. Out of Scope

* Bulk Renew/Replace across multiple records.
* Editing or restoring a Prior Record back to being the active record.

column1: Status : File Upload & Compliance Records
column31:
h2. Overview

This ticket documents the complete set of statuses, their trigger conditions, and the allowed transitions for both the *File Upload* flow and the *Compliance Record* flow, based on the confirmed status mapping.

h2. User Story

*As a* Connexus or Client user *I want to* see accurate, automatically-maintained statuses for uploaded files and compliance records, with clearly defined rules for when a status changes automatically versus manually *So that* I can trust the system to reflect the true state of every document without needing to track expiration dates myself

h2. A. File Upload Status Lifecycle

*Acceptance Criteria:*

# A file progresses through the following states, in order:
#* *Processing* — the file is undergoing OCR extraction and AI processing (system-only, transient state; not necessarily shown as a persistent grid status but represents the in-flight step between upload and the next status).
#* *Pending Review* — the file passed the eligibility check (≤80MB) and was successfully processed/extracted by AI. Tooltip: _"Read by AI and needs approval."_
#* *Pending Completion* — the file exceeded 80MB, or AI processing failed/flagged the file (unreadable, suspicious, low-confidence). Tooltip: _"Not read by AI & require Approval."_
#* *Approved* — every compliance record generated from that file's upload has been individually approved.
# A file cannot reach *Approved* status until *all* compliance records tied to it have been approved; until then, it remains in *Pending Review*.
# *Pending Completion* files never pass through AI-driven data extraction — all field entry for these is manual (per the separate Pending Completion ticket).
# These four visible statuses (Pending Review, Pending Completion, Approved, and the file's initial queued state) are system-generated only; no manual override is available at the file-upload level.

h2. B. Compliance Record — Status Definitions

*Acceptance Criteria:*

||Status||Trigger Source||Condition||
|*Active*|System default|Expiration Date is present and more than 30 days in the future|
|*Expiring*|System default|Expiration Date is present and is *≤ 30 days* from the current date|
|*Expired*|System default|Current date has passed the Expiration Date|
|*N/A*|Both system and user|Expiration Date is blank|
|*N/A anymore*|User only|Set manually by the user; carries no Expiration Date|

# *Active*, *Expiring*, and *Expired* are calculated automatically by the system based solely on the record's Expiration Date no manual selection is possible for these three while an Expiration Date is present.  [~accountid:63c8e40fd579d7c687552750] Users should be able to manually adjust the status which will then remove the expiration date (if adjusting to N/A, N/A Anymore).  If the user just adjusts the date, it should follow the logic above to whether it is active, expiring, or expired.
# *N/A* can occur two ways: automatically, when a record is approved with a blank Expiration Date (system default), or manually, when a user selects N/A regardless of the record's current status.
# *N/A anymore* can only be set manually by the user, from any current status.
# Neither *N/A* nor *N/A anymore* records carry an Expiration Date.

h2. C. Compliance Record — Status Transition Rules

h3. 1. Moving from a system-calculated status (Active / Expiring / Expired) to N/A or N/A anymore

* The user can manually change a record's status from *Active*, *Expiring*, or *Expired* to *N/A* or *N/A anymore* at any time.
* When this change is made, the system *automatically clears/removes the Expiration Date* on that record by default, since neither N/A nor N/A anymore statuses carry an Expiration Date.
* User will get a warning before saving the file that the expiration is removed.

h3. 2. Moving between N/A and N/A anymore

* The user can manually switch a record between *N/A* and *N/A anymore* in either direction.
* Both statuses require the Expiration Date to remain blank; no date entry is needed or allowed for this transition.

h3. 3. Moving from N/A back to a system-calculated status

* If the user change the status from N/A to system default, it will ask the user to add the expiration date. 
* The system then automatically recalculates and assigns the correct status — *Active*, *Expiring*, or *Expired* — based on that newly entered Expiration Date, exactly as it would for any other record.

h3. 4. Moving from N/A anymore back to a system-calculated status

* If the user adds/enters an Expiration Date on a record currently in *N/A anymore* status, the same forced recalculation applies.
* The system automatically assigns *Active*, *Expiring*, or *Expired* based on the newly entered Expiration Date.

h3. 5. Summary of allowed manual transitions

||From||To||Trigger||Result||
|Active / Expiring / Expired|N/A|User selects N/A|Expiration Date auto-cleared|
|Active / Expiring / Expired|N/A anymore|User selects N/A anymore|Expiration Date auto-cleared|
|N/A|N/A anymore|User selects N/A anymore|Expiration Date remains blank|
|N/A anymore|N/A|User selects N/A|Expiration Date remains blank|
|N/A|Active / Expiring / Expired|User enters an Expiration Date|System recalculates status from the new date|
|N/A anymore|Active / Expiring / Expired|User enters an Expiration Date|System recalculates status from the new date|

column1: Notifications Temporal Scaling
column31:
*User Story*
As a Connexus platform owner, I want the notification system to be scaled using Temporal orchestration, so that high-volume notification events, reminders, broadcasts, and multi-channel delivery are durable, observable, retryable, deduplicated, and not affected by {{Promise.all}} fail-fast or unbounded fanout issues.

*Background*
The current notification system uses SQS dispatcher/listener flows and notification handlers. Some paths still use unbounded {{Promise.all}}, which can cause one failed operation to impact the whole fanout and can overload DB, SES, FCM, or SQS during large reminder/broadcast runs. We need a Temporal-based orchestration model similar in spirit to the RFP approach: grouped work, isolated failures, controlled concurrency, and clear tracking.

*Scope*
Migrate notification dispatching from the current SQS-handler fanout model into a Temporal-orchestrated workflow model while keeping backward compatibility during rollout.

*Tasks*

* Add Temporal client, worker, task queue, config, and deployment setup for notification orchestration.
* Create a {{NotificationDispatchWorkflow}} that accepts {{eventType}}, {{payload}}, {{source}}, {{correlationId}}, {{dedupeKey}}, and {{requestedAt}}.
* Validate workflow inputs using existing notification Zod schemas.
* Replace direct notification handler fanout with Temporal workflow starts.
* Keep SQS as the initial ingress path, but acknowledge SQS only after the Temporal workflow is started.
* Create recipient planning activities to resolve recipients by notification domain: RFP, vendor, insurance, contract, and e-sign.
* Page large recipient sets and deduplicate by {{eventType + entityId + recipientId + date bucket}}.
* Create batch or child workflows for recipient-level processing.
* Replace unbounded {{Promise.all}} usage with Temporal child workflows, activity retry policies, and controlled concurrency.
* Create channel delivery activities for WEB, EMAIL, and PUSH.
* Track channel lifecycle accurately as {{PENDING -> QUEUED -> SENT/FAILED}}.
* Add idempotency/dedupe support to prevent duplicate reminders or repeated workflow retries from creating duplicate notifications.
* Add Temporal schedules for reminder flows such as RFP due date passed, vendor RFP reminders, contract expiry, insurance expiry, and signing reminders.
* Add workflow audit tracking with workflow ID, event type, entity ID, recipient counts, success count, failure count, skipped count, and retry count.
* Add logs and metrics for workflow start, batch processing, channel delivery, failures, retries, and completion.
* Add feature flag {{NOTIFICATIONS_TEMPORAL_ENABLED}} for safe rollout and fallback to the current SQS path.
* Run shadow/canary migration first for RFP/vendor reminder notifications before migrating all notification events.

*Guardrails*

* Define reminder date rules clearly: UTC vs tenant timezone, date bucket, and daylight-saving behavior.
* Add notification preference and channel eligibility checks before delivery.
* Add SES, FCM, DB, and SQS rate limits/backpressure settings.
* Separate retry behavior for transient failures versus permanent invalid payload, invalid token, missing recipient, or template errors.
* Add Temporal workflow versioning and deterministic workflow rules.
* Add Temporal search attributes for {{eventType}}, {{entityType}}, {{entityId}}, {{tenantId}}, {{correlationId}}, and {{status}}.
* Use {{Continue-As-New}} for very large reminder/broadcast runs.
* Add template rendering validation before sending email.
* Avoid logging sensitive metadata such as action tokens, signing links, raw email payloads, or full notification metadata.
* Handle existing SQS messages safely during migration.
* Add load tests for large RFP/vendor reminder and broadcast runs.
* Add replay tests for Temporal workflow determinism.
* Add rollback/runbook steps for disabling Temporal and returning to the current SQS flow.

*Pre-Fixes To Include*

* Fix e-sign notification schema/module drift before routing e-sign through orchestration.
* Fix email-only notifications appearing in the in-app unread count.
* Fix channel status accuracy so email/push are not marked {{SENT}} immediately after queueing.
* Fix SES poison-message handling so permanent bad messages do not retry forever.
* Deactivate invalid FCM tokens after permanent FCM failures.
* Fix unauthenticated FCM logout/device token deletion risk.
* Replace notification-handler unbounded {{Promise.all}} paths with controlled concurrency or Temporal child workflows.
* Add reminder-level dedupe keys before enabling scheduled workflows.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* High-volume notification reminders run through Temporal workflows.
* One failed recipient or channel does not fail the full notification batch.
* Duplicate workflow retries do not create duplicate notifications.
* Notification delivery status reflects actual channel outcome, not just queue submission.
* Large recipient sets are processed in controlled batches.
* Reminder workflows can be monitored, retried, cancelled, or inspected from Temporal.
* Existing notification producers continue working during migration.
* Temporal can be disabled through feature flag and the current SQS flow still works.
* RFP/vendor reminder counts match existing behavior before full rollout.
* Workflow audit records show total, sent, failed, skipped, and retried counts.
* Load testing proves the new orchestration can handle expected reminder/broadcast volume without overwhelming DB, SES, FCM, or SQS.

column1: RFP related additional scalings
column31:
*User Story*
As a Connexus platform owner, I want bid submission, copy-to-all, scope-of-work property mapping, and bid analysis bulk award/cancel flows to be scaled using durable orchestration, so that large portfolio RFPs with many properties, vendors, documents, and SOW mappings can be processed reliably without API timeouts, long DB transactions, unbounded {{Promise.all}} fanout, duplicate records, missed notifications, or inconsistent bid analysis state.

*Background*
The relevant scaling areas are:

* Vendor bid submission through bulk save/submit.
* Copying one bid response and documents to all properties.
* Mapping scope of work to many/all properties.
* Creating property-level SOW versions.
* Improve scope of work loading
* Copying SOW files to property-specific S3 paths.
* Large RFP create/update with many properties, SOWs, documents, and attachments.
* Bid analysis award-all-properties.
* Bid analysis cancel-award-all-properties.
* Post-submit and post-award notification/event dispatch.

The existing initial VPR creation writer is already relatively scalable because it chunks database work and uses idempotent inserts, so the main focus is on later bid-side user operations.

*Goal*
Move large bid-side operations out of the synchronous request path and into durable workflows with batching, idempotency, retries, progress tracking, and partial failure handling.

*In Scope*

* {{BidSubmissionWorkflow}}
* {{BidCopyToPropertiesWorkflow}}
* {{ScopeOfWorkPropertyMappingWorkflow}}
* {{BidAnalysisBulkAwardWorkflow}}
* {{BidAnalysisBulkCancelAwardWorkflow}}
* Operation status tracking
* Workflow audit records
* Idempotent retry behavior
* Post-workflow notification triggers

*Tasks*

* Add durable orchestration for bid-side bulk operations.
* Add feature flag to enable orchestration by operation type or size threshold.
* Return operation/job ID immediately for large operations.
* Add operation status API with progress counts.
* Add workflow audit table or equivalent tracking.
* Add logs and metrics by {{operationId}}, {{workflowId}}, {{rfpId}}, {{vendorId}}, {{scopeOfWorkId}}, and {{rfpPropertyId}}.
* Keep small operations synchronous where safe.
* Move large operations to async workflow execution.
* Replace unbounded {{Promise.all}} fanout with controlled concurrency.
* Keep DB transactions short and scoped to one batch.
* Move S3 file copy operations outside DB transactions.
* Separate retryable transient failures from permanent validation failures.
* Allow retry of failed properties/documents only.
* Dispatch notifications only after successful workflow commit points.

*Workflow IDs And Dedupe Keys*

* {{bid-submit:{rfpId}:{vendorId}}}
* {{bid-copy:{sourceVendorPropertyResponseId}:{operationId}}}
* {{sow-map:{scopeOfWorkId}:{propertyId}:{versionId}}}
* {{award:{rfpId}:{vendorId}:{rfpPropertyId}}}
* {{cancel-award:{rfpId}:{vendorId}:{rfpPropertyId}}}

*Bid Submission Requirements*

* Validate {{rfpId}} and {{vendorId}}.
* Validate all update IDs belong to the same RFP/vendor.
* Validate responses are still eligible for update or submit.
* Save bid field updates in controlled batches:
** {{totalCost}}
** {{upfrontCost}}
** {{vendorComments}}
** {{additionalComments}}
** {{paymentTerms}}
* Resolve all pending vendor property responses for the RFP/vendor.
* Submit pending responses in chunks.
* Write {{VendorPropertyResponseStatusHistory}} records idempotently.
* Prevent duplicate submission if the vendor clicks submit multiple times.
* Track per-property status:
** updated
** submitted
** skipped
** failed
* Emit {{RFP_BID_SUBMITTED}} and {{VENDOR_BID_RECEIVED}} only after successful submission.

*Copy-To-All Requirements*

* Validate source vendor property response.
* Validate source response belongs to the same RFP/vendor as targets.
* Resolve target responses in pages.
* Copy bid fields to targets in batches.
* Soft-delete or replace target documents in controlled batches.
* Copy source documents idempotently.
* Track copied, skipped, and failed target properties.
* Prevent one failed property/document from failing the full copy operation.

*Scope Of Work Requirements*

* Map SOWs to selected/all properties in batches.
* Create {{ScopeOfWorkProperty}} records idempotently.
* Create {{ScopeOfWorkPropertyVersion}} records idempotently.
* Copy SOW files to property-specific S3 paths through separate activities.
* Track each property mapping as:
** {{PENDING}}
** {{MAPPED}}
** {{FILE_COPIED}}
** {{FAILED}}
* Retry failed S3 copies without recreating DB rows.
* Support large RFP create/update flows where many SOWs and properties are attached.

*Bulk Award Requirements*

* Validate RFP and vendor.
* Validate candidate properties before processing.
* Validate selected vendor responses can move to {{AWARDED}}.
* Process award-all in property batches.
* For each property:
** set selected vendor response to {{AWARDED}},
** mark competing responses as {{LOST}},
** update RFP property status to {{AWARDED}},
** write vendor response status history,
** write RFP property status history.
* Dispatch award notifications only after successful batch commit.
* Track awarded, skipped, failed, and lost-response counts.

*Bulk Cancel Award Requirements*

* Validate RFP and vendor.
* Resolve all awarded vendor responses for the RFP/vendor.
* Determine previous statuses from status history before processing.
* Revert awarded vendor responses to previous status.
* Revert lost competing responses to previous status.
* Revert RFP property statuses to previous status.
* Write cancel-award history idempotently.
* Track canceled, skipped, failed, and reverted-lost-response counts.

*Guardrails*

* Define async threshold, for example more than 25 or 50 properties/documents.
* Do not hold DB transactions during S3 operations.
* Do not use unbounded {{Promise.all}} for property/document/vendor fanout.
* Use batch sizes for DB writes and file-copy activities.
* Prefer {{createMany}}, {{updateMany}}, raw SQL, or CTE-style batch writes where appropriate.
* Prevent duplicate documents on retry.
* Prevent duplicate SOW mappings and versions on retry.
* Prevent duplicate status history on retry.
* Prevent duplicate notifications on retry.
* Preserve existing small-operation behavior.
* Keep bid analysis counts consistent after submit, award, and cancel-award.
* Provide clear failure reason per failed property/document.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* Vendors can submit bids across many properties without API timeout.
* Copy-to-all works for large property counts without long DB locks.
* Scope of work can be mapped to many/all properties without request timeout.
* SOW file copies happen outside DB transactions.
* Bulk award-all works for large RFPs without one long transaction.
* Bulk cancel-award-all safely restores previous statuses.
* One failed property/document does not fail the full operation.
* Workflow progress is visible by operation/job ID.
* Retrying a workflow does not duplicate documents, SOW mappings, status history, submitted responses, awards, cancel-awards, or notifications.
* Notifications are emitted only after successful workflow stages.
* Existing small bid submissions, copy actions, SOW mappings, and awards continue working normally.

column31:
h2. *1. Copy Bid to All Properties / SOW-to-Property Mapping*

The maximum expected volume for this operation is approximately *5,000 properties*.

When the copy operation begins, the UI should display a progress bar showing the number of properties processed and remaining. The frontend should send the selected properties to the server in small batches through standard HTTP API requests.

If the operation is interrupted—for example, because the browser tab is closed, the network connection fails, or an API request encounters an error—the properties that were already processed must remain completed. When the user resumes the operation, the system should identify the remaining or failed properties and submit only those items as a new task.

The implementation must support:

* Partial-completion tracking
* Prevention of duplicate property mappings
* Small transactional batches through HTTP requests
* Retry of only failed or unprocessed properties
* Resumption without restarting the entire operation

h2. *2. Copy Scope of Work to All Properties*

This operation should follow the same batching, progress-tracking, retry, and recovery approach described above.

The additional requirement is *Scope of Work version management*.

When copying a Scope of Work:

* If the Scope of Work content has changed, the system must create a new version.
* If the content has not changed, the system must reuse the existing version and must not create a duplicate version.
* Properties must always be mapped to the correct Scope of Work version.
* The UI should display all properties currently mapped to the selected Scope of Work version.
* When the version has not changed, properties that are already mapped should be displayed with a tick icon.
* Once all selected properties have been successfully mapped, the UI should show the operation as completed using a verified icon.

The system must prevent duplicate mappings and ensure that retrying or resuming the operation does not map the same property more than once.

h2. *3. Bid Submission*

A bid submission may include up to approximately *5,000 properties*.

Before processing the submission, the system should evaluate:

* The total number of selected properties
* The expected database-query load
* The estimated processing complexity

For smaller submissions, the existing synchronous HTTP request flow can be used.

For larger submissions, the properties should be processed through a sequence of small HTTP batch requests. The UI should display submission progress while the batches are being processed.

If the browser tab is closed, the network connection is interrupted, or a batch fails, the successfully submitted properties must remain completed. When the user resumes the operation, the system should identify and resubmit only the failed or unprocessed properties.

The submission flow must support:

* Partial-submission tracking
* Idempotent processing
* Duplicate-submission prevention
* Retry of failed batches or individual properties
* Resumption from the last successfully completed point

h2. *4. Bulk Award and Cancellation*

Bulk award and cancellation operations may involve approximately *10,000 to 20,000 vendors*.

These operations should use a configurable threshold-based processing model:

* Below the configured threshold, the operation can use the standard synchronous HTTP request flow.
* Above the configured threshold, the operation must run as a background job.

While a background operation is running, the UI should display a *Processing* status.

Individual records must not be shown as *Awarded*, *Rejected*, or *Cancelled* until the corresponding operation has been successfully completed for that record.

After processing is complete, the UI should display the final status for each applicable record, such as:

* Awarded
* Rejected
* Cancelled
* Failed

The same batching, recovery, idempotency, and retry approach should be used for both bulk award and bulk cancellation.

If the background job is interrupted or partially fails, successfully processed records must retain their completed status. Only failed or unprocessed records should be retried.

Email notifications must be triggered only after the corresponding award, rejection, or cancellation operation has been successfully completed.

h2. User Story: Auto-Approval of Property Insurance Based on Property ID Match

*Title:* Auto-approve property insurance when property ID match is confirmed by DOM

*As a* system (Neo), *I want to* auto-approve property insurance requests when DOM confirms an exact property ID match against the database, *So that* valid, verified property insurance requests are processed without manual intervention, and unmatched requests are correctly routed for manual review.

h3. Description

When a property insurance request is submitted, Neo checks whether the property name has an exact match in the database. DOM is responsible for providing the corresponding *property ID* for that match.

* If DOM returns a *property ID*, Neo should *auto-approve* the insurance request.
* If DOM's response does *not* include a property ID, Neo should *not* auto-approve** the request — instead, it should be routed to *Pending Approval* for manual review.

h3. Acceptance Criteria

# *Given* a property insurance request with an exact property name match in the database, *When* DOM returns a valid property ID for that match, *Then* Neo automatically approves the insurance request without manual review.
# *Given* a property insurance request, *When* DOM's response does not include a property ID (no match or unmatched property), *Then* the request is moved to "Pending Approval" status for manual review.

h4. Description

Currently, the system maintains a *one-to-one relationship* between Agency Name and Agency Number:

* When an Agency Number is updated for a policy against a specific Agency Name, this mapping gets *stored in the database*.
* On subsequent policies, selecting the *same Agency Name auto-populates* the previously stored Agency Number.

*Per confirmation from Heather*, this auto-population/mapping behavior needs to be *removed*. Going forward:

* Agency Name and Agency Number should *not* be linked or dependent on each other.
* The same Agency Name should be allowed to have *different/duplicate Agency Numbers* across different policies, entered independently each time.

h4. Acceptance Criteria

# *Given* a policy with an Agency Name selected,
*When* the user enters/updates the Agency Number,
*Then* the system should *not* store this Agency Number as a default/mapped value against the Agency Name for future use.
# *Given* a new policy where the user selects an Agency Name that was previously used with a specific Agency Number,
*When* the Agency Name is selected,
*Then* the Agency Number field should *not auto-populate* based on prior entries.
# *Given* the same Agency Name used across multiple policies,
*When* different Agency Numbers are entered for each policy,
*Then* the system should allow and save these as *independent, duplicate entries* without validation errors or overwrites.
# *Given* existing historical data with Agency Name-Agency Number mappings,
*When* this change is deployed,
*Then* existing records should also be reflected with this change

*Complete RFP workflow, excluding RFP creation.* The testing scope includes:

* Adding additional vendors to an existing RFP
* Bulk acceptance of properties within the same RFP

* Awarding a single vendor from multiple participating vendors

* Validation of status transitions and workflow continuity across the above processes

column1: [TRELLO] Auto-Mapped Contracts Are Incorrectly Archived or Missing from Dashboard
column31:
*Summary* 

[https://trello.com/c/qXyG7puM|https://trello.com/c/qXyG7puM|smart-link] 

*End date requested by Nisha for these contracts:* 12/31/2026

Some contracts that are automatically processed and completed through the mapping workflow are not appearing correctly after processing. Instead of remaining visible on the Contract Management dashboard, some contracts are automatically moved to the *Archived* section, while others are missing from both the dashboard and the Archived list.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Upload contracts that are processed through automatic mapping.
# Allow the mapping process to complete successfully.
# Review the Existing dashboard and the Archived section.

*Actual Result:*

* Some automatically mapped contracts are moved directly to the *Archived* section.
* Some automatically mapped contracts are missing from the dashboard and cannot be found.

*Expected Result:*

* Successfully mapped contracts should remain visible on the Contract Management dashboard according to their status.
* Contracts should not be archived or disappear unless an explicit archive action or business rule requires it.

column1: [TRELLO] Enhancement: Submit All Bids with “Ready” Status Without Manual Selection
column31:
[https://trello.com/c/awzMLuZS|https://trello.com/c/awzMLuZS|smart-link] 

When users click the *Submit Bid* button, all bids/properties currently in *Ready* status should be submitted automatically. Users should not be required to manually select individual properties before submitting the bids.

*Current Behavior:*

* The *Submit Bid* button remains grayed out until the user manually selects at least one property with a *Ready* status.
* Users must select the Ready properties individually before they can submit the bids.

*Expected Behavior:*

* The *Submit Bid* button should be enabled when there is at least one bid/property with a *Ready* status.
* Clicking *Submit Bid* should automatically submit all bids/properties that are in *Ready* status.
* Manual selection should not be required for Ready bids.
* Properties that are not in *Ready* status should not be submitted.

*Summary* 

Potential vendors are not displayed after the vendor list is refreshed using the *Reset* button on an existing RFP, even after a vendor is removed from the *Do Not Use Vendors* list. The vendors are displayed correctly when a new RFP is created.

*Credentials :* 

[shini+regression@neoito.com|mailto:shini+regression@neoito.com]

Test@123

*Preconditions:*

* Client has 2 properties with the same City, State, and County.
* Two vendors have the same City, State, and County.
* Both vendors have at least one primary user.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Navigate back to the same RFP's *Send RFP to Vendors* page.
# Click *Reset* to refresh the vendor list.

*Expected Result:*

* *RFP List page – Vendor Count*

column1: Optimize RFP details, property nested vendors, and View by Vendor loading
column31:
h2. Problem

Large RFPs become slow or time out because unbounded data and vendor statistics are loaded during initial rendering.

h3. Verified staging measurements

RFP: {{9a1ceb3a-2b9c-48de-ba82-c6ac9ecc213d}}

* {{GET /rfp/:id}}: *25.3 seconds*
* {{GET /rfp/properties?limit=10}}: *0.9 seconds*
* {{GET /rfp-vendor-responses/property-stats}} for 10 properties: *timed out after 60 seconds*
* {{GET /rfp/vendors?limit=10}}: *10.8 seconds*
* Expanding one vendor:
** Correctly made one vendor-specific request
** Returned 25 properties in *1.8 seconds*
* Expanding a property made no nested-vendor request.

h2. Required behaviour

h3. View by Property

* Initial rendering must fetch only the paginated property list.
* Do not fetch vendor statistics or nested vendors for collapsed properties.
* Expanding a property must fetch data only for that property.
* Cache loaded results while the user remains on the page.
* A failed nested request must not block the property list.

h3. View by Vendor

* Initial rendering must fetch only the paginated vendor summary.
* Preserve the existing vendor-specific lazy loading on expansion.
* Do not preload properties for all vendors.

h3. RFP details

* The page must not download every RFP property through {{GET /rfp/:id}}.
* Existing consumers of the endpoint must remain compatible.

----

h2. Backend tasks

h3. 1. Add backward-compatible lightweight RFP details support

Files:

* {{apps/sow-rfq/src/services/rfp/rfp.controller.ts}}
* {{apps/sow-rfq/src/services/rfp/rfp.service.ts}}
* Relevant DTO and specification files

Add an optional {{includeProperties}} query parameter.

* Default it to {{true}} to preserve existing API behaviour.
* The RFP details UI must pass {{includeProperties=false}}.
* When false, do not select, sort, serialize, or return the full property collection.
* Continue returning {{_count.rfpProperties}}.

Do not calculate {{isSendRfpDisabled}} by loading every property. Use an existence/count query instead.

Cover these cases:

* No properties: {{isSendRfpDisabled = false}}
* All active properties are {{CLOSED}}, {{CLOSED_FOR_BIDS}}, or {{AWARDED}}: {{true}}
* At least one eligible property exists: {{false}}
* Soft-deleted properties do not affect the result

Also apply {{deletedAt: null}} to returned documents, scopes of work, and properties.

h3. 2. Optimize property statistics

File:

* {{apps/sow-rfq/src/services/rfp-vendor-responses/rfp-vendor-responses.service.ts}}

Ensure the statistics query:

* Accepts one property ID.
* Filters both tables by the supplied RFP.
* Excludes soft-deleted rows before aggregation.
* Returns zero counts when no responses exist.

Add {{vpr."rfpId" = $1}} to the join/filter so the database can use the RFP index.

h3. 3. Analyze and optimize the initial vendor query

File:

* {{apps/sow-rfq/src/services/rfp/rfp.service.ts}}
* Method: {{getVendors()}}

Capture {{EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)}} for:

* Vendor data query
* Pagination count query
* Awarded/submitted aggregation query

First apply the new indexes. If the request remains above the performance target, replace the correlated relation filter with a {{VendorPropertyResponses}}-first query:

# Select distinct active vendor IDs for the RFP.
# Join those IDs to {{Vendors}}.
# Apply vendor search, status, sorting and pagination.
# Count distinct vendor IDs for pagination.
# Keep nested property responses out of this query.

h3. 4. Add Prisma indexes

Update {{prisma/schema.prisma}}:

{noformat}model VendorPropertyResponses {
  // Existing fields

  @@index(
    [rfpId, vendorId, deletedAt, status],
    map: "vpr_rfp_vendor_deleted_status_idx"
  )
  @@index(
    [rfpPropertyId, deletedAt],
    map: "vpr_property_deleted_idx"
  )
}

model Vendors {
  // Existing fields

  @@index([name], map: "vendors_name_idx")
}

model RfpProperties {
  // Existing fields

  @@index(
    [rfpId, deletedAt, status],
    map: "rfp_properties_rfp_deleted_status_idx"
  )
}

model RfpDocuments {
  // Existing fields

  @@index(
    [rfpId, deletedAt],
    map: "rfp_documents_rfp_deleted_idx"
  )
}

model RfpScopeOfWork {
  // Existing fields

  @@index(
    [rfpId, deletedAt],
    map: "rfp_scope_of_work_rfp_deleted_idx"
  )
}

model RfpSendLog {
  // Existing fields

  @@index([rfpId], map: "rfp_send_log_rfp_idx")
}

model RfpStatusHistory {
  // Existing fields

  @@index(
    [rfpId, createdAt(sort: Desc)],
    map: "rfp_status_history_rfp_created_idx"
  )
}{noformat}

Generate and inspect the migration:

{code:bash}yarn prisma migrate dev --name optimize_rfp_details_queries
yarn prisma generate{code}

Confirm the migration does not recreate or remove unrelated indexes.

----

h2. Frontend tasks

h3. View by Property

# Remove the initial statistics request containing all visible property IDs.
# Move statistics and nested vendor queries into the expansion handler.
# On expansion, request only the selected property:
#* {{rfpId}}
#* {{propertyIds[]=expandedPropertyId}}
# Fetch the nested vendor list using the existing paginated vendor-response endpoint with the selected property ID.
# Use cache keys containing:
#* RFP ID
#* Property ID
#* Filters
#* Search
#* Page and limit
# Do not refetch when a loaded row is collapsed and reopened.
# Prevent duplicate requests from rapid clicks.
# Show loading and error states only inside the expanded row.
# Provide a local retry action for failed nested requests.

h3. View by Vendor

# Keep {{/rfp/vendors}} as the paginated initial request.
# Preserve the existing {{view-by-vendor}} request on expansion.
# Confirm only the expanded vendor ID is requested.
# Cache results per RFP, vendor, page, search and filters.
# Do not load nested properties for collapsed vendors.

h3. RFP details

Call:

{noformat}GET /rfp/:id?includeProperties=false{noformat}

Continue using {{/rfp/properties}} as the only source for the paginated property list.

----

h2. Regression tests

h3. Backend

Add tests covering:

* Existing callers still receive properties when {{includeProperties}} is omitted.
* {{includeProperties=false}} does not load full properties.
* {{isSendRfpDisabled}} remains correct for every status combination.
* Soft-deleted properties, documents and scopes are excluded.
* Statistics work with one property ID.
* Statistics ignore another RFP’s responses.
* Statistics ignore soft-deleted responses.
* Vendor pagination, search, status and counts remain unchanged.
* Expanding one vendor returns only that vendor’s paginated properties.

h3. Frontend

Add tests proving:

* Initial property render makes no statistics or nested-vendor request.
* Expanding one property makes one request for that property.
* Expanding a second property requests only the second property.
* Reopening a loaded property uses cached data.
* Nested request failure does not hide or block the property list.
* Initial vendor view makes no nested-property request.
* Expanding one vendor requests only that vendor.
* Property and vendor pagination still work.

----

h2. Acceptance criteria

* Initial View by Property makes no {{property-stats}} or nested-vendor request.
* {{GET /rfp/:id?includeProperties=false}} does not return all properties.
* Initial vendor view does not return nested property lists.
* Expansion produces exactly one entity-specific request.
* Existing API behaviour remains unchanged when {{includeProperties}} is omitted.
* No request times out for the representative 1,000-property RFP.
* RFP details, property statistics and initial vendor list each complete within five seconds on staging.
* Before/after {{EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)}} plans are attached to the PR.

h2. Rollout order

# Deploy Prisma indexes.
# Deploy backward-compatible backend changes.
# Deploy frontend lazy loading.
# Verify the representative large RFP.
# Monitor endpoint duration, timeout and database load metrics.

column1: Award,cancel single property and bulk property changes
column31:
award,cancel,award-all-properties,cancel-all-properties Changes

*Title:* Restrict Blocking to Property Level During Single/Bulk Awarding Process

*As a* user managing property awarding on the RFP detail page, *I want* the system to block only the specific property being awarded (not the entire RFP) and provide clear status/loading feedback, *So that* I can continue awarding other properties without unnecessary blockage, while system integrity (statuses, bulk actions, and property list) is maintained during the awarding process.

# *Property-Level Blocking Only*

* When a user initiates single property awarding, only that specific property should be blocked/locked.
* The RFP level should remain unblocked, allowing other actions to continue.

# *Loading Indicator Scope*

* A loading icon should display only on the property being awarded.
* Users must be able to award other properties simultaneously without any blockage or wait.

# *Status Integrity — No Intermediate States*

* Property-level and RFP-level statuses must not change to any intermediate/transient state during the awarding process.
* The current property status and RFP status should be retained as-is throughout the process.
* A new internal status field should be introduced to track "cancel pending" or "awarding in process" states.
* This new status field must be used for backend/system tracking only and should *not* be reflected/visible in the UI.

# *Bulk Awarding Restriction During Single Awarding*

* Bulk awarding action from the RFP detail page should be disabled/blocked while a single property within that RFP is in the process of being awarded.

# *Property List Protection During Bulk Awarding*

* During bulk awarding, the system must restrict users from deleting any property from the property list.
* Attempting to delete a property during this process should be prevented with appropriate system restriction (e.g., disabled action or validation message).

# *Performance — Awarding Time SLA*

* The property awarding process should complete within 1–2 minutes.
* Any delays beyond this threshold should be flagged for investigation/monitoring.

# *Manual Refresh Option*

* The UI should provide a refresh option/button.
* This allows users to manually fetch and view the latest status of the property without needing to reload the entire page.

column1: Add delete option for eligible records on Compliance Record File Upload page
column31:
User story
As an authorized user, I want to delete a compliance record from the File Upload page when its status is Processing, Pending Review, or Pending Completion, so that incomplete or unwanted uploads can be removed before completion.

Acceptance criteria

# A Delete option is displayed for records with the following statuses only:
#* Processing
#* Pending Review
#* Pending Completion
# The Delete option is not available for records in any other status.
# Selecting Delete displays a confirmation prompt that identifies the record.
# Confirming deletion removes the record and its associated file according to existing deletion, retention, and audit rules. The deletion remains effective after page refresh.
# Cancelling the confirmation leaves the record unchanged.
# Eligibility is validated server-side at deletion time so a record cannot be deleted if its status has changed.
# Unauthorized users cannot delete records, including through direct API requests.
# If deletion fails, the record remains intact and the user sees a clear error message.
# A successful deletion is recorded in audit history where auditing is supported.

Test coverage

* Verify visibility and successful deletion for each eligible status.
* Verify deletion is unavailable for non-eligible statuses.
* Verify confirm and cancel paths.
* Verify authorized and unauthorized users.
* Verify a status change between page load and deletion.
* Verify API failures do not leave partial or inconsistent data.

h3. Additional cases

# *Deleted approved record indicator:* If an approved compliance record is deleted, keep its source entry visible in *File Upload → Pending Review* or *Pending Completion*, as applicable. Display an information icon with the message: *“This approved compliance record has been deleted.”*
# *Approved status presentation:* In the Pending Review and Pending Completion lists, display *Approved* as a non-interactive status using the same visual treatment as the File Upload list page, rather than as a button.

h3. Additional acceptance criteria

# When an approved compliance record is deleted, its corresponding source entry remains visible in the applicable Pending Review or Pending Completion list.
# The source entry displays an information icon indicating that the approved record was deleted.
# The information message is accessible by mouse and keyboard and states: “This approved compliance record has been deleted.”
# The indicator is shown only when the associated approved compliance record has been deleted.
# Approved entries in both Pending Review and Pending Completion display a status-only UI consistent with the File Upload list page.
# The Approved status is non-interactive and cannot be used as an action button.
# Existing filters, pagination, record details, and other actions in both lists continue to work.

h3. Additional test coverage

* Delete an approved record originating from Pending Review and verify the source entry and information icon.
* Delete an approved record originating from Pending Completion and verify the source entry and information icon.
* Verify the information message by hover, click, and keyboard focus where supported.
* Verify the Approved status appearance matches the File Upload list page and is not clickable.
* Verify unaffected records retain their existing behavior.

column1: Compliance & Records: Restore scroll position after returning from record edit
column31:
h2. Issue description

When a user expands a property in the *Compliance & Records* list, opens and edits a nested compliance record, and then returns to the list, the property remains expanded but the page returns to a different or default scroll position. The user must manually scroll down to locate the expanded property again.

The list should restore the user to the same expanded property and scroll position.

h2. Environment

* *Application:* Connexus web application
* *Environment:* Staging
* *Module:* Compliance & Records

h2. Steps to reproduce

# Open *Compliance & Records*.
# Scroll down to a property that is not initially visible.
# Expand the property.
# Open a nested compliance record for editing.
# Edit and save the compliance record.
# Return to the Compliance & Records list.
# Observe the list position.

h2. Actual result

The property remains expanded, but the list does not return to its previous position. The user must scroll down to locate the property and edited record.

h2. Expected result

The previously expanded property remains expanded and is automatically brought back into view at the same, or nearest practical, scroll position.

h2. Acceptance criteria

# Returning after a successful edit restores the previously expanded property.
# The viewport returns to the previous position with the expanded property and edited record visible.
# Existing search, filter, sort, pagination, and expansion state remains unchanged.
# Scroll restoration works for records near the top, middle, and bottom of the list.
# No unexpected jump occurs after the list finishes loading.
# Returning without saving also restores the prior list position.
# Browser Back and the in-page Back action behave consistently.
# If edited data changes the record order or removes it from the current filtered results, the system falls back gracefully to the property header or nearest valid position.
# Slow or delayed list loading does not prevent the final scroll restoration.
# The behavior works when multiple properties are expanded.

column1: Client Contacts: “View Properties” pagination does not reset when switching contacts
column31:
h2. Issue description

On *Clients → Contact List*, the selected page in the *View Property List* modal is retained between contacts. If a user opens a contact with multiple pages of properties, navigates to page 2, closes the modal, and then opens another contact whose properties fit on one page, the second contact is queried using page 2.

This can incorrectly display *No results* even though the selected contact has properties. The screenshot shows a {{user-properties}} request sent with {{page=2}} while the modal displays no results.

h2. Preconditions

* Contact A has enough properties for at least two pages.
* Contact B has properties that fit on one page.

h2. Steps to reproduce

# Navigate to *Clients → Contact List*.
# Click *View Properties* for Contact A.
# Navigate to page 2 of the property list.
# Close the modal.
# Click *View Properties* for Contact B, whose properties fit on one page.
# Observe the modal and the property-list network request.

h2. Actual result

Pagination state from Contact A is retained. Contact B's request is sent with {{page=2}}, causing the modal to show *No results* or an invalid/stale page state.

h2. Expected result

Every time *View Properties* is opened for a contact, pagination resets to page 1 before data is fetched. The selected contact's available properties and correct pagination details are displayed.

h2. Acceptance criteria

# Opening *View Properties* for a different contact resets the selected page to page 1.
# The first property request for the newly selected contact uses {{page=1}}.
# Displayed rows and pagination metadata belong only to the currently selected contact.
# *No results* is displayed only when the selected contact genuinely has no properties.
# Repeatedly switching between contacts with different property counts does not retain an invalid page number.
# Existing property search, filters, page-size selection, and pagination continue to work correctly.
# Switching from the last page of a multi-page contact to a one-page contact displays the one-page contact's records correctly.
# Switching to a contact with no properties displays the correct empty state on page 1.
# Rapidly closing one modal and opening another does not allow an earlier API response to overwrite the newly selected contact's data.
# If property deletion reduces the total page count, reopening the modal starts on a valid page.

The attached screenshot provides UI and network-request evidence.
